# phpwcms 2.x Documentation — full content

<!-- docs/index.md -->

# phpwcms 2.x documentation

> Source: `README.md`, `https://github.com/slackero/phpwcms`

phpwcms is a free, open source web based content management system (CMS) and CMS framework, written in PHP 8.4+ and backed by MySQL or MariaDB. It has been continuously developed since 2002 and is maintained by [Oliver Georgi](https://github.com/slackero).

phpwcms is built for speed and for the separation of layout and content: you define the layout once in templates, editors fill structure levels and articles with content parts, and the system serves pages on demand — no page cache rebuilding ceremonies, no build step. It stays developer friendly: plain file templates, replacement tags, and frontend render scripts you can script against without touching the core.

## Documentation map

| Section | Contents |
| ------- | -------- |
| [General](general/concepts.md) | Core concepts: structure levels, articles, content parts, templates, URLs |
| [Requirements](requirements/index.md) | Server, PHP, database and extension requirements |
| [Installation & updates](installation/fresh-install.md) | Fresh installation, setup wizard, Docker, upgrading from 1.x |
| [Administration](administration/admin-panel.md) | Admin panel, users and usergroups, file storage, SEO and cache settings |
| [Backend](backend/01-overview.md) | Working inside the backend: structure, articles, files, messaging, profile |
| [Frontend](frontend/page-rendering.md) | How pages render, replacement tags, frontend scripts, RSS |
| [Templates](templates/template-system.md) | Layout tags, template editor, default templates, asset libraries |
| [Content parts](content-parts/index.md) | Every content part type with full option reference |
| [Modules](modules/index.md) | Shop, calendar, glossary, newsletter, ads, feedimport, addresses, seolog, statistics |

## Where to start

- Setting up a new site: [Installation](installation/fresh-install.md) then [Backend overview](backend/01-overview.md).
- Porting an existing 1.x install: [Updating](installation/updating.md).
- Theme and layout work: [Templates](templates/template-system.md).
- AI agent consumption: [llms.txt](llms.txt) (curated index) and [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt) (all pages concatenated), regenerated by `docs/_authoring/gen-llms.php`.
- Extending content behavior: [Frontend scripts](frontend/frontend-scripts.md).

<!-- docs/general/concepts.md -->

# Core concepts

> Source: `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php`, `index.php`

phpwcms organizes websites into a small set of orthogonal entities. Understanding these four — structure levels, articles, content parts, templates — is enough to work both as an editor and as a template developer.

## The content hierarchy

A site is one tree of **structure levels**. Each level holds any number of **articles**, and each article is a stack of **content parts** that make up its individual page.

```text
Structure level (site section)
├── Article (page)
│   ├── Content part 1
│   ├── Content part 2
│   └── …
├── Article (page)
└── sub-Structure level
    └── …
```

- <a id="structure-level"></a>**Structure level** — navigation-ready category node. Carries its own page template, level keywords, and URL alias. One level can be marked as visible in the menu or hidden but reachable.
- <a id="article"></a>**Article** — a page of the site (or a list entry when the level is configured to list its article summaries). Holds metadata (title, keywords, description, dates, visibility, remote URL) plus its content parts stack.
- <a id="content-part"></a>**Content part** — one functional block: text with image, image gallery, teaser list, form, search, map, and so on. This is where content editing happens; the [content parts reference](../content-parts/index.md) documents every type.
- <a id="article-summary"></a>**Article summary** — every article has an always-present summary block used in listings, teasers and RSS output.

The tree, articles and content parts live in the database (`phpwcms_categories`, `phpwcms_article`, `phpwcms_articlecontent`); uploaded binaries and converted images live on disk under `/filearchive` and `/content`.

## Templates

Layout never lives in the database content. A **layout template** (managed in the backend "Templates" section, stored in `phpwcms_template`) defines the HTML skeleton of a page and marks slots with `{` `}` layout tags:

```html
<header>{HEADER}</header>
<nav>{NAV_LIST_UL:F,0,3,,act_path}</nav>
<main>{CONTENT}</main>
<footer>{FOOTER}</footer>
```

The frontend engine fills `{CONTENT}` with the rendered article stack, `{HEADER}`/`{FOOTER}` etc. with your admin-defined header/footer code, and replacement tags like `{NAV_LIST_UL:…}` with generated blocks. The full tag set is documented under [Template layout tags](../templates/layout-tags.md).

Many content parts select an additional, article-specific **content part template** out of `template/inc_cntpart/<type>/*.tmpl`; each content part type ships [default templates](../templates/default-templates.md) that fall back automatically when nothing is selected. Layout and content stay separable: change the template, keep the content parts.

## Rendering model

A frontend request flows through `index.php` → `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php`:

1. Resolve the requested URL to a structure level and article (`aid`/`<article-alias>`/level alias).
2. Gather all content parts of the article in sort order. Each part is rendered by its renderer in `include/inc_front/content/cnt<N>.article.inc.php`, optionally through a selected `.tmpl` template.
3. Replace layout tags and replacement tags over the assembled page.
4. Run registered [frontend render scripts](../frontend/frontend-scripts.md) — your hook layer for custom filtering and output.
5. Emit the page; frontend caching applies per configuration.

Result pages are assembled per request; caching and gzip are backend-configurable. See [Page rendering](../frontend/page-rendering.md) for the tag pipeline in order.

## URLs and aliases

Default URLs are search engine friendly and alias based: `/index.php?<level-alias>` and `/index.php?<level-alias>,aid_<alias>` are canonical; with configured rewriting (`mode_rewrite` in `config.inc.php`) they become pure path URLs. Article aliases, level aliases and 301 forcing are all admin-configurable — details in [URL handling](url-handling.md).

## Users, groups and permissions

Backend access works through **users** and **usergroups**. A usergroup controls which backend sections and modules are visible, plus per-structure-level and per-file-category write rights; users inherit from their group, with per-user overrides. Frontend "visibility" of whole levels or single articles is independent from backend rights, letting the same CMS run a public site and a members-only area. See [Users and usergroups](../administration/users-usergroups.md).

## Modules

Modules are optional functional units (shop, calendar, glossary, newsletter, ads, …) shipped in `include/inc_module/`. Activated per installation in the admin panel and per usergroup, they add backend sections, their own tables and — where applicable — content part types that bridge module data into articles. See the [modules reference](../modules/index.md).

## Where the data lives

| Entity | Database table(s) |
| ------ | ----------------- |
| Structure levels | `phpwcms_categories` |
| Articles | `phpwcms_article` |
| Content parts | `phpwcms_articlecontent` |
| Templates / layout | `phpwcms_template`, `phpwcms_pagelayout` |
| Files | `phpwcms_file`, `phpwcms_filecat` |
| Backend users / groups | `phpwcms_user`, `phpwcms_usergroup` |
| Module data | one set per module (e.g. `phpwcms_shop`, `phpwcms_calendar`, `phpwcms_glossary`) |

Table prefixes (`db_prepend`, brand prefix) are set in the admin panel during setup; [Installation](../installation/setup-wizard.md) explains.

<!-- docs/general/url-handling.md -->

# URL handling

> Source: `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php` (resolution), `include/inc_lib/default.inc.php` (`rel_url()`, `abs_url()`, `returnGlobalGET_QueryString()`), `include/inc_front/front.func.inc.php` (`url_search()`), `include/config/dist.conf.inc.php`

## URL forms

phpwcms URLs name the page with the alias of the structure level or the article:

| Form | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| `index.php?<level-alias>` | Structure level page, e.g. `index.php?about-us` |
| `index.php?<article-alias>` | Article page by its own alias |
| `index.php?id=<level>[,<aid>…]` | Level and optionally article by numeric IDs (legacy combined form) |
| `index.php?aid=<article-id>` | Article by ID; `aid=<id>-<n>` addresses content part pagination page `<n>` |

Alias resolution runs one UNION query: a matching `articlecat.acat_alias` wins over `article.article_alias`. When the alias equals the index page alias, the site root renders. With rewriting configured the first (empty-valued) GET parameter becomes the path — `/about-us.html` — while remaining parameters stay as query string.

`PHPWCMS_ALIAS` defines the canonical name of the current request: the alias when one exists, otherwise `id=<level>` or `aid=<article-id>`.

## Rewrite configuration

| Key | Default | Description |
| --- | ------- | ----------- |
| `rewrite_url` | 1 | Enables path based URLs (`PHPWCMS_REWRITE`); when 0, `rel_url()`/`abs_url()` keep `index.php?` |
| `rewrite_ext` | `.html` | Suffix of rewritten URLs; `/` renders directory style (`/alias/`) |
| `alias_allow_slash` | 1 | Allows `/` inside aliases for path-like aliases |
| `alias_allow_utf8` | 1 | Keeps UTF-8 characters in aliases (requires `charset = utf-8`) |
| `allow_empty_alias` | false | When true, empty alias fields no longer auto-generate an alias |
| `reserved_alias` | empty array | Alias names blocked from use |

Outgoing markup rewrites by itself: `url_search()` in `front.func.inc.php` converts `href="index.php?…"` and `onclick="location.href='index.php?…'"` attributes into `<value><rewrite_ext>` paths (an old style `id=<cat>,<aid>` becomes `<cat>.<aid>`), and the image handler URL `img/cmsimage.php` shortens to `im`. The webserver side needs matching rewrite rules delivering `/alias.html` back to `index.php?<alias>`.

## rel_url and abs_url

`rel_url($add, $remove, $id_alias, $format, $glue, $bind)` and `abs_url()` build URLs from the current GET state in `$GLOBALS['_getVar']`:

- First pair values with `$add`, drop `$remove` (plus `$phpwcms['global_unregister_getVar']`), optionally substitute the first pair by `$id_alias` (e.g. `'aid=42'` or an alias).
- With rewriting on the first pair becomes `<value><rewrite_ext>` and the rest a normal query string; without, everything lands after `index.php?`.
- `$format` controls escaping: `htmlspecialchars` (default), `htmlentities`, `urlencode`, `rawurlencode`, or default (no escaping).
- `rel_url()` returns the URL relative to the site root and falls back to `PHPWCMS_URL`; `abs_url()` always prefixes the full site URL.

`{SITE}` (see [layout tags](../templates/layout-tags.md#site-paths)) provides the same absolute prefix inside markup.

## 301 forcing

| Key | Default | Behavior |
| --- | ------- | -------- |
| `force301_id2alias` | false | When a request uses numeric `id=`/`aid=` but an alias exists, send 301 to the alias URL; content part pagination (`aid-N`) stays numeric |
| `force301_2struct` | false | When a level shows exactly one article, 301 to the level alias |

Level redirects (`acat_redirect`) always 301 before anything renders. Both force keys switch off for POST requests and preview mode, and a level can exempt itself from the structure redirect with `acat_disable301`.

## Canonical handling

`$phpwcms['canonical_off']` disables the canonical link completely. Otherwise `content.article.inc.php` writes `<link rel="canonical">` into the head:

- A page requesting an alias resolves canonically; the single-article-of-a-level case canonically points to the level alias.
- When `force301_2struct` redirects anyway, the canonical step skips; content part pagination pages canonicalize to `aid=<id>-<page>`.
- Overrides: the article field *canonical URL* (`article_canonical`) or the level equivalent (`acat_canonical`) replaces the automatic value. A leading `{SITE}` expands to the site URL, a leading `/` mounts beneath it.

When more GET parameters than the page identity ride along (`count($_getVar) > 1`), automatic canonicalization drops — search or filter traffic keeps its identity rather than folding into the base page.

## 404 handling and the redirects admin

A request hitting nothing (level, article, alias) enters `$content['404error']`:

1. With alias `r404` or `REDIRECT_STATUS == 404`, the original `REDIRECT_URL` retries as alias once.
2. Failing that, the recorded combination (level id, article id, alias) looks up the `redirect` table — the same store the backend **Admin → Redirects** page manages (`p=14`, `include/inc_tmpl/admin.redirect.tmpl.php`). An active matching entry redirects with its configured code (301, 302, 307, 401, 404, 503; default 302) and increments its `views` counter. Entry types: `home` (level tree entry of the root), `alias`, `id`, `aid`, `link`.
3. No match: `$phpwcms['log_404error']` auto-inserts the failed combination so it appears in the admin list for later setup.
4. Nothing redirectable: HTTP 404 status with the current template's error block (`[404]` / `[404_ELSE]` sections, see [layout tags](../templates/layout-tags.md#list-mode-pagination-and-error-sections)).

The redirects admin lists entries with filters (active/inactive, search terms, page size), lets you define redirects manually and toggles existing entries active or inactive; `update_404redirect()` flushes the cached set.

## Related

- [Core concepts](concepts.md#urls-and-aliases)
- [Page rendering](../frontend/page-rendering.md) — resolution and 404 flow in execution order

# System requirements

> Source: `README.md` (Server & System Requirements), `composer.json`, `setup/setup.php`

## Server

| Requirement | Minimum | Recommended |
| ----------- | ------- | ----------- |
| PHP | 8.4 | 8.4 / 8.5 (tested on 8.4, 8.5) |
| MySQL / MariaDB | 5.5 | MariaDB 10.4+ / MySQL 8.0+, InnoDB, utf8mb4 |
| Web server | Apache with `mod_rewrite`, Nginx or IIS | Apache / Nginx |

Server config templates ship in the repo root: `_.htaccess` (Apache), `nginx.conf`, `web.config` (IIS).

## PHP extensions

Required for all features:

- `intl` — collation, internationalization
- `gd` — image scaling, cropping, thumbnails
- `iconv`, `mbstring` — multi-byte encoding handling
- `mysqli` — database driver
- `fileinfo` — MIME validation on upload
- `xmlreader`, `libxml`, `dom`, `simplexml` — feeds, sitemaps, XML processing
- `openssl` — secure SMTP, crypto, API transport
- `curl`, `bcmath` — external HTTP APIs, payment calculations

Image tooling beyond GD: ImageMagick and GhostScript extend supported input formats (EPS/AI/PS/PDF conversion, sharpening, colorspace control) when configured; see [Image processing](../administration/image-processing.md).

## Composer dependencies

Releases ship `include/vendor/` prebuilt. Installing from Git requires `composer install` (PHP 8.4). Key libraries: PHPMailer 7+, TinyMCE 8, htmlpurifier, phpspreadsheet, simplepie, league/commonmark, oauth2 providers (Google, Azure).

## Client

Backend UI is Bootstrap 5 based and targets current evergreen browsers; no legacy IE support. Frontend output is what your templates build — phpwcms imposes no browser baseline beyond your own CSS.

## Docker

A complete local stack (PHP 8.4, MariaDB 10.11, phpMyAdmin, Mailpit, image tools) ships as `docker-compose.yml` / `Dockerfile` — see [Docker installation](../installation/docker.md).

## Related

- [Fresh installation](../installation/fresh-install.md)
- [Setup wizard](../installation/setup-wizard.md)

<!-- docs/installation/fresh-install.md -->

# Fresh installation

> Source: `README.md` (Installation), `setup/index.php`, `setup/inc/step6.inc.php`, `setup/inc/setup.func.inc.php`

Confirm the [system requirements](../requirements/index.md) first — PHP 8.4+, a MySQL 5.5+/MariaDB database, and at least one graphics library. For a prebuilt local stack, see [Docker installation](docker.md).

## Install steps

1. **Download and extract** a phpwcms release archive (releases ship `include/vendor/` prebuilt, so no Composer step is needed) into the web server document root. Installing from Git instead requires `composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader` under PHP 8.4.
2. **Configure the web server**: use the shipped templates — rename `_.htaccess` to `.htaccess` for Apache (the setup wizard offers to do this), adapt `nginx.conf` or `web.config`. Rewritten URLs need `mod_rewrite`/matching server rules; see [SEO settings](../administration/seo-settings.md).
3. **Set write permissions** for the web server user on:
   - `content/` and its subfolders (`content/images/`, `content/tmp/`, `content/cache/`, `content/form/`, `content/rss/`, `content/pages/`)
   - `filearchive/` and `upload/`
   - `include/config/`
   - `template/` (and `template/template_lang/`)
   - `setup/setup.conf.inc.php` (the wizard's working config, chmod 666 if needed)
4. **Run the setup wizard**: open `https://your-domain.com/setup/` in the browser — see [Setup wizard](setup-wizard.md) for the seven steps including database creation, admin account and SMTP settings.
5. **Finalize and harden** as below.

Ownership should stay with the user the web server runs as (or a shared group) so the wizard can write `include/config/conf.inc.php`, `.htaccess` and the content directories.

## Post-install hardening

The wizard's final step displays the required warning itself: **delete or secure the `setup` directory before using phpwcms in production.**

- Remove the whole `/setup/` directory, or block access to it at the web server level. Re-adding it later only for upgrades is the documented workflow — `setup/upgrade.php` is downloaded separately per [Updating](updating.md).
- If automated writing of `include/config/conf.inc.php` failed during setup, the wizard links `setup/get_conf_file.php`, which downloads `conf.inc.php` as an attachment; place it into `include/config/conf.inc.php`. Downloading the file once appends `$NO_ACCESS = true;` to `setup/setup.conf.inc.php`, which blocks further wizard access until the line is removed.
- Verify `include/config/conf.inc.php` is not served as plain text — the `_.htaccess` and shipped server configs block `include/` and dot-prefixed files.
- Check `content/cache/`, `content/backup/` (created later by the updater with a deny-all `.htaccess`) and `filearchive/` listing behavior; deny direct directory listing for storage folders.
- Log into `login.php` with the admin account created in the wizard and change defaults as needed: [Users and usergroups](../administration/users-usergroups.md), [Cache and performance](../administration/cache-performance.md).
- Keep `template/` and `content/` under your own backup routine; the built-in [update engine](updating.md#in-app-system-update) backs up only on updates.

## Verify the install

- Frontend loads a default page on `https://your-domain.com/`; backend at `https://your-domain.com/login.php`.
- Admin → phpinfo shows the expected PHP version and extensions ([Admin panel](../administration/admin-panel.md)).
- Uploading an image to the file center generates a thumbnail — confirms the [image engine](../administration/image-processing.md) works.

## Related

- [Setup wizard](setup-wizard.md)
- [Docker installation](docker.md)
- [Configuration file](config-file.md)

<!-- docs/installation/setup-wizard.md -->

# Setup wizard

> Source: `setup/index.php`, `setup/setup.php`, `setup/inc/setup.func.inc.php`, `setup/inc/setup.check.inc.php`, `setup/inc/step0.inc.php`–`step6.inc.php`, `setup/get_conf_file.php`

The wizard installs phpwcms through a browser. Start it at `https://your-domain.com/setup/`. It refuses to run when `include/config/conf.inc.php` already exists — an existing installation blocks setup (the start page explains removal to re-run), and `setup/setup.php` redirects to the start page in that case.

## Steps

| Page | Title | Content |
| ---- | ----- | ------- |
| `setup/index.php` | Licence | GNU GPL-2.0 text in a scrollable box; the *I Agree* checkbox unlocks only after scrolling to the end. |
| `setup.php?step=0` | System requirements & environment check | Web server, PHP version (8.4+ required), MySQLi extension and client driver, sodium availability. Detects image tools (Imagick, ImageMagick CLI, GraphicsMagick CLI, GD, Ghostscript, NetPBM) with supported formats, plus recommended extensions (curl, mbstring, intl, openssl, zip, fileinfo) and PHP directives (memory limit, post/upload sizes). Blocks on an unwritable `setup/setup.conf.inc.php` (offers `chmod 666`); warns when recommendations are unmet. |
| `step=1` | Edition & whitelabel license | Standard GPL edition (leave the key empty) or Whitelabel edition: paste a signed license key, validated live via libsodium with licensee, domain and expiry shown. |
| `step=2` | Database server connection | Host, port (auto-detected), user, password, database name (created automatically when missing, utf8mb4), table prefix, persistent connection; with a whitelabel key a *Brand Table Prefix* field appears. After connecting: MySQL version, default/allowed language selection with browser-language detection, collation choice (utf8mb4 variants), *Create initial phpwcms database tables* checkbox, then the superuser form (name, username, password + repeat, email) writing the `usr_admin` account. |
| `step=3` | Site URL & email transport | Detected site basis URL, timezone select, sender email/name, mail transport (`mail()`, SMTP, unix sendmail), host/port, encryption (none/STARTTLS/SMTPS), SMTP authentication and credentials; whitelabel licenses additionally expose brand name, website URL and copyright. |
| `step=4` | Internal paths & storage | Document root, subdirectory (`root`), filestorage, template and FTP upload directory names, optional CDN image URL. Values must not start or end with a slash. |
| `step=5` | Content & media defaults | Max upload size (bytes), content column width, thumbnail and preview sizes, session timeout, graphics engine select (priority Imagick > ImageMagick > GraphicsMagick > GD2 > NetPBM with installed/badges), CLI library path, JPEG/WebP quality, sharpen level. |
| `step=6` | Finalization & permissions check | Writability check (auto-`chmod 0777` on failure) for the directories listed below, writes the configuration and `.htaccess`, displays the remove-`setup`-warning and a link to the login page. |

## What the wizard writes

| Target | Content |
| ------ | ------- |
| `setup/setup.conf.inc.php` | The wizard's working state — initialized by copying `include/config/dist.conf.inc.php`, then rewritten from the `write_conf_file()` template with every form value after each step. Keys not on any form keep the shipped defaults. |
| `include/config/conf.inc.php` | Copy of the state file; written in step 6 with write → copy → rename fallbacks. Only written when absent. Falls back to the `setup/get_conf_file.php` manual download when all writes fail. |
| `.htaccess` (document root) | Created from `_.htaccess` when missing; inside a subdirectory the wizard rewrites `RewriteBase /` to the subfolder path. Existing `.htaccess` files are left untouched. |
| `setup/.htaccess` | Written with `Deny from all` as a baseline block of the setup directory. |
| Database tables | From `setup/default_sql/phpwcms_init.sql` and `phpwcms_inserts.sql`, executed with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` / `INSERT IGNORE` guards on submit; existing tables with a different prefix are reported so you can change the prefix. |
| Admin account | Inserted into or updated in `phpwcms_user` with `usr_admin = 1`, hashed password, backend language, TinyMCE default. The *Edit Account* link reopens the form. |

The generated configuration enables the backend module and newsletter menus by default (`enable_backend_module`, `enable_backend_newsletter` = `true`) and generates a random `form_salt`. Modules install separately on first use in the backend, not from the wizard.

## Re-run behavior

- With `conf.inc.php` present, the start page blocks and setup redirects — delete `include/config/conf.inc.php` to start over (this does not drop database tables; the existing-prefix detection then reports and reuses them).
- The state lives in `setup/setup.conf.inc.php`, not in the session: you can leave mid-way and resume, and the file carries previous settings forward.
- After the configuration download through `setup/get_conf_file.php` the appended `$NO_ACCESS = true;` locks the wizard; remove the line to re-enable.

## Related

- [Fresh installation](fresh-install.md) — permissions and hardening around the wizard
- [Configuration file](config-file.md) — every key the generated file contains
- [Whitelabel branding](../administration/whitelabel.md) — license mechanics

<!-- docs/installation/docker.md -->

# Docker installation

> Source: `docker-compose.yml`, `Dockerfile`

The repository ships a complete local development stack: PHP 8.4 with Apache, MariaDB, phpMyAdmin and Mailpit, including the full graphics toolchain. It is a development environment — do not expose it to production as-is.

## Starting

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

Then open the setup wizard at `http://localhost:8080/setup/` to install (see [Setup wizard](setup-wizard.md)). If `include/config/conf.inc.php` exists from a previous run, setup blocks and the site serves directly at `http://localhost:8080`.

## Services

| Service | Image | Ports (host:container) | Purpose |
| ------- | ----- | ---------------------- | ------- |
| `web` | built from local `Dockerfile` (`php:8.4-apache`) | `8080:80` | phpwcms itself; repository bind-mounted at `/var/www/html`. |
| `db` | `mariadb:10.11` | `3307:3306` | Database with `--character-set-server=utf8mb4 --collation-server=utf8mb4_unicode_ci`; data in the named volume `db_data`. |
| `mailpit` | `axllent/mailpit:latest` | `8026:8025` (web), `1026:1025` (SMTP) | Captures all outgoing mail; limited to `MP_MAX_MESSAGES = 500`. |
| `phpmyadmin` | `phpmyadmin:latest` | `8081:80` | `PMA_HOST=db`, `PMA_PORT=3306`. |

## Environment values

| Variable | Value |
| -------- | ----- |
| `MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD` | `rootpassword` |
| `MYSQL_DATABASE` | `phpwcms` |
| `MYSQL_USER` | `phpwcms` |
| `MYSQL_PASSWORD` | `phpwcmspassword` |

Enter these in the setup wizard's database step: host `db`, port `3306`, database `phpwcms`, user `phpwcms`, password `phpwcmspassword`. Only the database data volume persists; the web directory is your working copy.

## PHP image details

The Dockerfile builds the web container with:

- PHP extensions: `gd` (freetype/jpeg/webp), `mysqli`, `pdo_mysql`, `intl`, `zip`, `mbstring`, `opcache`, plus `imagick` from PECL.
- Image tools: ImageMagick, GraphicsMagick, NetPBM, Ghostscript — with the ImageMagick `policy.xml` entries for PDF, EPS, PS and XPS granted `read|write` rights so document preview rendering works; see [Image processing](../administration/image-processing.md).
- PHP settings via a custom INI: `memory_limit = 256M`, `upload_max_filesize = 64M`, `post_max_size = 64M`, `max_execution_time = 300`, UTC timezone, and `display_errors` on for development.
- Apache modules `rewrite` and `headers` enabled, `AllowOverride All` for `.htaccess` support.
- Mail transport wired through msmtp: `sendmail_path = "/usr/bin/msmtp -t --host=mailpit --port=1025"`, so every `mail()` call from the CMS (SMTP_MAILER `mail`) lands in Mailpit.

## Mail testing with Mailpit

Mailpit exposes a web UI at `http://localhost:8026` where every caught message is readable, searchable and holdable, and an SMTP endpoint at `mailpit:1025` (host port 1026) that can also be used as an explicit SMTP target in the wizard or SMTP config. Delete all messages in the UI when a test run produced junk. Because the sendmail path already routes to Mailpit, newsletter and form-mail tests work without configuring real SMTP.

## Related

- [Fresh installation](fresh-install.md) — manual alternative to the wizard steps
- [System requirements](../requirements/index.md) — host-based requirement check

<!-- docs/installation/updating.md -->

# Updating

> Source: `include/inc_lib/update/update.php`, `update.api.php`, `update.backup.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/admin.update.tmpl.php`, `setup/upgrade.php`, `include/inc_lib/revision/` (`r401.php`–`r561.php`, `revision.php`), `README.md` (Upgrading), `CHANGELOG.md`

Always back up the database and files before updating, and confirm the host runs PHP 8.4+. Three paths cover every situation; all of them run the same database revision chain afterward.

**Back up before every update — no exceptions.** A full backup means both:

1. **Database dump** — complete, not the pre-update engine dump alone (`mysqldump --single-transaction <db> | gzip > backup.sql.gz` or phpMyAdmin "quick export" as gzip).
2. **Files** — at minimum `include/config/conf.inc.php`, `template/`, `filearchive/`, `content/images/`, `content/tmp/` (session/scratch), plus the current directory listing (`ls -laR > filelist.txt`) to prove what you had.

Store the backup off the web server — the built-in dumps land under `content/backup/` on the same hosting and die with it if the update or the server fails. Downloads, uploads, or `rsync` to a second host all count; a snapshot on the same disk is last resort only. Never start an update with unverified backups.

## In-app system update

**Admin → System Update** (`phpwcms.php?do=admin&p=18`) — for self-hosted installs above version 2.0.0; see [Admin panel](../administration/admin-panel.md#system-update) for the panel itself and its backup layout. The engine:

1. Fetches the latest release from the GitHub API (`slackero/phpwcms`), requires the PHP `zip` extension and writable `content/backup/`.
2. Dumps the database (pure PHP gzip dump) **before** downloading anything — dump failure aborts the run.
3. Downloads the release zip from GitHub hosts only, verifies the `.update-manifest` sha256 list per file, and stages the release extract.
4. Checks out a plan of added/modified/deleted files against the previous manifest; skips `include/config/`, `filearchive/`, `content/`, `upload/`, `setup/`, `.htaccess`, `robots.txt`. Your configuration, storage and templates survive every update.
5. Applies the plan under a maintenance flag (auto-expiring after 15 minutes, clearable in the panel) and writes the new `.update-manifest`.
6. Runs pending database revisions inline, records the run (status, file count, backup path, error) in `phpwcms_update_log`.

The built-in dump is a convenience for rollback, not your backup: it lives under `content/backup/` on the same server. Export the database separately and pull `content/backup/` off the host before you update.

Updates are blocked when a newer release would install on a half-migrated schema — run pending revisions first (a backend login triggers `phpwcms_revision_check()`). Rollback restores the pre-update file mirror per run. Older installs (2.0.0 or less) must use the standalone script or manual path.

## Standalone upgrade script

`setup/upgrade.php` is a self-contained CLI and browser updater that runs independently of the main application (own DB connection, pure-PHP dump, ZipArchive). Download it into an existing installation:

```bash
mkdir -p setup && curl -fsSL -o setup/upgrade.php \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/slackero/phpwcms/v2-dev/setup/upgrade.php
```

Run it either way:

```bash
php setup/upgrade.php                 # interactive CLI (prompts admin login)
# or open https://your-domain.com/setup/upgrade.php in the browser
```

Behavior:

- **Same backup rule as above, before you download anything: full database dump plus the protected files (`conf.inc.php`, `template/`, `filearchive/`, `content/images/`), stored off the server.** The script's own dump/zip under `content/backup/` covers rollback on the same host only.

- Requires PHP 8.4+ and an installed revision of `r401` or newer (the revision tracking was introduced in r401); upgrades from phpwcms 1.x without a manifest need the `--allow-unverified` flag.
- Authentication uses your admin backend credentials, including Two-Factor (TOTP or backup codes) when enabled; database migrations are gated behind that login.
- Detects the actual database table prefix (including whitelabel/`cmsgo` brand prefixes) and repairs missing whitelabel config lines in `conf.inc.php` when needed (`conf.inc.cmsgo-backup.php` keeps the original).
- Dumps the database and builds a files zip below `content/backup/<timestamp>/` (excluding `content/images/`, `content/tmp/`, `content/cache/`, `content/rss/`, `content/backup/` itself and `.git*` from the archive), then applies the release zip with the same preserved-paths rules as the in-app engine.
- Runs `phpwcms_revision_check()` up to the staged release revision, bringing the schema to r561 at the time of writing.
- CLI options: `--reinstall` or `--force` (overwrite the currently installed version again), `--allow-unverified` (upgrade legacy packages without a manifest).

## Manual upgrade

1. Back up the database **and** the protected files (`conf.inc.php`, `template/`, `filearchive/`, `content/images/`, `content/tmp/`) and store both copies off the web server — nothing in this path does it for you.
2. Extract the new release over the document root, **never overwriting** `include/config/conf.inc.php` and never deleting content in `filearchive/`, `content/images/` or `template/`.
3. Run the database migration: log into the backend once (runs pending revisions) or run `php setup/upgrade.php`; the revision chain detects outdated revisions automatically.
4. Empty `content/tmp/` and `content/cache/` so new templates and assets take effect, and flush the image cache when image handling changed ([Admin panel](../administration/admin-panel.md)).

## Database revision mechanism

`include/inc_lib/revision/revision.php` defines `PHPWCMS_REVISION`; the chain `r401.php` … `r561.php` contains the schema and data migrations since the revision tracking was introduced (r401). `phpwcms_revision_check()` compares the installed revision and runs each missing revision script in order, recording failures. The in-app updater refuses new runs until a failed migration is resolved; backend login or `setup/upgrade.php` retries the chain.

Database revisions are one-way transformations. If a revision fails half-applied, restore the database **and** files from your pre-update backup (see the backup rule at the top), then retry with the cause fixed.

## phpwcms 1.x → 2.x migration

This is the riskiest update path — legacy schema, version jumps, PHP changes. Treat the backup rule as mandatory: full database dump + all protected files, off the server, before you touch anything.

- **PHP baseline moved to 8.4.** 1.x installs run on PHP 7.4/8.0/8.1-compatible code; 2.x requires PHP 8.4 or newer — upgrade PHP first.
- **GD 1.x support removed**; pick a modern engine from the setup ([Image processing](../administration/image-processing.md)).
- The revision system starts at r401: upgrading from a 1.x state without revisions uses `setup/upgrade.php` (possibly with `--allow-unverified`) or the manual path; the in-app engine remains locked at versions 2.0.0 and below.
- Table prefixes: legacy `cmsgo`-style installs are detected and migrated automatically by the standalone script.
- Breaking changes and new features per release are listed in `CHANGELOG.md`; check it before updating production installs.

### Recommended workflow: upgrade locally, swap folders live

The production database and the old files folder are never touched during the upgrade itself. The migrated database lands under a **new table prefix** next to the old one, so the live switch is a folder swap with a rollback path that costs one folder restore.

1. **Back up the production database** — full dump (rule at the top of this page), plus the protected files list. From here on the production box stays untouched until the final switch.
2. **Install the production database locally for updating**: import the production dump into a local database. Everything from now on happens locally; only this DB copy is modified.
3. **Rename the copied tables to a new table prefix** so the migrated set can live beside the original when it comes back to the server. Generate the rename statements for every `phpwcms_*` table instead of hand-listing them:

   ```sql
   -- <NEW>_ = new prefix, e.g. cms2026_ — tables become <NEW>_phpwcms_…
   SELECT CONCAT('RENAME TABLE `', table_name, '` TO `<NEW>_', table_name, '`;')
   FROM information_schema.tables
   WHERE table_schema = DATABASE() AND table_name LIKE 'phpwcms\_%';
   ```

   Run the query, check the generated `RENAME TABLE` list twice against `SHOW TABLES;`, then execute it on the **local** copy. A spreadsheet-based variant of this recipe builds the same statements from a `SHOW TABLES;` paste; a static list can miss module tables, so prefer the generated form.
4. **Update with the new prefix**: set the new prefix (`db_prepend`) in the local `conf.inc.php` (or during local setup) and run the local 2.x application — `setup/upgrade.php` auto-detects the prefix and runs the revision chain on the renamed, data-carrying tables. Test content, modules, forms and image handling locally.
5. **Bring it live**: import the migrated database to the remote host. The remote database then holds both sets side by side — original `phpwcms_*` (old, untouched) and `<NEW>_phpwcms_*` (migrated). The remote deployment itself is mostly a **folder swap**: replace the application folder with the new 2.x build whose `conf.inc.php` points at the new prefix. Old code folder kept aside = instant rollback (point it back, and the old install still runs against its own tables).

   **Subdomain variant** — for zero-downtime switchovers, point a subdomain (e.g. `v2.example.com`) at the folder holding the new 2.x build before touching the main domain:
   - Give the subdomain its own web server section (`VirtualHost` for Apache, server block + `try_files` per the shipped `nginx.conf` for Nginx). The shipped root rewrite files (`.htaccess` / `nginx.conf`) work as-is under a subdomain document root.
   - Import the migrated database and set the new prefix in the subdomain build's `conf.inc.php`.
   - Test on the subdomain against real URLs. Because level aliases and article aliases are stored data, output matches production as soon as both builds read the same migrated set — check forms, images and shop flows, which depend on config and the migrated schema rather than aliases.
   - Switch: change the main domain's document root (or move the new build's folder) to the 2.x installation. Rollback = point the document root back to the old build; the old install still runs against its untouched `phpwcms_*` tables.

**Rollback semantics:** database revisions are one-way — the migrated set cannot be un-migrated. Rollback therefore means the folder swap back (the old `phpwcms_*` tables on the server were never modified), not reverting the migrated set. If the migrated set itself is the problem, restore it from the step-1 backup.

## Related

- [Admin panel](../administration/admin-panel.md) — panel details, maintenance flag, rollback
- [Fresh installation](fresh-install.md) — prerequisites

# Configuration file

> Source: `include/config/dist.conf.inc.php` (all defaults), `include/inc_lib/default.inc.php`, cross-linked feature pages

`include/config/conf.inc.php` is the single runtime configuration of a phpwcms install, created by the [setup wizard](setup-wizard.md) and never touched by updates. All entries live in the `$phpwcms` array as `$phpwcms['key'] = value;` statements. Defaults below quote the shipped `include/config/dist.conf.inc.php` — never copy values from another installation's file. Edit by hand, then clear affected [caches](../administration/cache-performance.md) where noted.

The setup-generated file adds one legacy key that `dist.conf.inc.php` no longer ships: `GETparameterName` (`'id'`) — it is read nowhere in 2.x code.

## Database

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `db_host` | string | `'localhost'` | Database server host or socket path. |
| `db_port` | int | `3306` | Database server port. |
| `db_user` | string | `''` | Database user name. |
| `db_pass` | string | `''` | Database password; also seeds `USER_KEY` and the `form_salt` fallback. |
| `db_table` | string | `''` | Database name. |
| `db_prepend` | string | `''` | Optional namespace in front of the table prefix; final prefix is `[<db_prepend>_]<brand_table_prefix>_` (see [Whitelabel branding](../administration/whitelabel.md)). |
| `db_pers` | bool | `0` | Use a persistent (non-closing) mysqli connection. |
| `db_charset` | string | `'utf8mb4'` | Default charset for new tables and connections. |
| `db_collation` | string | `'utf8mb4_unicode_ci'` | Default collation for new tables. |
| `db_version` | string | `''` | Recorded MySQL server version from install time; filled automatically. |
| `db_timezone` | string | `''` | MySQL session time zone name or offset; empty keeps the server default. |
| `db_sql_mode` | string | `'NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION'` | MySQL `sql_mode` set per session. |
| `db_errorlog` | bool | `false` | Log database queries and errors; see [Cache and performance](../administration/cache-performance.md). |

## Site URL and SSL

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `site` | string | `''` | Base URL of the site; empty auto-detects. Example value: `'http://'.$_SERVER['SERVER_NAME'].'/'`. |
| `site_ssl_mode` | bool | `0` | Turns SSL support of the CMS on (`1`) or off (`0`). |
| `site_ssl_url` | string | `''` | URL of the SSL certificate host, e.g. `'https://'.$_SERVER['SERVER_NAME'].'/'`. |
| `site_ssl_port` | int | `443` | Port the SSL service listens on. |

## Administrator account

Defaults written into a fresh install by the setup wizard; the wizard stores a `password_hash()` of the chosen password.

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `admin_name` | string | `'Webmaster'` | Display name of the install's administrator. |
| `admin_user` | string | `'admin'` | Login name of the super admin account. |
| `admin_pass` | string | `''` | Password hash; must be set — the setup wizard requires a password on install. |
| `admin_email` | string | `'noreply@example.com'` | Administrator email used for system communication. |

## Paths and directories

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `DOC_ROOT` | string | `$_SERVER['DOCUMENT_ROOT']` | Absolute document root; override for CLI or nonstandard layouts. |
| `root` | string | `''` | Subdirectory below the document root when phpwcms does not run at domain root; no leading/trailing slash. |
| `file_path` | string | `'filearchive'` | Filestorage directory name; see [File storage](../administration/file-storage.md). |
| `templates` | string | `'template'` | Template directory. |
| `content_path` | string | `'content'` | Frontend runtime directory for cache, images, tmp, rss, pages. |
| `cimage_path` | string | `'images'` | Image directory name below `content_path`. |
| `cdn_image_url` | string | `''` | Base URL of a CDN proxying `/content/images/` (e.g. `https://cdn.example.com`); the CDN must forward to the origin folder. |
| `ftp_path` | string | `'upload'` | FTP takeover directory; see [File storage](../administration/file-storage.md). |
| `ads_path` | string | `'marketing'` | Ads module storage name below `content_path` (the former `ads`). |

## Content and media limits

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `file_maxsize` | int | `52428800` | Per-file upload cap in bytes (50 MB); see [File storage](../administration/file-storage.md). |
| `content_width` | int | `978` | Max article content column width, important for multi-column image rendering. |
| `img_list_width` / `img_list_height` | int | `160` / `100` | List thumbnail size; see [Image processing](../administration/image-processing.md). |
| `img_prev_width` / `img_prev_height` | int | `978` / `734` | Large preview size and fallback for one-sided target dimensions. |
| `max_time` | int | `1800` | Backend logout after this many seconds of inactivity. |
| `responsive` | bool | `1` | `1` keeps image sizes as given, `0` caps width at `content_width`. |
| `preserve_image_name` | bool | `1` | Keep the original file name for resized image versions. |
| `cnt_sort` | string | `'a-z'` | Content sorting of listings: empty/`false` behaves like before, `'a-z'` or `'z-a'`. |

## URL rewriting and aliases

See [SEO settings](../administration/seo-settings.md) for rendering details.

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `rewrite_url` | bool | `1` | Rewritten URLs via the web server rules. |
| `rewrite_ext` | string | `'.html'` | Suffix of rewritten URLs (`/alias.html`, `/alias/`). |
| `alias_allow_slash` | bool | `1` | Allow `/` in aliases. |
| `alias_allow_utf8` | bool | `1` | Keep UTF-8 special characters in aliases (charset utf-8). |
| `allow_empty_alias` | bool | `false` | `true` disables alias auto-creation when the field is empty. |
| `reserved_alias` | array | `[]` | Alias names that must stay free. |
| `force301_id2alias` | bool | `false` | 301 redirect from ID URL to alias URL. |
| `force301_2struct` | bool | `false` | 301 redirect to the structure level for single-article levels. |
| `GET_pageinfo` | bool | `0` | Append breadcrumb path as `pageinfo` GET parameter to links. |
| `remove_empty_get_vars` | bool | `true` | Drop valueless GET parameters except the alias. |
| `unregister_getVar` | array | `[]` | Custom GET var names kept out of `rel_url()`/`abs_url()` globals. |
| `preserve_getVar` | array | `[]` | GET vars phpwcms normally strips but you want preserved. |
| `log_404error` | bool | `false` | Log every 404 for the redirect editor. |
| `disable_next_prev` | bool | `false` | Drop `<link rel="prev"/"next">` from pagination. |

## Language and charset

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `default_lang` | string | `'de'` | Default language code. |
| `DOCTYPE_LANG` | string | `''` | Language written into the doctype/`<html lang>`; defaults to `default_lang`. |
| `allowed_lang` | array | `array('en', 'de', 'fr', 'es')` | Languages the frontend may switch between. |
| `frontend_lang_key` | string | `'phpwcms_frontend_lang'` | Session/cookie key for frontend language choice. |
| `lang_parse` | bool | `true` | Parse frontend language block tags `[LANG:xx]…[/LANG]` / `[xx]…[/xx]`. |
| `use_content_lang` | bool | `false` | Use the article/structure-level language when resolving content. |
| `be_lang_parse` | mixed | `false` | Backend language block parsing: `false`, `'BBCode'` or `'BraceCode'`. |
| `charset` | string | `'utf-8'` | Page charset; keep utf-8. |
| `php_charset` | bool | `false` | `true` sets PHP's default charset to `charset`. |
| `i18n_parse` | bool | `1` | Parse browser-language `@@Text@@` translation markers. |
| `i18n_complex` | bool | `0` | `0` matches the easy two-char language form, `1` the `en-gb` form. |
| `php_timezone` | string | `''` | Override the PHP date default time zone. |

## Rendering and output

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `mode_XHTML` | int | `3` | Doctype: `1` XHTML 1.0 Transitional, `0` HTML 4.01 Transitional, `2` XHTML 1.0 Strict, `3` HTML5. |
| `header_XML` | bool | `0` | `1` sends `application/xhtml+xml` instead of `text/html`. |
| `IE7-js` | bool | `0` | Legacy IE7-js loader; obsolete, keep `0`. |
| `render_device` | bool | `0` | Enable user-agent specific template blocks `<!--if:mobile-->`, `<!--!if:mobile-->`, `<!--!if:default-->`. |
| `detect_pixelratio` | bool | `0` | Inject JavaScript that detects Retina devices. |
| `render_clean_html` | bool | `0` | Strip HTML comments from output; experimental. |
| `parse_html_mode` | string | `'before'` | When replacement tags parse against raw HTML: `before`, `after`, `before+after`. |
| `js_in_body` | bool | `0` | `1` moves `<script>` output before `</body>` instead of `<head>`. |
| `viewport` | string | `'width=device-width, initial-scale=1'` | Content of the viewport meta tag. |
| `X-UA-Compatible` | string | `''` | Legacy `X-UA-Compatible` meta/edge mode; keep empty. |
| `base_href` | mixed | `true` | Emit `<base href>`: `true` auto-detects, a string sets it, `false` disables. |
| `header_comment` | string | `''` | Custom comment emitted at the top of the HTML source. |
| `cp_default` | int | `0` | Default content part ID preselected where used; see structure level editor. |
| `frontend_edit` | bool | `0` | `1` adds direct-into-backend links to frontend content. |
| `allow_ext_init` | bool | `1` | Allow including custom scripts at frontend initialization. |
| `allow_ext_render` | bool | `1` | Allow including custom scripts at frontend rendering. |
| `allow_cntPHP_rt` | bool | `0` | Allow PHP replacement tags/includes inside content parts. |
| `allow_remote_URL` | bool | `0` | `1` permits remote URLs in `{PHP:...}` tags. |
| `enable_inline_php` | bool | `false` | Enables `[PHP]` blocks and `{PHP…}` tags in content. |
| `enable_deprecated` | bool | `false` | Re-enable functionality phpwcms marked deprecated. |
| `recipient_count` | int | `0` | Legacy, read nowhere in 2.x. |
| `set_article_active` | bool | `1` | Articles are active (`1`) or disabled (`0`) by default when created. |
| `set_category_active` | bool | `1` | Structure levels default to active on create. |
| `set_file_active` | bool | `1` | Files and folders default to active on create. |
| `set_news_active` | bool | `1` | News entries default to active on create. |
| `enable_backend_newsletter` | bool | `true` | Shows the newsletter menu in the backend; access is then governed by usergroups. |
| `enable_backend_module` | bool | `true` | Shows the module menu in the backend; access is then governed by usergroups. |

## Cache and debugging

| `version_check` | bool | `1` | Check the online phpwcms release for update notices. |

## Sessions and security

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `Login_IPcheck` | bool | `0` | Bind backend sessions to the login IP. |
| `trusted_proxies` | array | `[]` | CIDR ranges of reverse proxies/CDNs whose forwarded headers may be believed, e.g. `array('173.245.48.0/20', '2400:cb00::/32')`. |
| `trusted_proxy_priority_header` | string | `''` | Preferred client-IP header behind a trusted proxy, e.g. `'CF-Connecting-IP'`. |
| `SESSION_FEinit` | bool | `0` | Start PHP sessions for the frontend (`1`) or not (`0`, default). |
| `BOTS` | array | googlebot, msnbot, bingbot, ... | User agents that never start sessions. |
| `session.cookie_httponly.off` | bool | `false` | `true` makes the session cookie JavaScript-accessible. |
| `session.cookie_samesite` | string | `'Lax'` | Cookie SameSite: `None`, `Lax` or `Strict`. |
| `login_autocomplete` | bool | `true` | Allows the browser to store/autofill backend credentials. |
| `enable_GDPR` | bool | `true` | Anonymize IPs and other GDPR handling inside phpwcms logging. |
| `usergroup_support` | bool | `false` | Experimental group feature switch. |

## Files, forms and messaging

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `allowed_upload_ext` | string | long comma list | Upload extension whitelist; see [File storage](../administration/file-storage.md). |
| `multimedia_ext` | string | `'aif,aiff,mov,...'` | Extensions treated as multimedia in the file center. |
| `trash_delete_files` | bool | `false` | Delete stored files physically when trash is emptied. |
| `sanitize_dlname` | bool | `0` | Sanitize special characters in download filenames. |
| `inline_download` | bool | `1` | Open downloads inline where possible. |
| `form_tracking` | bool | `1` | Store each form submission in the database. |
| `form_salt` | string | `''` | Secret salt for form tracking; falls back to `db_pass` when empty, generated by setup. |
| `formmailer_set` | array | `array('allow_send_copy' => 0, 'global_recipient_email' => 'mail@example.com')` | Formmailer switches: copy-to-sender permission and fallback recipient. |
| `enable_messages` | bool | `0` | Internal messaging system; no longer recommended to use. |
| `feuser_regkey` | string | `'FEUSER'` | Key namespace for frontend user registration data. |
| `login.php` | string | `'login.php'` | Name of the backend login file, resolvable in URL helpers. |

## Social and SEO

See [SEO settings](../administration/seo-settings.md).

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `set_sociallink` | array | `array('article' => false, 'articlecat' => false, 'news' => false, 'shop' => false, 'render' => true)` | Defaults of the social/OpenGraph switch per type and `render` as global switch. |
| `twitter_site` | string | `''` | `@handle` for the `twitter:site` meta tag. |
| `canonical_off` | bool | `false` | `true` disables canonical link output. |
| `enable_seolog` | bool | `1` | Log search engine referrer data for the SEO log module. |

## Email (PHPMailer)

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `SMTP_FROM_EMAIL` | string | `'info@localhost'` | Default from/reply address. |
| `SMTP_FROM_NAME` | string | `'My Name'` | Default from/reply name. |
| `SMTP_HOST` | string | `'localhost'` | SMTP server host or IP. |
| `SMTP_PORT` | int | `25` | SMTP server port. |
| `SMTP_MAILER` | string | `'mail'` | Transport: `mail`, `smtp`, `sendmail` or `qmail`. |
| `SMTP_USER` | string | `'user'` | SMTP login name. |
| `SMTP_PASS` | string | `'pass'` | SMTP password. |
| `SMTP_SECURE` | string | `''` | `''`, `'ssl'` or `'tls'`. |
| `SMTP_AUTH` | bool | `0` | Enable SMTP authentication. |
| `SMTP_AUTH_TYPE` | string | `''` | `CRAM-MD5`, `LOGIN`, `PLAIN` or `XOAUTH2`. |
| `SMTP_XOAUTH_PROVIDER` | string | `''` | OAuth2 provider: `'Google'`, `'Microsoft'` or `'Azure'`. |
| `SMTP_CLIENT_ID` | string | `''` | OAuth2 client ID. |
| `SMTP_CLIENT_SECRET` | string | `''` | OAuth2 client secret. |
| `SMTP_TENANT_ID` | string | `''` | Microsoft OAuth2 tenant ID. |
| `SMTP_REFRESH_TOKEN` | string | `''` | OAuth2 refresh token; obtain via `bin/get-oauth-token.php`. |
| `SMTP_DEBUG` | int | `0` | SMTP debug level 0–4. |

## Support block

| Key | Sub-key | Default | Effect |
| --- | ------- | ------- | ------ |
| `support` | `name` | `''` | Custom company/support name shown in the backend dashboard. |
| `support` | `address` | `''` | Custom support address. |
| `support` | `phone` | `''` | Custom support phone number. |
| `support` | `email` | `''` | Custom support email; falls back to the GitHub support page when empty. |

<!-- docs/administration/admin-panel.md -->

# Admin panel

> Source: `phpwcms.php` (admin navigation, `do=admin` switch), `include/inc_tmpl/admin.update.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_lib/update/update.php`, `include/inc_lib/update/update.backup.php`, `include/inc_act/ajax_connector.php`, `include/inc_act/act_file.php`

The admin panel is the backend menu section **Admin**; the pages live under `phpwcms.php?do=admin` with a page ID (`p=`) each. It appears only to admin users, and each sub-page is additionally gated by a named permission. The full page map with page IDs and permission keys is documented in [Users and usergroups](users-usergroups.md) — see its [Admin panel reference](users-usergroups.md#admin-panel-reference) table. This page covers the entries without a dedicated page: System update, phpinfo, and the two maintenance actions.

## System update

Available to super admins (`usr_admin`) as **Admin → System Update**, page ID `p=18`. The panel is backed by the self-update engine in `include/inc_lib/update/update.php`; a standalone alternative and the full update paths are described in [Updating](../installation/updating.md).

The panel shows:

| Element | Behavior |
| ------- | -------- |
| Installed version | Version, release date and database revision (`r` value) of the current install. |
| Available version | Fetched from the GitHub releases API on first visit or via *Check for update*; the result is cached in the session. |
| Release notes | Rendered from the release body with a restricted Markdown subset (inline code, bold, http(s) links, lists); the text is HTML-escaped first. |
| Backup & update button | Starts an update run; requires CSRF token and POST. |
| Update history | Table of runs from the `phpwcms_update_log` database table with status badge and file count. |
| Rollback button | Offered per history row whenever a file backup exists — including rows stuck in `running`. |

A new run is blocked while database migrations are pending or failed (`phpwcms_revision_check_temp()`) and when the installed base version is `<= 2.0.0` — older installs must use [setup/upgrade.php](../installation/updating.md#standalone-upgrade-script) instead.

### Backup handling

Before touching any file, the engine writes a run directory `content/backup/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS>/`:

| Backup artifact | Content |
| --------------- | ------- |
| `database.sql.gz` | Gzipped dump (pure PHP, no `mysqldump`) of every table whose name starts with the configured table prefix: `DROP TABLE` + `CREATE TABLE` + row INSERTs per table. Written before the release zip is downloaded; a dump failure aborts the run. |
| `files/` | Mirror of every file the run will modify or delete, in document-root-relative paths. |
| `changed-files.txt` | Per-run report of added/modified/deleted files with sha256 hashes. |

The run directory gets a generated `.htaccess` (`Require all denied` / `Deny from all`). Free disk space below 10 MB aborts the update during preflight.

### Maintenance mode and rollback

While files are applied, a flag file `content/tmp/update/maintenance.flag` marks maintenance mode; the flag auto-expires after 15 minutes (stale flags mean the frontend serves normally) and can be cleared with the panel's *Clear maintenance mode* button. On any apply failure the flag stays active so a broken state is not exposed.

Rollback restores the `files/` mirror of the chosen run, marks the run `rolled_back` in the log and removes the document-root `.update-manifest` so the next update treats the install as manifest-less.

## phpinfo

**Admin → phpinfo()** (`p=15`) embeds `phpinfo()` output as HTML under the backend header, reusing the generated CSS while overriding the default body styling. The navigation link shows only for super admins; the page itself requires any `adm` admin permission. Use it to verify PHP version, extensions (`intl`, `gd`, `imagick`, `curl`, ...), loaded INI values and environment variables on a live install — the same data the setup wizard checks, but read-only.

## Maintenance actions

Both entries render for every member of the `adm` admin group in the sidebar. Execution is additionally checked per request:

| Action | Implementation | Permission | Effect |
| ------ | -------------- | ---------- | ------ |
| Flush image cache | `include/inc_act/ajax_connector.php?action=flush_image_cache` (CSRF token required) | `adm` | Deletes every `jpg`, `png`, `gif`, `svg` and `webp` file in `content/images/` — the generated resized/cropped versions. Source files in the filestorage are untouched; images regenerate on the next request. Reports the deleted file count. |
| Move deleted files | `include/inc_act/act_file.php?movedeletedfiles=<user id>` with a confirm dialog | `adm` or `filedelete` | Finds file rows flagged `f_trash = 9` (deleted but not yet purged) and either deletes the stored file or moves it to `filearchive/can_be_deleted/`, then marks the row `f_trash = 8`. Which of the two happens is controlled by `trash_delete_files`. |

After *Move deleted files*, clean up `filearchive/can_be_deleted/` manually — phpwcms never deletes the directory itself. Also flush the image cache after changing [image settings](image-processing.md); otherwise stale resized files keep serving old dimensions.

## Related

- [Users and usergroups](users-usergroups.md) — page map and permission keys
- [Updating](../installation/updating.md) — update paths, revision chain, 1.x migration
- [Image processing](image-processing.md) — what the image cache contains
- [File storage](file-storage.md) — `trash_delete_files`, filearchive layout

<!-- docs/administration/users-usergroups.md -->

# Users and usergroups

> Source: `include/inc_tmpl/admin.newuser.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/admin.edituser.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/admin.groups.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_act/act_user.php`, `include/inc_act/act_usergroup.php`, `phpwcms.php` (admin navigation)

Users are accounts with login credentials; usergroups group users and serve two purposes: membership lists and permission bundles. The admin panel appears only to users with `usr_admin = 1`, and every admin sub-page is additionally gated by a named permission (`adm*` key).

## Users

### Backend vs frontend users

One user account can serve either the backend or the frontend area — the *frontend user* switch decides which login it belongs to. Frontend users authenticate against `{FELOGIN}`-protected structure levels; backend users get the backend UI. Accounts flagged both see the backend and can enter FE-protected areas.

### Creating / editing

Managed from Admin → Users. Fields (create + edit):

| Field | Description |
| ----- | ----------- |
| Login name | `usr_login`, unique. |
| Password | `usr_pass`; new password field only appears on edit. |
| Real name | `usr_name`. |
| Email | `usr_email`; edit offers "send verification email" and separate new-email handling with `form_reset_*` toggles. |
| Active | switch — inactive accounts (`usr_aktiv` != 1) cannot log in but stay listed. |
| Admin | switch — grants backend (`usr_admin = 1`). |
| Frontend user | switch — makes the account a frontend account (`usr_fe = 1`). |
| Allowed content parts | `allowed_cp[]` multi-select — restricts which content part types this user may insert. Empty = all. |

Deletion (`act_user.php`) moves an account out of circulation rather than hard-deleting rows.

## Usergroups

### Member groups (editable)

A regular group holds a name, description, active flag and a **member list** chosen from all users:

| Field | Storage | Meaning |
| ----- | ------- | ------- |
| Name | `group_name` | 1–250 chars, required. |
| Description | `group_value` | Free text. |
| Members | `group_member` | Comma-separated user IDs, picked from both BE/FE accounts. |
| Active | `group_active` | Off = ignored at runtime; toggled per-row in the overview list. |

Deactivating (eye icon) or deleting (trash icon, `act_usergroup.php`) never touches the users themselves.

Frontend login areas and structure-level access lists reference these groups: a protected level lists group IDs / user IDs under `acat_access`, and its `acat_feusers` counterpart holds the allowed accounts. See [Structure tree](../backend/02-structure-tree.md).

### Permission groups (SYSGROUP)

A second set of groups lives in `phpwcms_sysvalue` keyed as SYSGROUP entries with fixed `group_syskey` names. They are read-only in the group editor and define who may use admin panel areas. Admin users are auto-added to all SYSGROUPs at login (`phpwcms.php` ensures `usr_admin` members). The keys:

| Sysgroup key | Grants |
| ------------ | ------ |
| `admlayout` | Admin → Page layout |
| `admtempl` | Admin → Templates, Template translations |
| `admcustomcpt` | Admin → Custom content parts |
| `admmailtpl` | Admin → Email templates |
| `admuser` | Admin → Users |
| `admugroup` | Admin → Usergroups |
| `admialias` | Admin → Image aliases |
| `admfilecat` | Admin → File categories |
| `admalias` | Admin → Aliases |
| `admlink` | Admin → Links & redirects |

Super admins (`usr_admin`) additionally get System update and phpinfo. The check runs through `has_admin_permission($key)`.

### Module groups

Every installed module auto-creates a matching group on first visit to the groups page (`group_modkey = <module name>`, seeded with all superadmins as members). Backend module menu visibility is driven by group membership there; see [Modules overview](../modules/index.md).

## Admin panel reference

Nav gating shown below; page IDs (`p=`) match `phpwcms.php?do=admin&p=N`.

| Page | Permission |
| ---- | ---------- |
| Users (`p=0`) | `admuser` |
| Usergroups (`p=1`) | `admugroup` |
| File categories (`p=7`) | `admfilecat` |
| Page layout (`p=8`) | `admlayout` |
| Templates (`p=11`) | `admtempl` |
| Image aliases (`p=12`) | `admialias` |
| Aliases (`p=13`) | `admalias` |
| Links & redirects (`p=14`) | `admlink` |
| phpinfo (`p=15`) | super admin only |
| Custom content parts (`p=16`) | `admcustomcpt` |
| Template translations (`p=17`) | `admtempl` |
| System update (`p=18`) | super admin only |
| Email templates (`p=19`) | `admmailtpl` |

Plus two maintenance actions available with any admin permission: flush image cache and move deleted files.

## Related

- [Admin panel](admin-panel.md) — configuration entries and maintenance
- [Structure tree](../backend/02-structure-tree.md) — per-level access assignment

<!-- docs/administration/file-storage.md -->

# File storage

> Source: `include/inc_lib/general.inc.php` (upload validation), `include/inc_tmpl/files.private.upload.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/files.ftptakeover.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_act/act_file.php`, `include/config/dist.conf.inc.php`

All uploaded files live in a single storage directory on the server, referenced by hash inside the database. There is no backend GUI for these values — file storage behaves according to the settings in `include/config/conf.inc.php` (defaults below come from `dist.conf.inc.php`).

## Settings

> Source: `include/config/dist.conf.inc.php`; validation flow in `include/inc_lib/general.inc.php`

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `file_path` | string | `'filearchive'` | Filestorage directory name below the document root. |
| `ftp_path` | string | `'upload'` | Directory the [FTP takeover](#ftp-takeover) reads. Must not start or end with a slash. |
| `file_maxsize` | int (bytes) | `52428800` (50 MB) | Per-file upload size cap. Also clamps the guestbook image size. Effective limits are additionally bounded by PHP's `upload_max_filesize` / `post_max_size`. |
| `allowed_upload_ext` | string (comma-separated) | long extension list (jpg, png, webp, pdf, zip, mp4, ...) | Extension whitelist for uploads. A file whose extension is not listed is rejected with HTTP error 415. |
| `multimedia_ext` | string | `'aif,aiff,mov,...'` | Extensions the file browser treats as multimedia entries. |
| `trash_delete_files` | bool | `false` | If `true`, emptying a file trash physically deletes the stored file. If `false`, the maintenance action moves it to `filearchive/can_be_deleted/` instead; see [Admin panel](admin-panel.md#maintenance-actions). |
| `sanitize_dlname` | bool | `0` | Rewrite special characters in `Content-Disposition` filenames on download when browsers choke on them. |
| `inline_download` | bool | `1` | Try to display downloads in the browser (`inline`) instead of forcing `attachment`. |
| `recipient_count` | int | `0` | Legacy key; the setting is no longer read in 2.x code and has no effect. It still exists in `conf.inc.php` written by the setup wizard. |

There is no storage quota system: the only limit is `file_maxsize` per file plus the disk space of the host.

## Upload processing

Every upload — through the file center dialog, drag-and-drop or FTP takeover — passes the same checks in order:

1. Filename sanitization, extension detection.
2. Size check against `file_maxsize`.
3. Target directory creation below the filestorage.
4. Extension check against `allowed_upload_ext` (case-insensitive). Rejected uploads remove the temporary file.
5. For image targets: `getimagesize()` against an allowlist of image types — content sniffing by actual image data, not by client MIME type.

Incoming client MIME types are only trusted when they match a MIME format pattern; otherwise the MIME type is derived from the extension map in `include/inc_lib/mimetype.inc.php`. On download, the `fileinfo` extension re-detects the MIME type of `application/octet-stream`/`force-download` files.

## filearchive layout

The filestorage stores files under their md5 `<hash>.<ext>` names, which the `phpwcms_file` database table maps to original names, folders, categories and permissions. Special entries:

| Entry | Meaning |
| ----- | ------- |
| `<hash>.<ext>` files | Uploaded originals as placed by upload/FTP takeover. |
| `can_be_deleted/` | Landing folder of the *Move deleted files* maintenance action. Never auto-purged; delete manually. |
| `image_placeholder.png` | Serves as fallback when a referenced source image is missing. |
| `image_memoryinfo.png` | Replaces an image when PHP memory is too low to resize it. |

The default `.htaccess`/web-server config should treat the directory as non-executable storage; downloads flow through `download.php` with resumable range support and ETag headers, not direct links.

## FTP takeover

Files uploaded by FTP into `ftp_path` (default `upload/`) appear in **Files → FTP upload**, listing name, size and date with checkboxes. Submitting the form (`include/inc_act/act_ftptakeover.php`) imports the marked files into a chosen file-center folder: they move into the filestorage under hash names and get database rows. The directory is scanned without an extension filter, but each import still passes the [upload validation](#upload-processing) checks.

## Related

- [Admin panel](admin-panel.md) — maintenance actions that clean or purge the filestorage
- [Users and usergroups](users-usergroups.md) — file categories (`p=7`) permission
- [Fresh installation](../installation/fresh-install.md) — writable directories on first install

<!-- docs/administration/seo-settings.md -->

# SEO settings

> Source: `include/config/dist.conf.inc.php`, `include/inc_front/front.func.inc.php` (structure data, meta tags), `include/inc_front/content.article.inc.php` (canonical), `sitemap.php`, root files `example.robots.txt`, `ai.txt`, `example.llms.txt`

All values are `include/config/conf.inc.php` keys; defaults quoted from `dist.conf.inc.php`. Per-page SEO fields (article/structure level) are edited in the backend; see [Structure tree](../backend/02-structure-tree.md) for the level form.

## URL rewriting and aliases

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `rewrite_url` | bool | `1` | Enables rewritten URLs; the frontend then renders `/im/` style image URLs and alias paths handled by the web server rewrite rules (templates in `_.htaccess`, `nginx.conf`, `web.config`). |
| `rewrite_ext` | string | `'.html'` | URL suffix: `/alias.html` (default) or a trailing `/` when set to `/`. |
| `alias_allow_slash` | bool | `1` | Permits `/` inside structure/article aliases. |
| `alias_allow_utf8` | bool | `1` | Keeps UTF-8 special characters in aliases (charset must be utf-8). |
| `allow_empty_alias` | bool | `false` | `true` prevents phpwcms from auto-creating an alias when the alias field is left empty. |
| `reserved_alias` | array | `[]` | List of alias names that may never be used (e.g. `array('admin', 'download')`). |
| `force301_id2alias` | bool | `false` | Sends a 301 redirect when an article/structure has an alias but the page is called by ID. |
| `force301_2struct` | bool | `false` | Sends a 301 redirect to the structure level when the level contains exactly one article. |
| `GET_pageinfo` | bool | `0` | Appends `&pageinfo=/cat1/cat2/page-title.htm` breadcrumb information to site links. |
| `remove_empty_get_vars` | bool | `true` | Drops valueless GET parameters (except the alias) from URLs. |
| `log_404error` | bool | `false` | Logs each 404 hit so redirects can be defined from the log; the redirect editor lives in Admin → Links & redirects (`p=14`). |
| `disable_next_prev` | bool | `false` | `true` suppresses the `<link rel="prev">`/`<link rel="next">` head tags that content-part pagination emits (the pagination links themselves still render). |

Rewriting only works when the web server passes unmatched requests to `index.php` — ship the matching rewrite config (`_.htaccess` renamed to `.htaccess` for Apache is created by the setup wizard; [Setup wizard](../installation/setup-wizard.md)). A missing `mode_rewrite`-style rewrite setup yields `index.php?alias` URLs but no broken pages, because both forms render.

## Meta tags from structure levels and articles

For each level phpwcms reads `acat_keywords`, `acat_info` and `acat_pagetitle`, for each article `article_keywords` and `article_description`:

| Rendered meta tag | Filled from |
| ----------------- | ----------- |
| `<meta name="description">` | Custom `meta.description` head block set via template/level; otherwise the structure level's `acat_info` (Info field). |
| `<meta name="keywords">` | Merged keywords of the current structure level and article(s). |
| Page title | Layout template title plus level `acat_pagetitle`/`acat_overwrite` settings. |

`enable_GDPR` (default `true`) additionally makes search-engine-related logging anonymize IPs where phpwcms handles logging itself (see [Modules overview](../modules/index.md)).

## Canonical links

| Key / field | Values | Effect |
| ----------- | ------ | ------ |
| `canonical_off` | bool, default `false` | `true` disables canonical tag output entirely. |
| `acat_canonical` (structure level) | string | Explicit canonical URL that overrides the generated one for this level. |
| `article_canonical` (article) | string | Explicit canonical URL for the article; overrides level value. |

Without an explicit value the canonical points to the article's own URL — including the canonical target of a content-part pagination (`...-<page>` alias) — and falls back to the level's single-article alias when `force301_2struct` is off.

## Open Graph and Twitter

| Key / field | Type | Default | Effect |
| ----------- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `set_sociallink` | array | `['article' => false, 'articlecat' => false, 'news' => false, 'shop' => false, 'render' => true]` | Per-type default state of the social/OpenGraph switch and whether OpenGraph meta renders at all (`render`). The per-article/level/News switch overrides the defaults. |
| `acat_opengraph` (level) | bool | default `1` | Disables OpenGraph for the whole structure branch when off. |
| `article_opengraph` (article) | bool | — | Per-article switch (`article_opengraph` field in the article form). |
| `opengraph_imagesize` | string | `'1200x630x0'` | Size spec `WxH[x1=crop]` the `og:image` thumbnail is generated with; ignored when empty (then `1200x630x1`). |
| `twitter_site` | string | `''` | `@handle` of the website account, emitted as `twitter:site`. `twitter:card` and `twitter:creator` are always emitted while OpenGraph renders. |

The OpenGraph title, description, URL and type (`website` / `article`) are composed from level/article data automatically; the image is the first article/level social image, rendered through the [image processing pipeline](image-processing.md).

## Sitemap

`sitemap.php` in the document root emits a Google-style XML sitemap. Include it in a [robots.txt](#robots-ai-txt-and-llms-txt) or in search console to get articles indexed.

- Lists active, non-deleted, search-visible articles on public, sitemap-enabled structure levels, plus active [News](../modules/index.md) module entries.
- A level or article participates only when its *Sitemap* checkbox (`acat_nositemap` = 1 / `article_nositemap` = 1) is set — the field name is inherited from older versions although the meaning is "include in sitemap".
- Custom URLs: create `include/config/sitemap.custom.php` defining `phpwcms_getCustomSitemap(&$struct)` returning `array('url' => ..., 'date' => ...)` entries, or add entries to `include/config/sitemap.custom.ini` in INI sections (`[1] url = "https://..."` / `date = "YYYY-MM-DD"`). Both ship as templates.
- When no article qualifies, the base URL alone is emitted; flags `sitemap_set_base` / `sitemap_set_default` in the custom functions control whether the base link and all default articles render.
- Output is cached for 12 hours in `content/cache/sitemap.cache.xml` — delete the file to force regeneration after publishing.

<a id="robots-ai-txt-and-llms-txt"></a>
## robots, ai.txt and llms.txt

These are plain static files served from the document root — no code renders them. The repository ships examples only for `robots.txt`; use them as starting points:

| File | Ships as | Purpose |
| ---- | -------- | ------- |
| `robots.txt` | `example.robots.txt` | Search crawler rules plus `Sitemap:` line pointing at `sitemap.php`. |
| `ai.txt` | `ai.txt` (active) and `example.ai.txt` | Bot-specific crawling rules, protection for `/login.php`, `/filearchive/`, `/include/`, `/setup/`, and an EU TDM Article 4(3) reservation. |
| `llms.txt` | `llms.txt` (active) and `example.llms.txt` | Structured project context for LLMs per the llmstxt.org specification. |

Copy the active `ai.txt`/`llms.txt` or adapt the examples for your domain; the updater preserves `robots.txt` during an update.

## Search logging

`enable_seolog` (default `1`) enables logging of search engine referrer data (bot identification + search referrers) consumed by the [SEO log module](../modules/index.md). Bot user agents additionally skip sessions — the list is the `BOTS` config array (read-only behavior, `googlebot`, `bingbot`, ...).

## Related

- [Cache and performance](cache-performance.md) — page delivery, HTTP cache headers
- [Admin panel](admin-panel.md) — where the update engine and redirect editor sit
- [Structure tree](../backend/02-structure-tree.md) — per-level SEO fields
