<!-- docs/administration/cache-performance.md -->

# Cache and performance

> Source: `index.php` (page delivery, cache headers), `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php` (structure cache, lazy loading), `include/inc_lib/imagick.convert.inc.php` (image cache), `sitemap.php` (sitemap cache), `include/config/dist.conf.inc.php`

## Page delivery

phpwcms renders every page on request and builds no full-page cache table. The former 1.x page cache (`phpwcms_cache` database table, controlled by `cache_enabled`) does not exist in 2.x: no code reads `cache_enabled`, and the two remaining keys only steer HTTP headers.

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `cache_enabled` | bool | `0` | Legacy key. Read nowhere in 2.x code; kept for configuration compatibility. |
| `cache_timeout` | int (seconds) | `0` | When set, the frontend sends `Expires`, `Last-Modified`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<timeout>` and `Pragma: public` headers with each page. `0` disables them. |

Output compression (gzip/deflate) is not handled by phpwcms — the web server does it (`mod_deflate`/`mod_brotli`, `ngx_http_gzip_module`). File downloads explicitly disable `zlib.output_compression` so binary delivery stays intact.

## Server-side data caches

| Cache | Location | Invalidates |
| ----- | -------- | ----------- |
| Image cache (generated sizes) | `content/images/` — one file per width/height/crop/quality/sharpen/colorspace combination, named by md5 thumb key | Admin → [Flush image cache](admin-panel.md#maintenance-actions); regenerate automatically on next request |
| Structure meta cache | `phpwcms_sysvalue` table, key `frontend_render` — serialized level/article metadata | Rebuilt automatically while rendering; no manual action needed |
| Sitemap cache | `content/cache/sitemap.cache.xml`, 12 hours | Delete the file after publishing to regenerate immediately |
| Image convert cache | `content/images/<hash>-<function>.<ext>` for `/im/convert...` endpoint requests (e.g. grayscale conversion) so repeated conversion requests stay cheap | Part of the image cache, flushed together |

## Lazy loading

`lazy_loading` (string, default `'lazy'`) controls how images and iframes load: `lazy` (recommended), `eager`, or `auto`. Templates render `{LAZY_LOADING}` where the value should appear in markup; the frontend replaces the tag globally in the rendered page. See [Template system](../templates/template-system.md) for placement inside custom templates.

## Performance-relevant switches

| Key | Default | Effect |
| --- | ------- | ------ |
| `gd_memcheck_off` | `0` | `1` disables the PHP memory pre-check before GD resizing (faster on known-good hosts, riskier on small memory limits). |
| `version_check` | `1` | Checks the current phpwcms release online for [System update](../installation/updating.md) notifications; `0` for offline servers. |
| `render_clean_html` | `0` | Strips HTML comments from the page source before output; marked experimental. |
| `recipient_count` | `0` | Legacy, no longer read in 2.x. |

Frontend sessions add database work per request: keep `SESSION_FEinit` at `0` (default) when no [frontend login](../general/concepts.md) is used. Bot user agents never start sessions regardless.

## Debug and diagnosis switches

| Key | Default | Effect |
| --- | ------- | ------ |
| `db_errorlog` | `false` | Logs database queries/errors — enable only while diagnosing. |
| `log_404error` | `false` | Logs each 404 for the redirect editor; see [SEO settings](seo-settings.md). |
| `SMTP_DEBUG` | `0` | SMTP debug level 0–4 for mail delivery problems; see [Configuration file](../installation/config-file.md). |
| `disable_generator` | `false` | `true` removes `<meta name="generator">` and the `X-phpwcms-Release` response header. |
| `disable_processed_in` | `false` | `true` removes the `X-phpwcms-Page-Processed-In` response header that reports page render time. |
| `browser_check` | array (`fe`/`be` = `false`) | Enables the browser-update.org notice in frontend and/or backend for outdated browsers ("vs" sets version rules, "insecure"/"required" tune behavior). |

Whitelabel mode force-disables the generator and processing-time headers; see [Whitelabel branding](whitelabel.md).

## Related

- [Admin panel](admin-panel.md) — image cache flushing, update maintenance mode
- [Image processing](image-processing.md) — how the cache file names derive from parameters
- [Configuration file](../installation/config-file.md) — full key reference

<!-- docs/administration/image-processing.md -->

# Image processing

> Source: `include/config/dist.conf.inc.php`, `include/inc_lib/helper.image.php` (`Phpwcms_Image_lib`), `include/inc_lib/imagick.convert.inc.php` (`image_manipulate()`, `get_cached_image()`), `include/inc_lib/general.inc.php` (`is_ext_true()`), `img/cmsimage.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/admin.imagealiaslist.tmpl.php`

## Graphics engine

`image_library` selects the engine; `library_path` holds the binary directory when a CLI tool is used.

| Value | Engine | Notes |
| ----- | ------ | ----- |
| `GD2` | PHP GD extension | Default. Handles jpg, gif, png, webp; no sharpening, no EPS/AI/PS/PDF source rendering. |
| `Imagick` | PHP Imagick (PECL) extension | Highest priority recommendation when installed. |
| `ImageMagick` | ImageMagick CLI (`convert`/`magick`) | Needs `library_path`. |
| `GraphicsMagick` or `GM` | GraphicsMagick CLI (`gm`) | Needs `library_path`. |
| `NetPBM` | NetPBM CLI tools (`pnmscale`) | Needs `library_path`. |

The setup wizard detects installed tools (`detect_system_image_tools()`) and recommends Imagick > ImageMagick > GraphicsMagick > GD2. GD 1.x support was dropped in 2.x.

## Source formats

Thumbnail sources depend on the engine — `is_ext_true()` maps an upload extension to the engine's working format:

| Source extensions | GD2 | ImageMagick / GraphicsMagick / Imagick |
| ----------------- | --- | -------------------------------------- |
| jpg, jpeg | yes (jpg) | yes (jpg) |
| png, gif, webp, svg | yes | yes |
| tif, tiff, psd, bmp, pic, wmf, tga, jp2, ico, ... | no | converted, target jpg |
| **eps, ps, ai, pdf** | no | rendered to png; PostScript/PDF requires Ghostscript (`gs`) plus an ImageMagick `policy.xml` that grants PDF/EPS/PS read|write rights |

`imgext_disabled` (comma-separated string, default empty) excludes types from image handling — e.g. `'pdf,ps'`. Image extensions are also filtered at the SQL level when GD2 is active: the file query restricts to `jpg, jpeg, png, gif, bmp, svg, webp`.

The Docker image ships ImageMagick, GraphicsMagick, NetPBM, Ghostscript and the Imagick PHP extension with the PDF/EPS/PS/XPS policy entries enabled; see [Docker installation](../installation/docker.md).

## Quality, sharpening, colorspace

| Key | Default | Applies to | Effect |
| --- | ------- | ---------- | ------ |
| `jpg_quality` | `85` | all engines | JPEG output quality 25–100. |
| `webp_enable` | `1` | all engines | Delivers resized images as WebP when the client supports it; source stays intact. |
| `webp_quality` | `85` | all engines | WebP output quality. |
| `sharpen_level` | `1` | ImageMagick/GM/Imagick | 0 = off … 5 = extra sharp. Ignored by GD. |
| `resize_animated_gif` | `true` | all engines | Attempts resizing animated GIF frames; can increase file size. |
| `im_fix_colorspace` | `'RGB'` | ImageMagick-based | Colorspace written into converted images; switch to `SRGB` when colors render wrong on newer ImageMagick builds. The `xGS` parameter in the [image endpoint](#dynamic-image-endpoint) converts to gray instead. |
| `gd_memcheck_off` | `0` | GD | `1` skips the automatic memory-limit adjustment before resizing. |

## Default image dimensions

| Key | Default | Effect |
| --- | ------- | ------ |
| `content_width` | `978` | Maximum article content column width; base for multi-column image rendering. |
| `img_list_width` / `img_list_height` | `160` / `100` | File list thumbnail size. |
| `img_prev_width` / `img_prev_height` | `978` / `734` | Large preview size; also the fallback dimension when only one target dimension is given. |
| `responsive` | `1` | `1` keeps given image sizes, `0` caps width at `content_width`. |
| `preserve_image_name` | `1` | Keeps the original file name for resized versions. |

## Dynamic image endpoint

Resized/cropped images are requested through one URL. With rewriting enabled the path is `/im/...`, otherwise `img/cmsimage.php?...`:

```
/im/WIDTH[[xHEIGHT][xCROP][xQUALITY][xGS]]/HASH.EXT
```

- `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` in px, either may be `0`.
- `CROP`: `1` crops centered; `2`-`19` divide the target into a grid; a position suffix `-tl`, `-tc`, `-tr`, `-cl`, `-cr`, `-bl`, `-bc`, `-br` moves the crop origin.
- `QUALITY` 10–100 overrides `jpg_quality`/`webp_quality`.
- `GS` delivers a grayscale conversion.
- The file part is the md5 storage hash (or file ID) plus extension; SVG files are passed through as XML with recalculated dimensions instead of raster resizing.
- `cmsimage_redirect` (`false`) redirects to the static generated file in `content/images/` instead of streaming it through the endpoint.

`cmsimage_settings` (array, default empty) prevents endpoint flooding: list every allowed size string, e.g. `array('500x500x0', 'default' => '1280x800x1')`. The `default` entry (or the first entry) applies when a request uses an unlisted size; `'empty'` returns a transparent GIF instead.

## Image aliases

Admin → Image aliases (`p=12`) manages the `f_alias` column of the `phpwcms_file` table. The page lists image files that have no alias yet and can batch-generate aliases from their file names, optionally prefixed with a keyword; aliases are sanitized for uniqueness. Alias values stay editable per file in the file center.

## Related

- [Admin panel](admin-panel.md) — image cache flushing
- [Cache and performance](cache-performance.md) — image cache location and invalidation
- [Configuration file](../installation/config-file.md) — full key reference
- [Text w/image](../content-parts/01-text-with-image.md) — content part using the pipeline

<!-- docs/administration/whitelabel.md -->

# Whitelabel branding

> Source: `include/inc_lib/whitelabel.inc.php`, `bin/WHITELABEL.md`, `setup/inc/setup.func.inc.php` (`setup_validate_whitelabel_key()`), `include/config/dist.conf.inc.php`

Whitelabel mode replaces the phpwcms identity in the backend with your own brand. It requires a valid signature — the feature is config-driven but cryptographically secured against arbitrary rebranding:

- The key is a single string: `<base64url(payload JSON)>.<base64url(Ed25519 signature)>`.
- Verification uses libsodium (`sodium_crypto_sign_verify_detached`) against the embedded master public key in `whitelabel.inc.php`. Without the `sodium` extension, whitelabel never activates.
- The payload carries licensee, domain pattern, brand name, table prefix and optional expiry (`valid_until` as Unix timestamp); an expired key deactivates whitelabel.
- The domain pattern matches the current `HTTP_HOST`: `*` for any host, exact domain, or `*.domain.com` wildcard.

The setup wizard validates a pasted key live and shows licensee, domain and expiry (see [Setup wizard](../installation/setup-wizard.md)); a CLI checker/inspector exists in the maintainer toolchain (`bin/whitelabel-license.php --verify="<key>"`).

## Configuration keys

> Source: `include/config/dist.conf.inc.php`, `include/inc_lib/whitelabel.inc.php`

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------ |
| `whitelabel_key` | string | `''` | Signed license key; empty or invalid means standard phpwcms branding. |
| `brand_name` | string | `''` | Product name replacing "phpwcms" across backend UI, page titles, labels and messages. Falls back to the license payload's `brand_name` when empty. |
| `brand_logo_light` | string | `''` | Logo URL or path for the light theme (backend header, login page). |
| `brand_logo_dark` | string | `''` | Logo for dark theme; falls back to `brand_logo_light` when empty. |
| `brand_logo_email` | string | `''` | Email logo as URL or `data:image/...;base64` data URI (raster PNG/JPG/WebP/GIF only). Falls back to `brand_logo_light` when it is a raster image. |
| `brand_custom_css` | string | `''` | Backend stylesheet URL or path, injected as a `<link>` for UI theming. |
| `brand_support_url` | string | `''` | Custom support/documentation URL. |
| `brand_url` | string | `''` | Product website URL used in the footer; falls back to `brand_support_url`. |
| `brand_copyright` | string | `''` | Footer copyright text, prefixed with `Copyright © <year>` unless it already contains a copyright notice; falls back to the license payload's copyright, then licensee. |
| `brand_table_prefix` | string | `''` | Non-`phpwcms` database table prefix in whitelabel mode (see below). |

Configuration values always win over license payload values when both are set.

## What whitelabel mode changes

When `phpwcms_whitelabel_init()` activates (`PHPWCMS_WHITELABEL` defined, `is_whitelabel()` true):

- Language strings and UI text containing `phpwcms`, `phpWCMS` or `PHPWCMS` are rewritten to the brand name (`apply_brand_replacements()`), including release notes shown in the update panel.
- The backend footer, login page footer and the About dialog show brand name, logo, URL and copyright instead of the phpwcms attribution and GitHub link.
- `<meta name="generator">` and the `X-phpwcms-Release` and `X-phpwcms-Page-Processed-In` HTTP headers are disabled regardless of their own config keys.

Without an active license the standard branding (footer linking github.com/slackero/phpwcms, default logo and copyright) renders.

## Database table prefix

The effective table prefix is assembled in `include/inc_lib/dbcon.inc.php`:

```
DB_PREPEND = [<db_prepend>_]<brand_table_prefix>_
```

`brand_table_prefix` defaults to `phpwcms`, so standard installs keep `phpwcms_` table names. In whitelabel mode the prefix becomes `<brand_prefix>_` (e.g. `cmsgo_phpwcms_article`) — set it before the first install since it decides every table name; changing it later would leave the schema orphaned. The setup wizard exposes a *Brand Table Prefix* field on the database step when a valid license key is present (`[a-zA-Z0-9_]` only), and the standalone updater can repair it in existing installs ([Updating](../installation/updating.md)). `db_prepend` still works as an optional additional namespace in front of it.

## Example configuration

```php
$phpwcms['whitelabel_key']    = 'eyJsaWNlbnNlZSI6...';
$phpwcms['brand_name']        = 'Brand';
$phpwcms['brand_logo_light']  = 'img/brand-logo.svg';
$phpwcms['brand_logo_dark']   = 'img/brand-logo-dark.svg';
$phpwcms['brand_custom_css']  = 'template/inc_css/brand.css';
$phpwcms['brand_support_url'] = 'https://www.example.com/support';
$phpwcms['brand_url']         = 'https://www.example.com';
$phpwcms['brand_copyright']   = 'Example Dev Team';
$phpwcms['brand_table_prefix']= 'example';
```

## Related

- [Setup wizard](../installation/setup-wizard.md) — license entry during installation
- [Configuration file](../installation/config-file.md) — full key reference
- [Admin panel](admin-panel.md) — branding in the update panel

<!-- docs/backend/01-overview.md -->

# Backend overview

> Source: `phpwcms.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/be_start.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_lib/backend.functions.inc.php`, `include/inc_lib/whitelabel.inc.php`, `include/inc_lib/wysiwyg.editor.inc.php`, `include/inc_lib/default.inc.php` (theme helpers)

The backend lives at `/phpwcms.php` and requires a login through `login.php`. It is a Bootstrap 5 based single-column application: a fixed header bar, a collapsible left navigation, the content area, and a footer. Every page is output with the charset configured in the installation and a `Content-Security-Policy` meta tag assembled in `phpwcms.php`.

## Layout

| Area | Content |
| ---- | ------- |
| Header | Brand logo (link to the backend home), frontend preview link, search, profile link, logout, theme switcher |
| Left sidebar | Main navigation described below, a collapse button, and a small footer line listing loaded JS libraries |
| Content | The active section, wrapped as cards; a status message (success/error) is rendered above it |
| Footer | Version and copyright, switchable by the whitelabel feature (`is_whitelabel()`, `get_brand_name()`) |

Branding, logo, footer wording and custom CSS can be replaced by whitelabel settings from `include/config/custom_settings.php`; see `include/inc_lib/whitelabel.inc.php`.

## Main navigation

> Source: `phpwcms.php` (nav building), `include/inc_lib/navi_text.inc.php`

The sidebar shows an item only when the user has the matching permission. Permissions come from active, non-trashed usergroups whose `group_syskey` matches the key below, and super admins (`usr_admin = 1`) pass every check. See [Users and usergroups](../administration/users-usergroups.md).

| Item | Icon | Gated by | Links to |
| ---- | ---- | -------- | -------- |
| Dashboard | `fa-tachometer-alt` | always | `phpwcms.php` |
| Articles | `fa-copy` | `artcent` or `artnews` | Article center, New article (requires `artcent`), News (requires `artnews`) |
| Files | `fa-folder-open` | `filecent`; sub-items additionally `fileaction`, `fileupload` | File center, File actions, Multiple file upload |
| Modules | `fa-puzzle-piece` | `enable_backend_module` config plus `module` group; per-module `group_modkey` groups | one entry per module |
| Communication | `fa-envelope` | `enable_backend_newsletter` config plus `nl`; sub-items additionally `nlabo`, `nllist`, `nlrecip` | Newsletter subscriptions, Newsletter, Newsletter subscribers |
| Admin | `fa-cog` | `adm`; sub-items per page (`admlayout`, `admtempl`, `admuser`, `admugroup`, `admialias`, `admfilecat`, `admalias`, `admlink`, …) | Page layout, Templates, User administration, User groups, and so on |

Below the Admin menu, users with any admin permission also find two maintenance actions: *Flush image cache* (AJAX call to `include/inc_act/ajax_connector.php`) and *Move deleted files* (`include/inc_act/act_file.php?movedeletedfiles=…`). Super admins additionally get *System update* and `phpinfo()`.

The header holds the per-user items instead: the account menu opens the [Profile](06-profile.md) page (visible when the user is member of the `profile` group or is an admin, with different icons for super admin, frontend user and backend user), and *Logout* ends the session.

## Dashboard

> Source: `include/inc_tmpl/be_start.tmpl.php`, plus `template/inc_default/startup.php`

The dashboard (`phpwcms.php` without parameters) lists two tables: the most recently edited articles and the most recently edited [content parts](../general/concepts.md#the-content-hierarchy). For both, the top drop-down chooses the row count — 5 to 150 or all — and the value is stored in the `homeMaxArticles` / `homeMaxCntParts` cookies for one year. A hidden content type filter (`homeCntType`) narrows the content part list. Both lists offer a visibility toggle (eye icon) and an edit link per row; non-admin users only ever see their own articles here.

The installation's own `template/inc_default/startup.php` renders additional dashboard widgets and can be customized per template.

## Header search

> Source: `phpwcms.php` (search form), `include/inc_tmpl/be_start.tmpl.php`

The search icon in the header opens a form whose term is stored in `$_SESSION['phpwcms_backend_search']` and applied on the next dashboard view: article rows are matched against title, subtitle and summary; content part rows against title, subtitle, text and HTML body. The heading above each list shows `Search: <term>` while a term is set; clearing the search resets the session value.

## User context

Login state is kept in the session (`checkLogin()`). The most relevant values:

| Session value | Meaning |
| ------------- | ------- |
| `wcs_user_id`, `wcs_user`, `wcs_user_name` | Account ID, login name, display name |
| `wcs_user_admin` | 1 = super admin; bypasses every group check `has_admin_permission()` performs |
| `wcs_user_lang` | Backend language; validated against `include/inc_lang/backend/<lang>/` |
| `wcs_user_theme` | Backend theme, see below |
| `WYSIWYG_EDITOR` | WYSIWYG choice, see below |
| `wcs_user_cp` | Content parts the user has selected to be offered when adding parts |
| `wcs_allowed_cp` | Content parts allowed by the account (empty = all) |
| `structure` | Structure tree expansion state per user, persisted in `usr_var_structure` |

## WYSIWYG editor settings

> Source: `include/inc_lib/wysiwyg.editor.inc.php`

The editor used for the [article summary](03-articles.md) and for content part rich text is chosen per user in the [profile](06-profile.md#account-card):

| Value | Editor |
| ----- | ------ |
| 0 | Plain textarea (editor off) |
| 1 | CKEditor 4 — loaded from `include/inc_ext/ckeditor/`; custom configuration in `template/config/ckeditor/ckeditor.config.js` (or `ckeditor.config-tabs.js` for tabbed forms) when present, otherwise a built-in toolbar |
| 2 | TinyMCE 8 — loaded from `include/vendor/`, German and other UI languages via `include/vendor/mklkj/tinymce-i18n/` |

With `FCK_FileBrowser` enabled in the configuration, both editors get file/article browser pickers backed by `filebrowser.php` and `articlebrowser.php`.

## Theme switching

> Source: `phpwcms.php`, `include/inc_lib/backend.functions.inc.php` (`get_backend_theme()`, `set_theme_cookie()`), `include/inc_lib/default.inc.php` (`get_theme_boot_script()`)

The adjustment icon in the header opens a drop-down with **Auto**, **Light** and **Dark**. The choice is persisted as `wcs_user_theme` in the session and database, mirrored into the `phpwcmsBETheme` cookie and into `localStorage("phpwcms_theme")` as an AJAX fallback. An inline boot script set in `get_theme_boot_script()` sets `data-theme` and resolves `data-bs-theme` to the stored value — or to `prefers-color-scheme` for *Auto* — before the stylesheet renders, so no light/dark flash occurs. The same choice exists as a form field in the [profile](06-profile.md#account-card) page.

## Other interface conventions

- **Icons**: FontAwesome 7 Free/Brands glyphs bundled in `include/inc_css/backend.min.css`; icon-only controls carry real `<i>` elements and tooltips.
- **CSRF**: every backend link carries a token generated by `get_token_get_string()`; POST forms include hidden token fields (`validate_csrf_tokens()` runs on every request).
- **Sidebar**: the collapse toggle stores its state in `localStorage("phpwcms_sidebar_collapsed")`; on small screens the bars icon (`#button-menu`) toggles the menu instead.
- **Status messages**: backend actions report through `set_status_message()` / `show_status_message()` and appear at the top of the next page.
- **Keyboard shortcuts**: the current backend defines no global keyboard shortcuts; interaction is mouse/touch based.

- [Articles](03-articles.md)
- [Files — file center](04-files-filecenter.md)
- [Messaging](05-messaging.md)
- [Profile](06-profile.md)

<!-- docs/backend/02-structure-tree.md -->

# Structure tree

> Source: `include/inc_tmpl/article.structlist.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_lib/admin.functions.inc.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/admin.structform.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_lib/admin.structure.inc.php`, `include/inc_act/act_structure.php`

The first tab of the **Articles** section renders the site's structure tree: level 0 (the index page) at the top, its [structure levels](../general/concepts.md#the-content-hierarchy) as folder rows, and each level's articles nested below. `phpwcms.php?do=articles` and `phpwcms.php?do=articles&p=6` show the same tree; the struct form itself opens under `p=6&struct=<level_id>` (or `struct=index` for level 0).

Saving a level is gated by the `artstruc` SYSGROUP — writes through `include/inc_act/act_structure.php` are ignored for users outside that group or without super admin rights.

## Tree actions

> Source: `include/inc_lib/admin.functions.inc.php` (`listmode_edits()`), `include/inc_act/act_structure.php`

Every level row offers a pencil edit button, a **More actions** drop-down, and a visibility toggle:

| Action | Behavior |
| ------ | -------- |
| Insert level | Opens the struct form with a new parent (`struct=<id>`) and a sort value of `(child count + 1) * 10` |
| New article | Opens the article form with that level preselected |
| Copy level | Marks the level; clicking the paste arrow on any target level creates a deep copy — level, its settings (with a fresh alias), all articles and all child levels (`copy_level_to_level()`); non-admins become the owner of the copy |
| Cut level | Marks the level; the paste arrow moves it under the target level (`acat_struct`, `acat_sort`), with the target's own subtree excluded |
| Sort up / Sort down | Swaps the `acat_sort` values between neighbors; both values must be ≥ 10 |
| Delete | Marks the level `acat_trash = 9`, renames its alias to `<alias>_del-<timestamp>`, and marks all contained child levels and articles deleted the same way |
| Eye icon | Toggles `acat_aktiv` inline for the row (also available on level 0) |

The level name is a live preview link (`phpwcms-preview`) opening the level in the frontend; the folder icon carries a tooltip with level ID, alias, sort value and assigned template.

## Level fields

> Source: `include/inc_tmpl/admin.structform.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_act/act_structure.php` (column mapping to `phpwcms_articlecat`)

The form header shows the parent level the new/edited level belongs to. Buttons: *Update* (submit, stays on the form), *Save and close*, *Cancel*.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| Category title (`acat_name`) | text | — | Menu name, up to 2000 chars, at least one word required. |
| Category alternative title (`acat_title`) | text | — | Alternative name, up to 2000 chars. |
| Alias (`acat_alias`) | text | — | URL alias, up to 1000 chars. Links assemble it from the level name, the parent alias or the level's own alias; `allow_empty_alias` in the configuration decides whether the alias may be empty. |
| OnePage ID (#anchor) support (`acat_onepage`) | switch | 0 | Level name acts as an anchor target in OnePage templates. |
| Language (`acat_lang`, `acat_lang_type`, `acat_lang_id`) | radio + picker | default language | Shown only when more than one backend/frontend language is enabled; links this level to a level (`category`) or article (`article`) ID of the default language. Not available for the index page (which is always default language). |
| Page title (`acat_pagetitle`) | text | — | Overwrites the page `<title>` on frontend pages of this level. |
| CSS class (`acat_class`) | text | — | Class fragment for frontend output; only letters, digits, space, underscore and hyphen survive the save. |
| Redirect to (`acat_redirect`) | text | — | External/global redirect target; empty = no redirect. The frontend redirects 301 to this URL when the level opens. |
| Canonical link (`acat_canonical`) | text | — | Canonical URL emitted for this level. |
| Keywords (`acat_keywords`) | textarea | — | Comma separated list, stored max 255 chars. |
| Category infotext (`acat_info`) | textarea | — | Free text description, up to 32000 chars. |
| Template (`acat_template`) | select | parent level's template | Layout template from `phpwcms_template`; the default template is marked. |
| Settings (`acat_overwrite`) | select | Default | Optional settings file from `template/inc_settings/template_default/*.php` overwriting `conf.template_default.inc.php` values for this level. |
| Pagination (`acat_paginate`) | switch | 0 | Enables article pagination on the level. |
| Topcount (`acat_topcount`) | number | index page value | Number of articles used by listings. |
| Articles per page (`acat_maxlist`) | number | 0 | Pagination batch size. |
| Sort value (`acat_sort`) | number | `(children + 1) * 10` on insert | Manual order of the level inside its parent; not present on the index page form. |
| Ordering of assigned articles (`acat_order` + `acat_ordersort`) | radio groups | stored as sum | Manual (0), date (2), changed date (4), start date (6), kill date (10) or title (8), each combined with ascending (0) or descending (1) — e.g. start date descending = 7. |
| Access group list (`acat_permit`) | dual multi-select | — | Shown only with `usergroup_support`. Groups moved to the left column get level access; writes the group IDs to `acat_permit` and forces "Visible for users logged on only" plus search off. |
| Content part selection (`acat_cntpart`) | dual multi-select | — | Restricts which content part types may be inserted on this level (negative option values select whole [optgroup]s). Empty = all. |
| Default content part (`acat_cpdefault`) | select | global `cp_default` or 0 | Content part type preselected when creating an article here. |
| Cache off (`acat_cacheoff`) + Cache timeout (`acat_timeout`) | switch + select | Default | Timeout in seconds: 60, 300, 900, 1800, 3600, 14400, 43200, 86400, 172800, 604800, 1209600, 2592000; the switch forces 0 = no cache. |
| Search (`acat_nosearch`) | switch (`off`) | off | Turns the search off for pages of this level. |
| Hide (`acat_hidden`) | switch | 0 | Level is hidden from navigation. |
| Visible when active (`acat_hiddenactive`) | switch | 0 | With "Hide": the hidden level still appears when one of its articles is the current page. |
| Visible for users logged on only (`acat_regonly`) | switch | 0 | Requires a frontend login to view articles on this level. |
| Visible (`acat_aktiv`) | switch | `set_category_active` config | Level is active/visible at all. |
| SSL (`acat_ssl`) | switch | 0 | Forces an SSL redirect for this level. |
| Sitemap (`acat_nositemap`) | switch | on for new levels, `index` = default | Includes/excludes the level from the sitemap. |
| Available after end date / archive (`acat_archive`) | switch | 0 | Articles stay listed after their end date once archived. |
| Allow Social Sharing (`acat_opengraph`) | switch | `set_sociallink.articlecat` config | Enables OpenGraph output; the new-level default falls back to 0 when the config is off. |
| Breadcrumb (`acat_breadcrumb_default`, `acat_breadcrumb_nothidden`, `acat_breadcrumb_nolink`) | switches | Default | Bitmask storage: nothidden = 1 (show hidden levels in breadcrumb), nolink = 2 (level breadcrumb entry without link). |

New levels inherit `acat_topcount`, `acat_order` and `acat_cntpart` from the index page configuration; all other fields start from `set_category_active` and safe zero/empty defaults.

### The index page (level 0)

The form opened with `struct=index` edits the `$indexpage` array — name, alternative title, alias, infotext, keywords, page title, template, listing/pagination defaults, order and every switch listed above. Saving does not write a database row; it generates `include/config/conf.indexpage.inc.php` as a flat PHP file instead, so keep the file writable. Language links and the sort value input are absent from this form.

<!-- docs/backend/03-articles.md -->

# Articles

> Source: `include/inc_lib/article.editcontent.inc.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/article.editsummary.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/articlecontent.list.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_lib/article.readform.inc.php`, `include/inc_act/act_articlecontent.php`, `include/inc_act/act_structure.php`, `include/inc_act/act_articlesort.php`

An [article](../general/concepts.md#the-content-hierarchy) is edited in two views, both under `phpwcms.php?do=articles&p=2&s=1&id=<article_id>`:

- the **basis information** form (`aktion=1`) for metadata, summary and list images, and
- the **content part stack** (`aktion` unset), which also opens the content part editor with `aktion=2&acid=<cp_id>`.

Non-admin users see and edit only articles they own (`article_uid` = their account ID); copying an article reassigns ownership to the copying user.

## Basis information form

> Source: `include/inc_tmpl/article.editsummary.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_lib/article.editcontent.inc.php` (POST handling, lines 205-458)

The form has four tabs — Content, Images, Meta data, Settings — and three submit buttons: *Update* (submits and stays, `updatesubmit`), *Save* (submits and closes) and *Cancel*. Cancel compares the serialized form against the initial state and asks for confirmation before leaving unsaved changes. Saving requires the title to be non-empty and keeps `article_tstamp` (the "updated at" stamp) driven by content part changes via `change_articledate()`.

### Content tab

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| Category (`article_cid`) | select | preselected structural level | Destination level of the article; "Home" = level 0. |
| Article title (`article_title`) | text | — | Required, up to 5000 chars; the level name link copies the category name into the field. Side switch hides the title in frontend output (`article_notitle`). |
| Subtitle (`article_subtitle`) | text | — | Up to 5000 chars. |
| Article alias (`article_alias`) | text | generated from title | Up to 1000 chars; buttons propose title-only, parent-path + title or category-path + title aliases; `alias_allow_slash` decides whether `/` or `-` joins the segments. |
| Language (`article_lang`, `article_lang_type`, `article_lang_id`) | select + radio + picker | default language | Shown only with more than one language; links this article to the default-language article (`article`) or level (`category`) whose ID is picked via the article browser. Below the field, sibling translations of the linked article are listed as links. |
| Alias ID (`article_aliasid`) | text | — | Optional numeric ID to reuse another article's alias context; *Use this article's header data* (`article_headerdata`) adopts that article's header information. |
| Summary (`article_summary`) | WYSIWYG | — | Rich text summary used by listings, teasers and RSS; rendered with the user's [WYSIWYG editor](01-overview.md#wysiwyg-editor-settings). |

### Images tab

Two independent images each combine a file picker (`filebrowser.php?opt=0`), size fields and a caption:

| Field | Applies to | Notes |
| ----- | ---------- | ----- |
| Image / max width / max height (`cimage_*`) | article detail | Defaults come from `template_default.article.image_default_*`; a preview thumbnail renders while editing. |
| Enlarge (`cimage_zoom`), Lightbox (`cimage_lightbox`) | article detail | Lightbox force-checks Enlarge. |
| Caption (`cimage_caption`) + suppress switch | article detail | Pipe-separated parts: caption, alt, link plus target, title, copyright. |
| Same as summary image (`cimage_usesummary`) | article listing | Reuses the detail image in lists. |
| Image / size / caption (`cimage_list_*`) | article listing | Independent listing image with its own zoom/lightbox/caption; defaults from `template_default.article.imagelist_default_*`. |

### Meta data tab

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| Page title (`article_pagetitle`) | text | — | Overwrites the frontend `<title>`. |
| Menu title (`article_menutitle`) | text | — | Short title for menus/breadcrumbs. |
| Redirect to (`article_redirect`) | text | — | Sends the frontend visitor to this URL. |
| Canonical link (`article_canonical`) | text | — | Canonical URL for the article. |
| Keywords (`article_keyword`) | tag input | — | Autosuggest over existing categories; stored comma separated and written to the keyword table via `_dbSaveCategories()`. |
| Description (`article_description`) | textarea | — | Meta description. |
| Author (`article_username`) | text | current user name | Free-form author line, up to 200 chars. |
| Robots (`article_meta_noindex`, `article_meta_nofollow`) | switches | 0 | Emits `noindex` / `nofollow`; stored in the `article_meta` JSON column. |
| Created at / Updated at | display | — | Read-only stamps; *Updated at* shows the frozen time when saving without updating the stamp. |

### Settings tab

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| Active (`article_aktiv`) | switch | `set_article_active` config | Publishes the article; also togglable from every list. |
| Start date / Starts (`set_begin` + `article_begin`) | datetime (flatpickr) | off | Scheduled start; checked with seconds precision. Empty or cleared with the checkbox. |
| End date / Ends (`set_end` + `article_end`) | datetime (flatpickr) | off | Scheduled end. |
| Sort value (`article_sort`) | number | 0 | Manual position; drag-drop or arrow sorting rewrites these values. |
| Prioritization (`article_priorize`) | select −30…+30 | 0 | Weight used by teasers ordering. |
| Article listing template (`article_tmpllist`) | select | default | Template from `template/inc_cntpart/articlesummary/list/`. |
| Article detail template (`article_tmplfull`) | select | default | Template from `template/inc_cntpart/articlesummary/article/`. |
| CSS class (`article_meta_class`) | text | — | Class added to frontend output, max 250 chars. |
| Summary: max words (`article_listmaxwords`) | number | — | Truncates the summary shown in listings. |
| Hide summary text (`article_hidesummary`) | checkbox | 0 | Summary block is not output on the detail page. |
| [More…] link (`article_morelink`) | checkbox | 1 | Shows the more link under the summary in listings. |
| No teaser (`article_noteaser`) | checkbox | 0 | Excludes the article from teasers. |
| Paginate articles (`article_paginate`) | checkbox | 0 | Splits content parts into paginated subsections. |
| Article owner (`article_uid`) | select | current user | Settable by admins only; non-admin saves keep their own ownership. |
| Cache off + Cache timeout (`article_cacheoff`, `article_timeout`) | switch + select | Default | Per-article frontend cache timeout; same value list as the struct form. |
| Sitemap (`article_nositemap`) | checkbox | on by default only as level default | Include the article in the sitemap. |
| No search (`article_nosearch`) | checkbox | off | Excludes from backend/frontend search. |
| RSS (`article_norss`) | checkbox | 1 on new articles | RSS feed inclusion. |
| Allow Social Sharing (`article_opengraph`) | checkbox | `set_sociallink.article` config | OpenGraph tags for this article. |
| Available after end date (archive) (`article_archive`) | checkbox | 1 on new articles | Article stays listed after its end date when archived. |

## Content part stack

> Source: `include/inc_tmpl/articlecontent.list.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_act/act_articlecontent.php`, `include/inc_act/act_structure.php`, `include/inc_act/act_articlesort.php`

The stack view shows article metadata (alias, category, keywords, flags, dates, owner), then one card per template block — CONTENT (main, paginated when the article paginates), LEFT, RIGHT, HEADER, FOOTER, CPSET and SYSTEM ("no render" containers) — with content parts ordered inside each block.

### Managing content parts

| Action | How | Notes |
| ------ | --- | ----- |
| Add | Type drop-down (new content part) button | The drop-down lists the level's allowed types (`acat_cntpart`), further restricted by the user's `wcs_allowed_cp`; submitting with `ctype` opens the new part's editor. |
| Edit | Pencil on the row | `aktion=2&acid=<id>`; type may be changed to another type/module, which merges the stored values through the target type's readform. |
| Copy within article | Copy icon on the row | `act_structure.php?do=8|<cp>|<aid>|<sort>`; asks for confirmation, inserts the duplicate after the source at `sorting + 5`. |
| Move to another article | Cut/copy in one article → paste arrow on the target article row in the structure tree | `do=7` (move, reindexes both stacks) / `do=8` (copy) in `act_structure.php`. |
| Sort | Drag with the grip handle, or chevron up/down links | Drag posts the complete new order to `act_articlesort.php`; arrows swap neighbor values via `act_articlecontent.php?sort=` and never cross block boundaries. |
| Show/hide | Eye icon | Toggles `acontent_visible` (also on the dashboard's content part list). |
| Delete | Trash icon | Sets `acontent_trash = 9` after a confirmation dialog. Ownership: a part is deletable/toggleable by its owner or an admin. |
| Preview | Button above the header | Opens the article in the frontend with the `phpwcms-preview` flag in a dedicated window. |

Each row shows the content part label, ID badge, last edit date, the block-paginate page number when pagination is on, and a per-type summary rendered by `include/inc_tmpl/content/cnt<N>.list.inc.php`.

Every save through the content part editor touches `article_tstamp`, clears the frontend cache and marks referenced files as in-use for the file center traffic light (`phpwcms_mark_content_files_used()`).

## Revisions

There is no per-article revision history in 2.x. The `include/inc_lib/revision/` directory holds database migration scripts (`r401.php` …) executed automatically at login by `phpwcms_get_available_revisions()` — they upgrade the installation schema, not article content.

## Related

- [Structure tree](02-structure-tree.md)
- [Content parts reference](../content-parts/01-text-with-image.md)

# Files — file center

> Source: `include/inc_tmpl/files.reiter.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_lib/files.private-functions.inc.php`, `include/inc_lib/files.public-functions.inc.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/files.private.*.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_act/act_file.php`, `include/inc_act/act_download.php`, `include/inc_act/act_multiupload.php`

The **Files** section (`phpwcms.php?do=files`) organizes everything a site uploads. Folders and files are rows of the `phpwcms_file` table (`f_kid = 0` = folder, `f_kid = 1` = file), not filesystem directories; binaries live on disk under the configured `file_path`, stored under an MD5 hash name. The file center nav shows three entries, each behind its own permission: File center (`filecent`), File actions (`fileaction`, `p=4`), Multiple file upload (`fileupload`, `p=8`).

## Tabs

> Source: `include/inc_tmpl/files.reiter.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/files.private.trash.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/files.search.tmpl.php`

| Tab | URL | Content |
| --- | --- | ------- |
| Private files | `f=0` | Your own folder tree and files; admins see all users' files, others only `f_uid =` their own ID. Upload, new folder, editfile and editdir forms replace the list while open. |
| Public files | `f=1` | Read-only listing of all files with `f_public = 1` and `f_aktiv = 1`; a user drop-down filters by owner. |
| Search | `f=3` | Full-text search over file name, description and tags across the private area. |
| Trash can | `f=2` | Files moved to trash (`f_trash = 9`), restorable from here. |

The toolbar above the tabs is per-tab: upload and new-folder buttons on the private tab, expand/collapse-all, thumbnail on/off (stored per user in `wcs_user_thumb`), and a help dialog listing every icon. A cut file changes the new-folder button into a paste button.

## Folders and files

> Source: `include/inc_lib/files.private-functions.inc.php` (`list_private()`), `include/inc_act/act_file.php`

Folders and files offer:

| Control | On folders | On files |
| ------- | ---------- | -------- |
| Edit (pencil) | Folder name/description form (`editdir`) | File detail form (`editfile`) |
| More actions | Upload into folder, new subfolder, paste (when cut is active), delete when empty | Download (`act_download.php?dl=<id>`), cut/paste between folders, move to trash when not in use |
| Eye icon | Toggles `f_aktiv` | Toggles `f_aktiv` |
| Lock icon | Toggles `f_public` | Toggles `f_public` |

Only the owner or an admin may move a file to trash (`act_file.php?trash=`), which flags the row `f_trash` — the binary stays on disk until an admin runs *Move deleted files* (admin or `filedelete` permission): with `trash_delete_files` off it moves the binaries to `filearchive/can_be_deleted/`, with it on the files are physically unlinked.

The colored dot next to every file is the usage indicator from `files.private-usage.inc.php`: red = currently referenced by content (articles, or calendar/glossary/shop module data), not deletable; yellow = uploaded less than 24 hours ago and not yet used; green = unused and 24 hours or older; black = was referenced before but is no longer. The same status appears in file detail and disables the trash action while content uses the file.

## Upload

> Source: `include/inc_tmpl/files.private.upload.tmpl.php`

The single-file upload form (`f=0&upload=0` or `&upload=<folder_id>`) posts one file plus metadata:

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| Directory (`file_pid`) | select | root | Target folder. |
| File (`file`) | file | — | One file per submit; client-side size check against the effective max (PHP `upload_max_filesize` / `post_max_size` / `file_maxsize`, lowest wins), plus the `file_maxsize` config limit of 52428800 bytes (50 MB). |
| Use IPTC data as caption (`file_iptc_as_caption`) | checkbox | `iptc_as_caption` config | Fills title, description, copyright and alt from the image IPTC block; tags preview shows below the field while a file is selected (via `exif.min.js`). |
| Title / Description / Copyright / Alt | text | — | One set per active language when `allowed_lang` holds more than one (`f_vars` per-language storage); IPTC fallback fills every language when `iptc_as_caption_all_lang` is set. |
| Keywords (`file_keywords`) | selects | — | Predefined file categories/keys from `phpwcms_filecat` / `phpwcms_filekey`; "needed" categories must select a value. |
| Additional info (`file_shortinfo`) | text | — | Short line, max 750 chars. |
| Tags (`file_tags`) | tag input | — | Autosuggest over existing file tags; saved into the tag table. |
| Sorting (`file_sort`) | number | 0 | Order inside the folder, before `f_name`. |
| Active (`file_aktiv`) | switch | `set_file_active` config | File is visible in listings. |
| Granted download (`file_granted`) | switch | 0 | See download protection below. |
| Public (`file_public`) | switch | `set_file_active` config | File appears in the public tab / public listing. |
| Gallery download (`file_gallerydownload`) | switch | 0 | Marks the file for gallery download handling. |

Forbidden names (`.htaccess`, `web.config`, `lighttpd.conf`, `nginx.conf`, leading dot) and non-whitelisted extensions (`allowed_upload_ext`) are rejected; SVG dimensions are read by an SVG metadata parser.

## Multiple file upload and FTP takeover

> Source: `include/inc_tmpl/files.ftptakeover.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_act/act_multiupload.php`, `include/inc_act/act_ftptakeover.php`

`do=files&p=8` combines two import paths in one page:

1. **Dropzone multi-upload** — drag-and-drop many files at once into the configured folder; each file becomes a normal file row (`f_aktiv = 1`, `f_public = 1`).
2. **FTP takeover** — lists files found in the configured `ftp_path` directory on the server; checkboxes select them, and a form applies directory (or a new folder), keywords, metadata and status switches to every marked file before it is imported into the file center.

## File detail

> Source: `include/inc_tmpl/files.private.editfile.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_lib/files.private-usage.inc.php`

The file edit form shows ID, hash, size, extension, image width/height in pixels, creation date and the usage indicator, plus all fields of the upload form. Editing notes:

- The file name may change; a missing extension is appended automatically. Renaming the alias deletes cached derived images in `content/images/` that used the old alias.
- The binary itself is not replaceable through this form — the hash never changes; replace a file by uploading a new one and updating references.
- IPTC data of the stored image is listed and can be applied as title/description/copyright/alt with one checkbox.

## Download protection

> Source: `include/inc_act/act_download.php`

Backend downloads always pass through `include/inc_act/act_download.php`. Without it the physical file stays in `filearchive/` under its hash name. Access rules:

| File state | Who can download |
| ---------- | ---------------- |
| `f_public = 0` (`private`) | Owner and admins only |
| `f_public = 1`, `f_aktiv = 1` | Any authenticated backend user; with `pl` parameter also frontend flows |

`f_granted` ("Secured frontend download only") marks a file that frontend file resolution (`_getFileInfo()`) skips for visitors without a frontend login — such files resolve and download only while a frontend user is logged in. Backend downloads always pass through `include/inc_act/act_download.php` and stay reachable for the owner and admins regardless:

| File state | Who can download from the backend |
| ---------- | --------------------------------- |
| Listed from the private tree (`dl` without `pl`) | Owner and admins only |
| Listed from the public tab (`dl` + `pl`) | Any backend user for `f_public = 1` files; own files in any state |

## File actions

> Source: `include/inc_tmpl/files.actions.tmpl.php`

The bulk page (`p=4`, permission `fileaction`) works on one selected folder: it lists the files with checkboxes and applies one action to all marked files — delete to trash, move to another folder, set active/public status, or reassign owner (admin use). Below it, an *unused files* search lists files with no content references; their trash action stays disabled while the usage check still reports references.

<!-- docs/backend/05-messaging.md -->

# Messaging

> Source: `phpwcms.php` (do=messages dispatch), `include/inc_lib/checkmessage.inc.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/message.subscription.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/newsletter.list.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/message.subscribers.tmpl.php`

The sidebar item is labeled **Communication** (`be_nav_messages`). It appears only when `enable_backend_newsletter` is on in the configuration and the user belongs to the `nl` group; each of its three pages is additionally gated by the group members listed below. Opening any of these pages with the newsletter module disabled silently renders the dashboard instead.

The page dispatch additionally requires super admin rights (`usr_admin = 1`) — group membership decides visibility in the menu, but only admins see the pages themselves.

## Pages

| Page | URL | Group | Content |
| ---- | --- | ----- | ------- |
| Newsletter subscriptions | `do=messages&p=2` | `nlabo` | List of subscription lists with recipient counts; create, edit and delete lists (system lists refuse deletion). |
| Newsletter | `do=messages&p=3` | `nllist` | Overview of newsletter issues with publication date, last sending and total/queued/sent/opened recipient counts; create and edit issues, and start sending (`&send=1`, `newsletter.send.tmpl.php`) for issues that have a queue. |
| Newsletter subscribers | `do=messages&p=4` | `nlrecip` | Subscriber list; CSV import (`&import=1`, via `subscriberimport.form.tmpl.php` and a result page) and export (`include/inc_act/act_export.php?action=exportsubscriber`). |

The older *Message center* and *New message* pages (`p=0` / `p=1`, `message.center.tmpl.php`, `message.send.tmpl.php`) are commented out in `phpwcms.php` — internal messaging between backend accounts is currently not reachable through the navigation.

## Unread-message indicator

`include/inc_lib/checkmessage.inc.php` counts rows in `phpwcms_message` with `msg_read = 0` for the signed-in user and, when any exist, appends an envelope icon to the Communication nav entry. The counter renders on every backend page load; there is no message reading view behind it in the current dispatch.

## Form results

There is no backend view collecting frontend form submissions. The formmail [content part](../general/concepts.md#the-content-hierarchy) shows only its target/label summary in the content part stack (`include/inc_tmpl/content/cnt10.list.inc.php`); submitted data goes straight into the configured emails. For subscriber-driven mailings, use the newsletter pages above.

<!-- docs/backend/06-profile.md -->

# Profile

> Source: `include/inc_tmpl/profile.account.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_lib/profile.updateaccount.inc.php`, `phpwcms.php` (do=profile dispatch)

The profile page (`phpwcms.php?do=profile`) is reached from the user icon in the header; it shows only when the user belongs to the `profile` SYSGROUP. Super admins are seeded into every SYSGROUP when the group does not exist yet, but can be removed from the group afterwards — in that case the header link disappears. The page exists in two variants: backend accounts and frontend accounts render the same form — the icon differs (`fa-user-shield` for admins, `fa-user-check` for frontend users, `fa-user` / `fa-user-cog` in between).

Saving requires the account not to be the `guest` login; changed values are written to `phpwcms_user` and mirrored into the session.

## Account card

> Source: `include/inc_tmpl/profile.account.tmpl.php`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| Username (`form_loginname`) | text | current login | Unique check runs before saving; a taken name aborts the update. |
| New password / Repeat (`form_password`, `form_password2`) | password | empty | Both must match; empty leaves the password unchanged; minimum length 5 characters. Show/hide toggle per field. |
| Email (`form_useremail`) | text | current email | Validated; on change a notification is sent to the old address, and a password change triggers a confirmation email to the account address, both rendered from the system email templates. |
| Language (`form_lang`) | select | current backend language | Backend UI language, one entry per `include/inc_lang/backend/<lang>/lang.inc.php`; legacy directory aliases (`cz`, `se`, `vn`, `el`) are mapped to their ISO codes and an invalid value falls back to the default language or `en`. Also sets the `phpwcmsBELang` cookie. |
| Theme (`form_theme`) | select | auto | Backend theme: auto (follows system scheme), light, dark. Writes the session value and the `phpwcmsBETheme` cookie; see [Backend overview](01-overview.md#theme-switching). |
| WYSIWYG (`form_wysiwyg`) | select | inactive | 0 = textarea, 1 = CKEditor (labeled legacy), 2 = TinyMCE 8 (labeled default); see the [backend overview](01-overview.md#wysiwyg-editor-settings). |
| Content parts (`profile_account_cp[]`) | checkbox grid | all checked | Selects which content part types the editor offers when adding parts to an article (`wcs_user_cp`); types blocked by the account's `allowed_cp` list render disabled and cannot be checked. |

## Two-factor authentication card

A second card manages TOTP 2FA for the account:

- **Enable**: the page generates a pending secret (session `pending_2fa_secret`), shows its QR code and `otpauth://` URL, and activates after a 6-digit code from the authenticator app is confirmed. On success, eight single-use backup recovery codes are displayed once and stored hashed in `usr_vars`.
- **Disable**: requires the current password; clears the secret and backup codes.

Both actions post `form_aktion` = `enable_2fa` / `disable_2fa`, handled by `profile.updateaccount.inc.php` in the same `do=profile` dispatch.

## Data storage

| Value | Stored in |
| ----- | --------- |
| Login name, password, email | `phpwcms_user` (`usr_login`, `usr_pass` bcrypt-hashed, `usr_email`) |
| Backend language | `usr_lang` plus the `phpwcmsBELang` cookie |
| Theme and WYSIWYG choice | `usr_vars` (serialized `theme`); WYSIWYG additionally in the `usr_wysiwyg` column and session `WYSIWYG_EDITOR` |
| Selected content parts | `usr_vars` (serialized `selected_cp`), kept in `wcs_user_cp` |
| 2FA state | `usr_2fa_enabled`, `usr_2fa_secret`, backup codes in `usr_vars` (`2fa_backup_codes`) |

The profile form does not change group memberships, admin flags or [structure-level](02-structure-tree.md) permissions — those belong to the [user administration](../administration/users-usergroups.md).

---

<!-- docs/frontend/page-rendering.md -->

# Page rendering

> Source: `index.php`, `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php`, `include/inc_front/content.article.inc.php`, `include/inc_front/content/*.article.inc.php`

Every frontend request runs `index.php` top to bottom. `content.func.inc.php` does the URL resolution, article rendering and tag replacement; `index.php` assembles the final HTML and emits it. The order below is the actual execution order.

## 1. Bootstrap

1. `index.php` loads `include/config/conf.inc.php`, `default.inc.php`, `helper.session.php`, `dbcon.inc.php`.
2. When `content/tmp/update/maintenance.flag` is fresh (< 15 minutes), a 503 maintenance page renders instead.
3. `$IS_A_BOT` decides whether a session initializes (`SESSION_FEinit` or preview request). `cleanupPOSTandGET()` and `buildGlobalGET()` fill `$GLOBALS['_getVar']`; `FE_CURRENT_URL` captures the full URL; `init_frontend_edit()` prepares backend edit links.
4. `ob_start()` buffers the whole render; the config defaults and language files load (`conf.template_default.inc.php`, `conf.indexpage.inc.php`, `cnt.lang.inc.php`, `modules.check.inc.php`, `article.contenttype.inc.php`, `imagick.convert.inc.php`, `front.func.inc.php`, `ext.func.inc.php`), then `content.func.inc.php` runs.
5. Search engine referrers log into `log_seo` when `enable_seolog` is on.

## 2. Request mode

- `$_POST` requests disable the 301 forcing (see [URL handling](../general/url-handling.md)).
- `?phpwcms-preview` enters preview mode: it disables forcing, requires a backend login (otherwise redirects to the site root) and defines `PREVIEW_MODE`, which lifts the article `begin`/`end` time checks.
- `?print=1` selects the HTML print template, `?print=2` the PDF template (`PRINT_PDF`, requires `$phpwcms['wkhtmltopdf_path']`).
- `?phpwcms_output_action=F-filter1|filter2--S-SECTION1|SECTION2` requests a trimmed fragment of defined template sections instead of a full page; handled at the very end of `index.php`.

## 3. URL resolution

`$aktion` is the six-slot array `[<level-id>, <article-id>, <print>, <level-mode>, <show-article>, 0]`:

| URL form | Resolution |
| -------- | ---------- |
| `index.php?id=<cat>[,<aid>…]` | Legacy combined form; validates the level, else 404; a comma separates level and article |
| `index.php?aid=<id>-<cppage>` | Resolves the article's level via a DB lookup; `-<n>` selects the content part pagination page |
| `index.php?<alias>` | Single UNION query against `articlecat.acat_alias` first, then `article.article_alias`; the first empty-valued GET key in `_getVar` is the alias |

Alias based URLs define `PHPWCMS_ALIAS`; the constant also covers `id=`/`aid=` forms later when no alias resolves.

## 4. 404 and redirects

When the requested level, article or alias does not exist, `$content['404error']` fills:

1. Requests arriving with alias `r404` or `REDIRECT_STATUS == 404` retry the original `REDIRECT_URL` as alias once more.
2. The failing combination (id/aid/alias) queries the `redirect` table — an active entry issues a redirect (codes 301, 302, 307, 401, 404, 503, default 302; types `home`, `alias`, `id`, `aid`, `link`) and bumps its view counter.
3. Without a matching entry, `$phpwcms['log_404error']` inserts a new record.
4. Otherwise `headerRedirect('', 404)` emits the 404 status — and the active template's error block (`[404]…[/404]`) renders on that attempt.

Structure level redirects (`acat_redirect`) and SSL forcing (`site_ssl_mode`, `acat_ssl`) 301 before any content renders.

## 5. Permissions and template choice

`get_breadcrumb()` builds `$LEVEL_ID`, `$LEVEL_KEY`; a `regonly` level anywhere on the path sets `PERMIT_ACCESS = FALSE`. `_checkFrontendUserAutoLogin()` runs, and unauthorized visitors redirect with HTTP 401 to the configured login URL (`feloginurl` template override or `$template_default['login_form_url']`).

The [template fallback chain](../templates/template-system.md#which-layout-template-is-used) then selects `$block`, the page layout follows (missing pagelayout aborts with an admin hint), and `template/inc_settings/template_default/` overrides apply. `js.inc.php` loads next.

## 6. Content assembly

`frontend_init` scripts include (see [frontend scripts](frontend-scripts.md)), then one of two branches runs:

- **Article list mode** (no article requested, more than one article, or `topcount = -1`): `list_articles_summary()` (in `front.func.inc.php`) renders the list into `$content['main']` through `article_summary_list.tmpl`.
- **Article mode**: `content.article.inc.php` loads the article row (visible-mode aware), resolves alias articles, builds article redirects (301, meta refresh or JavaScript window handling), canonical, pagetitle, description, summary image with [the summary template chain](../templates/template-system.md#which-content-part-template-is-used), then loops all visible content parts in sort order: each renderer `include/inc_front/content/cnt<N>.article.inc.php` appends to `$content['main']` (or a named block in `$content['CB']`), tab and content-part-group content collects into `$content['cptab']`.

A category holding exactly one article shows the article directly and sets `$content['set_canonical']`; `force301_2struct` may 301 the request to the level alias first.

## 7. Layout assembly

- Normal mode (`layout_render` 0/1/2 of the [page layout](../templates/template-editor.md#page-layout-editor-p8)): table markup (`get_table_block()`), div markup, or the raw `maintext` — the custom mode.
- Print/PDF mode: `template/inc_default/print.tmpl` or `pdf.tmpl` wraps the maintext.

`{CONTENT}` is replaced, custom blocks render with `[BLOCK]`/`[BLOCK_ELSE]`, content part tab placeholders `<!-- <tabid> -->` fill, list-mode sections resolve, and `render_device()` applies its first pass.

## Replacement cascade

The assembled page then runs the replacements in exactly this order through `content.func.inc.php`:

1. `{CURRENT_ARTICLEID}`, `{CURRENT_CATEGORYID}`, `[LEVEL<n>_ID]`/`{LEVEL<n>_ID}`
2. `[IF_CAT:…]`, `[IF_NOTCAT:…]` condition blocks
3. `{SHOW_CONTENT:…}` content pulling
4. `{SITE}`, `{TEMPLATE}`, `render_PHPcode()` (PHP tags with `enable_inline_php`)
5. `{BREADCRUMB…}`
6. `{NAV_LIST_UL:…}`
7. Deprecated navigation and `{RANDOM}`-family tags (`enable_deprecated`)
8. `{DATE_*}`, `{TIME_*}` fixed date/time tags
9. Search form markers `###search_input_…###`
10. `{RELATED:…}` keyword related articles, `{NEW:…}` newest articles
11. `{RSSIMG}`
12. `{KEYWORD:…}`
13. `{URL:…}` external page include
14. `{BROWSE:UP/NEXT/PREV…}`
15. `html_parser()` pass (BB codes, `[img]`, `[mail]`, links, line breaks) unless `parse_html_mode` says `after` — including the `$content['globalRT']` custom tags
16. Redirect code into htmlhead; `PHPWCMS_ALIAS` definition
17. **frontend_render scripts** and module render scripts run here
18. Optional second `html_parser()` pass
19. `render_device()` second pass, PHP re-render, `{LAZY_LOADING}`
20. Frontend edit links and CSS
21. Meta description/keywords insertion
22. Open Graph and Twitter/X card meta rendering (`set_sociallink` config)
23. `generator` meta — unless disabled or whitelabeled
24. `[PRINT]`/`[PRINT_PDF]` link wrappers
25. Article context tags: `{AUTHOR}`, date tags (`render_cnt_date()` → `{DATE:…}`, `{NOW:…}`, `{LIVEDATE:…}`, `{KILLDATE:…}`), `{CATEGORY}`
26. `{SOCIAL_SHARE…}`
27. `<!-- JS: … -->` and `<!-- CSS: … -->` head comments; `frontend.js` legacy detection
28. Article/level onload handling (DomReady, Unload, inline scripts)
29. Search highlight wrapper (`?highlight=` words over `<!--SEARCH_HIGHLIGHT_START//-->…<!--SEARCH_HIGHLIGHT_END//-->` sections)
30. Content part pagination: `{CP_PAGINATE}`, `[CP_PAGINATE_PREV]/[NEXT]`, `[CP_PAGINATE_MENU]`, `link rel="prev"/"next"`
31. `[NO_PRINT]` stripping in print mode, `[LOGGED_IN]/[LOGGED_OUT]` sections
32. `[HTML]…[/HTML]` and `[HTML_SPECIAL]…[/HTML_SPECIAL]`, CKEditor resized image post-processing, XHTML Strict attribute cleanup
33. Cookie consent v3 or v2 script injection, GA/GTM/Matomo tracking code, pixel-ratio detector
34. `custom_htmlhead` flush into `<head>` (or shifted above `</body>` with `js_in_body`)
35. `index.php?aid=/id=` links rewritten to their aliases where they exist
36. `[LANG:…]`/`[<lang>]…[/</lang>]` blocks and `@@…@@` tokens (i18n)
37. `{GT:…}` spans (deprecated, `gt_mod`)
38. Legacy `image_resized.php` img tags migrated to the `cmsimage` schema
39. `download.php?f=` rewritten to `dl/` when rewriting is on; image extensions forced to `.webp` when `webp_enable` fits the client

## Final HTML assembly

`index.php` continues:

1. `page_start` builds the doctype (`PHPWCMS_DOCTYPE` per `mode_XHTML`), charset, viewport (`$phpwcms['viewport']`), `<base>` (`base_href`), `<title>` from `$content['pagetitle']`, the deprecated page-layout CSS attributes, the template CSS `<link>` files and `$block['htmlhead']`, closes `</head>`, opens `<body>` with the configured id/class plus `$content['body_id']`.
2. With rewriting on, `url_search()` rewrites remaining `href="index.php?…"` and `onclick` URLs to `/<value><rewrite_ext>…` forms, and the `img/cmsimage.php` prefix shrinks to `im`.
3. `page_end` appends `$block['bodyjs']`, the optional browser-update.org script and `</body></html>`.
4. `render_clean_html` strips HTML comments when enabled.

Output: the buffered page flushes. `cache_timeout` (config, level `acat_timeout` or article `article_cache`) drives `Expires`, `Last-Modified` and `Cache-Control` response headers; per-level caching beyond headers is not implemented in the current frontend — the config key `cache_enabled` exists but the page pipeline no longer reads it. File based caches do exist for resized images, feeds and `{URL}` includes (`check_cache()`).

Finally `X-phpwcms-Release` and the processing-time header emit (unless disabled or whitelabeled), PDF requests route through `include/inc_front/pdf.inc.php`, `phpwcms_output_action` requests return only the requested, filtered sections, and `ob_end_flush()` ships the page.

## Related

- [Frontend scripts](frontend-scripts.md)
- [Replacement tags](replacement-tags/01-nav-list-ul.md)
- [Layout tags](../templates/layout-tags.md)

<!-- docs/frontend/frontend-scripts.md -->

# Frontend scripts

> Source: `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php` (include loops), `include/inc_lib/general.inc.php` (`get_tmpl_files()`), `include/inc_module/*/frontend.init.php`, `include/inc_module/*/frontend.render.php`

Two hook directories let you run own PHP inside every page render without touching core files:

| Directory | Runs | Gate |
| --------- | ---- | ---- |
| `template/inc_script/frontend_init/` | early — after template and page layout load, before article rendering | `$phpwcms['allow_ext_init']` (default 1) |
| `template/inc_script/frontend_render/` | after the replacement cascade, before the final `render_device()` pass | `$phpwcms['allow_ext_render']` (default 1) |

Both loops use `get_tmpl_files()` to collect all `*.php` files in the directory and `include_once` them in alphabetical order. Subdirectories are ignored, which is why the shipped examples live in a `disabled/` folder — move a sample up one level to activate it. Each directory carries an `.htaccess` (`Deny from all`) to block direct HTTP access.

## What init scripts can do

At init time you have the full setup: `$phpwcms`, `$content['struct']`, the level breadcrumb in `$LEVEL_ID`/`$LEVEL_KEY`, `$block` (template settings), `$pagelayout` and `$template_default`. No page markup exists yet. Typical uses:

- **Redirection or language handling** — `lang_redirect.php`, `domaincheck.php` ship as examples.
- **Body ID injection** — `$content['body_id']` (see `frontend_init/disabled/inject_body_id.php`):
  ```php
  if (isset($LEVEL_ID[1])) {
      $content['body_id'] = $LEVEL_ID[1];
  }
  ```
- **Frontend user context** — `felogin.init.php` wires the ini based fe-login.

Content part trigger functions registered here run for every rendered content part (see registration patterns below).

## What render scripts can do

Render scripts receive the almost finished page in `$content['all']` and modify it in place:

```php
$content['all'] = str_replace('{MYTAG}', 'value', $content['all']);
```

They also run before the final device pass and the meta/OpenGraph insertion, so tags they write get processed by the remaining cascade (`render_device()`, `render_PHPcode()`, alias link rewriting).

## Content part triggers

A render or init script may register a callback that each content part passes through after rendering:

```php
function CP_CreateDate($text, $data) {
    $change_date = strtotime($data['acontent_created']);
    return str_replace('{CPDATE}', international_date_format('DE', 'd.m.Y', $change_date), $text);
}
register_cp_trigger('CP_CreateDate');
```

`trigger_cp()` calls every registered function with the content part markup and its database row — handy for tokens like `{CPDATE}` that need the CP record.

## Module provided scripts

Modules register hook scripts declaratively in their `module.default.php` and `include/inc_lib/modules.check.inc.php` collects them for active modules into `$phpwcms['modules_fe_init']` and `$phpwcms['modules_fe_render']`:

```php
$_module_fe_render = true;   // registers include/inc_module/<mod>/frontend.render.php
$_module_fe_init   = true;   // registers include/inc_module/<mod>/frontend.init.php
```

Both arrays include right after the template directory equivalents. The glossary module ships `frontend.render.php` — a concise example: it checks `isset($content['glossary'])`, defines `replace_glossary_tag()` and rewrites page markup matching `\[glossary <keyword>]…\[/glossary]` into `<abbr class="glossary" title="…">` elements, looking the keyword up in the glossary table and caching results in `$content['glossary_cache']`. Module render scripts follow the same rules and globals as `template/inc_script/frontend_render/` scripts.

## Globals cheat sheet

| Variable | Available in | Typical use |
| -------- | ------------ | ----------- |
| `$phpwcms` | both | configuration values, `USER_AGENT` |
| `$content` | both | `struct`, `main`, `all` (render only), `CB`, `articles`, `opengraph` |
| `$template_default` | both | classes, attributes, settings arrays |
| `$block` | both | template settings, `custom_htmlhead`, `js_ondomready` |
| `$pagelayout` | both | page layout values |
| `$content['globalRT']` | render | register replacement tags replaced in the final `html_parser()` pass |

Head building helpers from `front.func.inc.php`/`js.inc.php` work in both layers: `set_meta()`, `inlineJS()`, `jsOnDomReady()`, `initJSLib()` or direct `$block['custom_htmlhead']` entries (keys prefixed `head_` always stay in the head even with `js_in_body` on).

## Security notes

- Every script must check `PHPWCMS_ROOT` at its top:
  ```php
  if (!defined('PHPWCMS_ROOT')) {
      die('You Cannot Access This Script Directly, Have a Nice Day.');
  }
  ```
- Only files with a `.php` extension load; anything else in the directory is data for you, not code.
- Both layers are off when their config gate is 0 — a hardened public install can run pure frontend logic without them.
- Scripts execute in full request context: they can read the session and redirect responses. Treat the directories as code deployment, not media storage.

## Related

- [Page rendering](page-rendering.md) — where the layers sit in the pipeline
- [Layout tags](../templates/layout-tags.md)

<!-- docs/frontend/deprecated-tags.md -->

# Deprecated tags

> Source: `include/inc_front/deprecated.inc.php`, `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php` (deprecated branch), `include/config/dist.conf.inc.php` (`enable_deprecated`, `gt_mod`)

The tags on this page survive only behind the compatibility switch:

```php
$phpwcms['enable_deprecated'] = true; // config.inc.php
```

With the switch off, `content.func.inc.php` skips the whole deprecated branch and never loads `deprecated.inc.php` — every tag below stays unrendered in the page source. Do not use these tags in new templates; the maintained equivalents live under [NAV_LIST_UL](replacement-tags/01-nav-list-ul.md).

## Navigation tags

| Tag | Syntax | Renders by |
| --- | ------ | ---------- |
| Row navigation | `{NAV_ROW}` | `nav_level_row(0)` — all levels of the level tree, `|` separated from `template_default['nav_row']` settings |
| Row navigation variant | `{NAV_ROW:<start-id-or-CURRENT>:<show-home>}` | Same renderer, `show_home` = 0/1 |
| Level list | `{NAV_LIST}` | Normalized to `{NAV_LIST:0}` |
| Level list variant | `{NAV_LIST:<top-level>:<class>}` | `nav_list_struct()` — nested `<ul>` list with `listActive<depth>` classes |
| Top level list | `{NAV_LIST_TOP}`, `{NAV_LIST_TOP:<home-label>:<class>}` | `css_level_list()` with parent level on |
| Current level list | `{NAV_LIST_CURRENT}`, `{NAV_LIST_CURRENT:<level>:<back-label>:<class>}` | `css_level_list()` scoped to the current level, default class `list_level` |
| Simple table nav | `{NAV_TABLE_SIMPLE}` | `nav_table_simple_struct()` — one-column `<table>` of all levels |
| Table nav | `{NAV_TABLE_COLUMN}`, `{NAV_TABLE_COLUMN:<level>}` | `nav_table_struct()` — table navigation honoring the `template_default['nav_table_struct']` defaults, loads `frontend.js` |

These renderers use the legacy `$content['cat_path']` breadcrumb and the `nav_row` / `nav_table_struct` option blocks in `include/config/conf.template_default.inc.php`.

## Image placeholders

`html_parser_deprecated()` rewrites markup style placeholders of the 1.x era:

| Tag | Result |
| --- | ------ |
| `{RANDOM:path}` | ` <img>` of a random image found under `path` (`.gif`, `.jpeg`, `.jpg`, `.png`); `{RANDOM:SRC:path}` returns only the absolute image URL |
| `{RANDOM_GIF:path}` | `<img src="img/random_image.php?type=0&amp;imgdir=path">` |
| `{RANDOM_JPEG:path}` | Same with `type=1` |
| `{RANDOM_PNG:path}` | Same with `type=2` |
| `{IMAGE:file}` | `<img src="picture/file">` |
| `{IMAGE_LEFT:file}` | Same, floated left |
| `{IMAGE_RIGHT:file}` | Same, floated right |
| `{IMAGE_CENTER:file}` | Same inside a centered `<div>` |

## Style tag

`{GT:<style>}…{/GT}` wraps its content in `<span class="gt-<style>">`. It has its own gate and renders when `$phpwcms['gt_mod']` is on, independent of `enable_deprecated`.

## Related legacy behavior

Not gated by `enable_deprecated`, but rewritten unconditionally in the final cascade: old `<img src="image_resized.php?...">` markup converts to the `img/cmsimage.php` (or `im/`) schema. Keep that in mind when re-cutting old 1.x markup.

## Related

- [Page rendering](page-rendering.md#replacement-cascade) — where the deprecated branch runs
- [NAV_LIST_UL](replacement-tags/01-nav-list-ul.md)

<!-- docs/frontend/rss-feeds.md -->

# RSS feeds

> Source: `feeds.php`, `rss.php`, `include/config/feeds.ini.php`, `include/inc_front/content/cnt22.article.inc.php`

phpwcms produces site feeds and consumes external ones. Two directions, two mechanisms:

| Direction | Mechanism |
| --------- | --------- |
| Publish site articles | `feeds.php` builds a feed from the article table |
| Consume external feeds | Content part 22 (RSS feed) renders a feed URL inside a page; the Feedimport [module](../general/concepts.md#modules) imports feeds into articles |

## feeds.php

`feeds.php` loads the feed definitions from `include/config/feeds.ini.php` (a PHP-guarded INI file — keep the first line intact) and renders with the bundled `UniversalFeedCreator`. When the INI file holds no usable entries a built-in `default` feed applies.

Request parameters:

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --------- | ------- |
| `?feed=<name>` | Uses the `[<name>]` INI section; when unknown, the value acts as `structureID` on the default feed |
| `?format=<FORMAT>` | Overrides `defaultFormat`; valid: `0.91`/`RSS0.91`, `1.0`/`RSS1.0`, `2.0`/`RSS2.0`, `ATOM`/`ATOM1.0`, `ATOM0.3` |

The rendered feed caches into `content/rss/<format>-<filename>` for `cacheTTL` seconds via `useCached()`, then `saveFeed()` emits it. When `structureID` sits in the query (unknown `feed=` value), the filename becomes `<structureIDs>.xml`.

## Feed configuration

> Source: `include/config/feeds.ini.php`

| Field | Default | Description |
| ----- | ------- | ----------- |
| `title` | `Daily RSS feed` | Feed title |
| `description` | empty | Feed description |
| `link` | auto `PHPWCMS_URL` | Feed home link |
| `syndicationURL` | empty, then SELF | Canonical feed URL |
| `imagesrc`, `imagetitle`, `imagelink`, `imagedescription` | empty | Optional feed image |
| `useauthor` | 1 | Render per-item author tags |
| `feedAuthor`, `feedEmail` | editor strings | Author fallback (ATOM always needs one) |
| `timeZone` | `+01:00` | Timezone offset, empty = GMT |
| `cacheTTL` | 3600 | Feed file cache seconds, 0 disables caching |
| `structureID` | empty (all) | Structure level IDs or aliases, comma separated; the site root alias resolves to level 0 when the root is public |
| `maxentries` | 10 | Article limit |
| `encoding` | `UTF-8` | Output charset |
| `defaultFormat` | `RSS2.0` | Format when no `format=` GET value |
| `filename` | `default_feed.xml` (or md5 of name+title) | Cache file name |
| `orderBy` | `livedate` | `livedate`, `killdate`, `createdate`, `changedate` |
| `order` | `DESC` | `ASC`, `DESC` or `RAND` |

## Article selection

The feed SQL selects articles that are active, not deleted and not flagged `article_norss`, inside their publication window (`article_begin`/`article_end`), with `article_nosearch = 0`. Only public structure levels ship: levels must be active, not in trash and `acat_regonly = 0` — regonly levels never produce feed items. Items carry title, summary (falling back to subtitle), link by [URL handling](../general/url-handling.md), dates, guid and, when enabled, the author line. Multi-language markup strips through the same `[<lang>]` block parser the frontend uses (`combinedParser()`), and text converts into the feed's charset.

## rss.php

`rss.php` no longer generates feeds; it redirects to `feeds.php`. Keep links working across 1.x installs.

## RSS feed content part (CP 22)

Content part 22 pulls an *external* feed into the page:

- `rssurl` — the feed URL, parsed with the SimplePie based `rss_obj`.
- Template: selected file from `template/inc_cntpart/rssfeed/`, default `template/inc_default/rssfeed.tmpl`, hard-coded `<li>` markup as last fallback. Tags: `[RSSFEED]` wrapper with `[TITLE]`, `[SUBTITLE]`, `[ATTR_CLASS]`, `[ATTR_ID]`, `{ITEMS}`, `{FEEDINFO}`, `[LINK]`; per item `[ITEM]` loop with `LINK`, `TITLE`, `DESCRIPTION`, `CONTENT`, `AUTHOR`, `IMAGE`; the feed info header carries `IMAGE`, `TITLE`, `DESCRIPTION` and `{DIVIDER}`.
- `timeout` — cache seconds (default 3600), files under `content/rss/`; `cacheoff` disables caching.
- `item` — maximum item count.

## Related

- [Page rendering](page-rendering.md)
- [Core concepts](../general/concepts.md)
