<!-- docs/frontend/replacement-tags/index.md -->

# Replacement tags

> Source: `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php` (replacement cascade), `include/inc_front/front.func.inc.php`, `include/inc_front/ext.func.inc.php`

Replacement tags are `{NAME}` or `{NAME:parameter}` markers that the frontend resolves to generated HTML, text or values. They are the template developer's layer between raw content and the finished page. phpwcms resolves them late in the request, after every content part has rendered, so a tag placed anywhere in a template — or pasted into any content field — gets the same treatment.

## Where replacement tags work

Everything the renderer produces ends up in one assembled string (`$content['all']` in `content.func.inc.php`), and the replacement cascade runs once over that string. Tags therefore work wherever you can write template text:

- **Layout templates** — the page skeleton managed in the admin panel.
- **Content part templates** — `template/inc_cntpart/**` and the defaults in `template/inc_default/`.
- **Admin header/footer code of a template** — the `HEADER` and `FOOTER` block fields stored in the template record.
- **Custom blocks** — additional blocks a layout template defines.
- **Structure level and article fields** — for example level keywords or a custom canonical value.

Layout block tags such as `{CONTENT}`, `{HEADER}`, `{LEFT}`, `{RIGHT}`, `{FOOTER}` are filled directly from the rendered article stack before the cascade runs; see [replacement tag pages](#reference) for what the cascade itself resolves.

## Processing order

`index.php` loads `content.func.inc.php`, renders all content parts of the current article (or the article list of the level), assembles the layout, and passes the result through the steps below (line references: `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php`, current 2.x source):

1. `404` block handling: `[404]…[/404]` when the page was not found, `[404_ELSE]…[/404_ELSE]` otherwise.
2. Layout render (table, div or main-only) or print layout; `{CONTENT}` replaced by the rendered content, `{CURRENT_URL}` in print mode.
3. Custom blocks: `{KEY}` filled from `$content['CB']`, wrapped by `[KEY]…[/KEY]` / `[KEY_ELSE]…[/KEY_ELSE]`.
4. Content part tabs: `<!-- TAB_x -->` markers.
5. `[IF_LIST_MODE]` / `[ELSE_LIST_MODE]` sections.
6. Device conditionals: `<!--if:…-->…<!--/if-->` (first pass, `render_device()`).
7. `{CURRENT_ARTICLEID}` and `{CURRENT_CATEGORYID}`.
8. `[LEVEL<n>_ID]…[/LEVEL<n>_ID]` with the `{LEVEL<n>_ID}` replacer.
9. `[IF_CAT:id,id]` / `[IF_NOTCAT:…]` sections with the `{IF_CAT_ID}` / `{IF_NOTCAT_ID}` replacers.
10. `{SHOW_CONTENT:…}`.
11. `{SITE}` and `{TEMPLATE}`; then `render_PHPcode()` — `{PHP:…}`, `[PHP]…[/PHP]` and `{PHPVAR:…}` (only with `$phpwcms['enable_inline_php']`).
12. `{BREADCRUMB…}`; then `{NAV_LIST_UL:…}`; then the deprecated `NAV_*` family when `enable_deprecated` is set.
13. Fixed date and time tags: `{DATE_LONG}`, `{DATE_MEDIUM}`, `{DATE_SHORT}`, `{DATE_ARTICLE}`, `{TIME_LONG}`, `{TIME_SHORT}`, `{TIME_ARTICLE}`.
14. Search form placeholders `###search_input_###`.
15. `{RELATED:…}`, `{NEW:…}`, `{RSSIMG}`, `{KEYWORD:…}`, `{URL:…}`, `{BROWSE:…}`.
16. `html_parser()` — the text markup layer — plus all registered `$content['globalRT']` pairs. Depending on `$phpwcms['parse_html_mode']` this runs here (empty or `before`, the default), later instead (`after`), or twice (`before+after`).
17. Frontend render scripts: `template/inc_script/frontend_render/*.php` (when `allow_ext_render`) and module frontend renders — your custom hook layer; scripts can add their own `$content['globalRT']` entries here.
18. Device conditionals (final pass), `render_PHPcode()` again, `{LAZY_LOADING}`.
19. Automatic `description` / `keywords` meta, Open Graph and Twitter Cards, `generator` meta.
20. `[PRINT]` / `[PRINT_PDF]` links, then the article-level tags `{AUTHOR}`, the `{DATE:…}` family via `render_cnt_date()` and `{CATEGORY}`.
21. `{SOCIAL_SHARE…}`; `<!-- JS: … -->` and `<!-- CSS: … -->` comments.
22. Content part pagination: `{CP_PAGINATE}`, `{CP_PAGINATE_PREV}`, `{CP_PAGINATE_NEXT}`, `{CP_PAGINATE_CLASS}` and the `[CP_PAGINATE_MENU]`.
23. `LOGGED_IN` / `LOGGED_OUT` sections, `[HTML]` / `[HTML_SPECIAL]` conversion.
24. Cookie consent, tracking codes (GA/GTM/Piwik), alias URL rewriting for `index.php?aid/id` links, i18n `@@Text@@` and `[LANG:xx]` parsing, `{GT:…}` (deprecated).
25. `index.php` assembles the final document: doctype with `{DOCTYPE_LANG}`, base href, `<title>`, CSS files, custom `<head>` code, body tag, body JS — see the pipeline description in [core concepts](../../general/concepts.md).

`render_cnt_date()` (step 20) and the fixed `{DATE_*}`/`{TIME_*}` tags (step 13) run over the whole page, so date tags resolve anywhere — layout, header/footer and content part output alike.

## Custom replacement tags

A [frontend render script](#processing-order) (step 17) registers its own tags by adding key/value pairs to `$content['globalRT']`:

```php
$content['globalRT']['{MY_TAG}'] = 'replaced with this';
```

The pairs are applied during `html_parser()` / after the scripts with plain `str_replace`, so keep the key a literal string with braces. See the [replacement tag reference](#reference) and the deprecated list below for what is built in.

## Reference

| Page | Group |
| ---- | ----- |
| [NAV_LIST_UL](01-nav-list-ul.md) | ul/li navigation |
| [Site and server tags](02-site.md) | `{SITE}`, `{TEMPLATE}`, `{IP}`, `{LAZY_LOADING}` |
| [SHOW_CONTENT](03-show-content.md) | embed articles and content parts |
| [Article tags](04-article.md) | `{AUTHOR}`, `{CATEGORY}`, article summary fields |
| [Content part pagination](05-cp-paginate.md) | `{CP_PAGINATE}` and related tags |
| [Meta and head tags](06-meta.md) | page title, canonical, Open Graph, `{DOCTYPE_LANG}` |
| [Date and time](07-date-time.md) | `{DATE_*}`, `{TIME_*}`, `{DATE:…}` family |
| [Login functions](08-login-functions.md) | `LOGGED_IN`/`LOGGED_OUT`, frontend login tags |
| [RSS](09-rss.md) | `{RSSIMG}`, feed links |
| [Functions and misc](10-functions-misc.md) | `{NEW}`, `{RELATED}`, `{BROWSE}`, `{URL}`, `{BREADCRUMB}`, search form, leftovers |

## Deprecated replacement tags

The following tags still exist but render only when `$phpwcms['enable_deprecated']` is set in `config.inc.php`:

- Navigation: `{NAV_LIST}`, `{NAV_LIST_TOP}`, `{NAV_LIST_CURRENT}`, `{NAV_ROW}`, `{NAV_ROW:…}`, `{NAV_TABLE_SIMPLE}`, `{NAV_TABLE_COLUMN}`
- Images: `{RANDOM:…}`, `{RANDOM_GIF:…}`, `{RANDOM_JPEG:…}`, `{RANDOM_PNG:…}`, `{IMAGE:…}`, `{IMAGE_LEFT:…}`, `{IMAGE_RIGHT:…}`, `{IMAGE_CENTER:…}`
- The deprecated HTML pass wraps a second set of legacy text markers; these are all listed in [deprecated tags](../deprecated-tags.md).

Additional deprecated behavior outside that switch: `{GT:…}` renders only with `$phpwcms['gt_mod']`, and `image_resized.php` image URLs are rewritten to the current resize path on output. Both are covered by [deprecated tags](../deprecated-tags.md) — the pages above deliberately do not duplicate that reference.

---

<!-- docs/frontend/replacement-tags/01-nav-list-ul.md -->

# NAV_LIST_UL

> Source: `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php` (tag dispatch), `include/inc_front/front.func.inc.php` (`buildCascadingMenu()`)

The primary navigation replacement tag. Renders the structure level tree as `ul/li` markup. Works in layout templates, content parts and admin header/footer code alike; there is no restriction on how often you place it.

## Syntax

```
{NAV_LIST_UL: menu_type, start_id, max_depth, class_path, class_active, ul_id_name, wrap_ul_div, wrap_link_text, articlemenu}
```

All parameters comma separated. Unset trailing parameters can be left blank (`,,`). No `{`/`}` needed around class names themselves.

## Parameters

| # | Name | Default | Description |
| - | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| 1 | menu_type | *(empty)* | Output variant, see table below. |
| 2 | start_id | 0 | Structure level ID to start from; 0 = root. |
| 3 | max_depth | 0 | Maximum level depth; 0 = all levels. |
| 4 | class_path | *(empty)* | CSS classes for the active path, `|` separated. |
| 5 | class_active | *(empty)* | CSS classes for the active link, split as `class\|extra`. |
| 6 | ul_id_name | *(empty)* | Optional `id` for each level `ul` (`<ul id="…-0">` etc.). |
| 7 | wrap_ul_div | 0 | `0` off, `1` `<div>`, `2` `<div id="…">`, `3` `<div class="navLevel-0">`. Values >3 fall back to 2, <0 to 0. |
| 8 | wrap_link_text | *(empty)* | Link text wrapper: `prefix|suffix` around the `<a>` text. |
| 9 | articlemenu | *(empty)* | Article list options, only relevant for article-menu types — see below. |

## Menu types

| Type | Behavior |
| ---- | -------- |
| *(empty)* | Plain full menu, all levels unfolded. |
| `A` | Include article titles of each level as menu items. |
| `AH` | `A`, but skip the first (avoids doubling the parent link). |
| `B` | Bootstrap dropdown compatible `<li class="dropdown">` markup. |
| `BA` / `BAH` | Bootstrap + articles (+ hide first). |
| `P` | Also render a parent-level link. |
| `PA` / `PBA` / `PBAH` | Parent variants of the article types. |
| `F` | Folded: only the active path unfolds. |
| `FA` / `FAH` / `FP` / `FPA` / `FPAH` | Folded combined variants (fold + articles / parent). |
| `HCSS` / `HCSSP` | Horizontal sample CSS menu, optionally with parent. |
| `VCSS` / `VCSSP` | Vertical sample CSS menu, optionally with parent. |

`HCSS*`/`VCSS*` emit `<div class="navmenu-…">` scaffolding meant as starting points for custom CSS.

## Article menu options (9th parameter)

Only used by types containing `A`. Pipe separated, colon separated sub-values:

```
{NAV_LIST_UL:FAH,0,3,,nav-active,menu,2,|,[level]x300x80x1[|description:40|inside|<span class="…">}  (illustrative composition)
```

| Slot | Values | Purpose |
| ---- | ------ | ------- |
| 1 | `level` (or ID) | Per-level article menu — used to scope rendering. |
| 2 | `W×H[×1]` | Article summary image size; `×1` enables crop. |
| 3 | `description[:N]`, `menutitle[:N]`, `teaser[:N]`, `teaser:HTML` | Text source: summary description, level title or teaser text; `N` = character limit. |
| 4 | `inside` | Render the summary span inside the link instead of after it. |
| 5 | HTML | Custom wrap template for the summary, `%IMAGE%`, `%IMAGE_NAME%`, `%TEXT%` placeholders, default `<span class="amenu-extended">…</span>`. |

## Output

The renderer produces nested `<ul>`s, one class per depth (`navLevel-<depth>` naming when `wrap_ul_div` is 3), with the active path marked by the classes from parameter 4/5. Article entries reuse the summary image and teaser text configured above.

Typical layout template usage:

```html
<nav>{NAV_LIST_UL:F,0,2,active-path,active,mainnav,1,|</nav>
```

## Deprecated related tags

`{NAV_LIST}`, `{NAV_LIST_TOP}`, `{NAV_LIST_CURRENT}`, `{NAV_ROW}`, `{NAV_TABLE_SIMPLE}`, `{NAV_TABLE_COLUMN}` still exist but are replaced only when `enable_deprecated` is active in `config.inc.php` — do not use them in new templates. See [deprecated tags](../deprecated-tags.md).

---

<!-- docs/frontend/replacement-tags/02-site.md -->

# Site and server tags

> Source: `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php` (page cascade), `include/inc_front/front.func.inc.php` (`html_parser()`), `include/inc_lib/general.inc.php` (`replaceGlobalRT()`)

These tags stand for installation-wide paths and request values. They work everywhere the replacement cascade runs — layout templates, content parts, admin header/footer code.

## Syntax

```
{SITE}
{TEMPLATE}
{PHPWCMS_URL}
{PHPWCMS_TEMPLATE}
{IP}
{PHPWCMS_RESIZE_IMAGE}
{LAZY_LOADING}
{RSSIMG}
```

All are plain tags without parameters.

## Parameters

| Tag | Resolves to | Description |
| --- | ----------- | ----------- |
| `{SITE}` | `PHPWCMS_URL` | Absolute installation URL, protocol aware. See [PHPWCMS_URL](#phpwcms_url). |
| `{TEMPLATE}` | `TEMPLATE_PATH` | URL path of the current template directory, for example `template/`. |
| `{PHPWCMS_URL}` | `PHPWCMS_URL` | Same value as `{SITE}`; see [PHPWCMS_URL](#phpwcms_url). |
| `{PHPWCMS_TEMPLATE}` | `TEMPLATE_PATH` | Same value as `{TEMPLATE}`. |
| `{IP}` | visitor IP | Client IP, anonymized in GDPR mode. See [GDPR mode](#gdpr-mode). |
| `{PHPWCMS_RESIZE_IMAGE}` | image resize path | `img/cmsimage.php` or, with URL rewriting, `im`. |
| `{LAZY_LOADING}` | loading attribute string | `loading="…" decoding="async"` from `$phpwcms['lazy_loading']` (`lazy`, `eager` or `auto`, default `lazy`); empty when disabled. Content parts append it to their `<img>` tags. |
| `{RSSIMG}` | RSS icon markup | Value of `$template_default['rss']['image']`, an inline SVG feed icon. |

`{RSSIMG}` belongs to the [RSS group](09-rss.md) and is listed here only for completeness.

## Output

`{SITE}` and `{TEMPLATE}` are replaced twice so that both the final page and the text markup layer see them:

- In the main cascade (`content.func.inc.php`), before navigation rendering.
- Inside `html_parser()` after content part text is parsed, so a `{SITE}` inside article text also resolves.

```html
<!-- template source -->
<a href="{SITE}page.html"><img src="{TEMPLATE}img/logo.png" alt="" /></a>

<!-- output -->
<a href="https://example.com/page.html"><img src="template/img/logo.png" alt="" /></a>
```

{LAZY_LOADING} is a single pass at the end of the cascade (`str_replace`), because content parts embed it into image tags while rendering.

<a id="phpwcms_url"></a>
## PHPWCMS_URL

`{SITE}` and `{PHPWCMS_URL}` carry the same value, but run on different stages:

| Tag | Replaced in | Runs for |
| --- | ----------- | -------- |
| `{SITE}` | page cascade and `html_parser()` | every frontend request |
| `{PHPWCMS_URL}` | `replaceGlobalRT()` | newsletter mail text (content parts 12/23) and `verify.php` output |

Use `{PHPWCMS_URL}` in templates that ship both to the browser and into mail text, for example a newsletter confirmation template. Otherwise use `{SITE}`.

## GDPR mode

With `$phpwcms['enable_GDPR']` set (constant `PHPWCMS_GDPR_MODE`), `{IP}` returns `getAnonymizedIp()` — the second half of the address is zeroed (IPv4 `76.97.0.0` style) — instead of the raw client address from `getRemoteIP()`. The tag only resolves inside `replaceGlobalRT()`, so it is available in newsletter mail text and at `verify.php`, not in the main page cascade.

## Not present in 2.x

Older releases and third party documentation list additional "site" tags that no longer exist in this code base. Do **not** use them; the table shows what replaced them:

| Removed tag | Replacement |
| ----------- | ----------- |
| `{SITE_NAME}`, `{SITE_LEVELKEY}`, `{SITE_LINK_*}` | plain template text; level names come from the structure, navigation from [NAV_LIST_UL](01-nav-list-ul.md) |
| `{PHPWCMS_ROOT}` | PHP constant, not a replacement tag |
| `{PHPWCMS_USER_IP}`, `{USER_AGENT}`, `{HTTP_DNT}` | not handled; use device conditionals `<!--if:…-->` or a frontend render script |
| `{PHPWCMS_DOMAIN}` | not handled |

## Related

- [NAV_LIST_UL](01-nav-list-ul.md) — navigation built from the level tree
- [Meta and head tags](06-meta.md) — page title and canonical values also use absolute URLs
- [Deprecated tags](../deprecated-tags.md) — the legacy image and navigation tags

---

<!-- docs/frontend/replacement-tags/03-show-content.md -->

# SHOW_CONTENT

> Source: `include/inc_front/ext.func.inc.php` (`showSelectedContent()`), `include/inc_front/front.func.inc.php` (`list_articles_summary()`)

`{SHOW_CONTENT}` pulls rendered content into the current page: whole article summary teasers (`AS*` modes) or the output of single content parts (`CP*` modes). It evaluates once per assembled page, so the embedded content cannot contain another `{SHOW_CONTENT}`.

## Syntax

```
{SHOW_CONTENT:MODE,id[,id[,...]]}
```

`MODE` selects what to fetch and how to sort; the remaining comma separated numbers are article IDs (for `AS*`) or content part IDs (for `CP*`). The tag dispatches with `/\{SHOW_CONTENT:(.*?)\}/`.

## Parameters

| # | Parameter | Default | Description |
| - | --------- | ------- | ----------- |
| 1 | mode, optional `|count` / `|template` | — | Mode table below; the part before the first comma may carry `|count` and/or `|template` (AS modes only). |
| 2…n | id list | — | Article IDs (`AS*`) or content part IDs (`CP*`). Non numeric entries are dropped; only numeric IDs greater than 0 load. |

The `|count` / `|template` suffixes (AS modes): `AS|10` limits output to 10 articles, `AS|10|custom.tmpl` also names a list template, `AS|custom.tmpl` names the template only. A template name is accepted when a file `template/inc_cntpart/articlesummary/list/<name>` exists, or the literal `default`.

## AS modes — article summaries

`AS` returns article summaries rendered through a list template. Sorting suffixes (code comment: "L = live, K = kill, C = change date, R = random, T = keyword"):

| Mode | Sort | Note |
| ---- | ---- | ---- |
| `AS` | no explicit sort, order of the given IDs | |
| `AS*P` appended `P` | same as the base mode | adds `article_priorize DESC` in front of the sort column |
| `ASL` / `ASLD` | `article_begin ASC` / `DESC` | live date |
| `ASK` / `ASKD` | `article_end ASC` / `DESC` | kill date |
| `ASC` / `ASCD` | `article_tstamp ASC` / `DESC` | change date |
| `AST` / `ASTD` | `article_keyword ASC` / `DESC` | keyword |
| `ASR` | `RAND()` | random |

> **Note:** `ASCD` is broken in the current source: the order term references the column `article_tspamp` instead of `article_tstamp`, so a page requesting sorted-by-change-date output fails at the database level. Use `AS` plus a frontend render script workaround until this is fixed.

### AS selection options

Instead of an ID list, the second parameter may be a keyword:

```
{SHOW_CONTENT:AS,new}
{SHOW_CONTENT:AS,random}
{SHOW_CONTENT:AS|10,new}
{SHOW_CONTENT:AS,related|AND,keyword1[,keyword2,...]}
```

| Keyword | Behavior |
| ------- | -------- |
| `new` (default) | Most recent articles, `article_created DESC`; limit the count with the `|count` suffix in the mode block. |
| `random` | Random pick from the matching set (`RAND()`); same count handling. |
| `related` | Matches `article_keyword LIKE %KEY%` for every following keyword; `|AND` requires every keyword, `|OR` (default) any. The current article is excluded automatically. |

All AS requests automatically exclude `article_deleted=0`, respect the visibility mode and the live/kill window, and drop the current article ID.

## CP modes — content parts

| Mode | Behavior |
| ---- | -------- |
| `CP` | Renders one content part by its CP ID. Skips CPs assigned to the `CPSET` or `SYSTEM` blocks. |
| `CPA` | Renders the article's own content parts (IDs = article IDs), excluding `CPSET`/`SYSTEM`, in manual sort order. |
| `CPAD` | As `CPA`, descending. |
| `CPS` | Renders one content part by CP ID, `SYSTEM` block only. |
| `CPAS` / `CPASD` | As `CPA`, but only `SYSTEM` block content parts, ascending / descending. |

CP output re-runs the full content part renderer (`include/inc_front/content/cnt<N>.article.inc.php` or a module renderer), with the spacing, top link and frontend edit link each content part configured. Alias content parts (type 24) resolve their target, and module content parts (type 30) render only when the module is active. Inside CP templates you can print the content part ID with `{CPID}` or `[%CPID%]`.

Access control applies: content parts where `acontent_granted` denies the current frontend login state are skipped.

## Output

AS output comes from `list_articles_summary()`. The default template reads `template/inc_default/article_summary_list.tmpl`; the mode block may name another one. The template fields:

| Field | Content |
| ----- | ------- |
| `{TITLE}` / `{SUB}` | article title / subtitle, guarded by `[TITLE]`, `[SUB]` |
| `{SUMMARY:n}` | summary text, capped at `n` words (negative value: characters) |
| `{CATEGORYID}` | article level ID |
| `{CLASS}` | article class from `*CSS-class*` keywords and article meta |
| `{IMAGE}` | list image `<img>` element |
| `{ZOOMIMAGE}` | zoom/link popup markup when configured |
| `{THUMB_NAME}` `{THUMB_REL}` `{THUMB_ABS}` `{THUMB_WIDTH}` `{THUMB_HEIGHT}` | generated thumbnail values |
| `{IMAGE_NAME}` `{IMAGE_REL}` `{IMAGE_ABS}` `{IMAGE_WIDTH}` `{IMAGE_HEIGHT}` | zoom image values |
| `{IMAGE_ID}` `{IMAGE_HASH}` `{IMAGE_EXT}` | original file values |
| `{CAPTION}` `{CAPTION_SUPPRESS}` `{ALT}` `{IMAGE_TITLE}` `{COPYRIGHT}` | image caption parts from the file info |
| `{ARTICLELINK}` `{TARGET}` | link target of the article, target attribute |
| `{EDITOR}` `{ARTICLEID}` | author name, article ID |
| `{MORE}` | "read more" markup, `template_default['top_readmore_link']` |
| `{SPACE}` | set for every entry after the first |
| `[SYSTEM]…[/SYSTEM]` | renders `SYSTEM` block content parts of the article (detail/list scope) |
| date fields | `{DATE:…}`, `{NOW:…}`, `{LIVEDATE:…}`, `{KILLDATE:…}` see [date tags](07-date-time.md) |

Pagination: `list_articles_summary()` also renders the article list navigation when the level paginates. The list top/bottom placement and a global tag are configured with `$template_default['article_paginate_show']`; with `rt{RT}` the navigation is exposed to the page as the global tag `{RT}`.

## Examples

```
{SHOW_CONTENT:CP,1043}
{SHOW_CONTENT:AS,12,17,42}
{SHOW_CONTENT:ASLD|8,12,17,42}
{SHOW_CONTENT:AS|teaser.tmpl,related|AND,NEWS,SALES}
{SHOW_CONTENT:AS|5,new}
```

## Related

- [Article tags](04-article.md) — the same summary fields on the article detail page
- [Date and time](07-date-time.md) — date fields inside AS templates
- [NAV_LIST_UL](01-nav-list-ul.md) — article menu variant covers a similar teaser use case

<!-- docs/frontend/replacement-tags/04-article.md -->

# Article tags

> Source: `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php` (article level pass), `include/inc_front/content.article.inc.php` (detail renderer), `include/inc_front/front.func.inc.php` (`render_cnt_date()`, `setPageTitle()`)

When the request shows an article (`aid` or an article alias), the renderer stores the article record in `$content` and adds an article specific pass to the cascade. The tags below resolve on the whole page — layout template, header/footer and content part output.

## Syntax

```
{AUTHOR}
{CATEGORY}
{DATE_ARTICLE}
{TIME_ARTICLE}
{CURRENT_ARTICLEID}
{CURRENT_CATEGORYID}
```

## Parameters

| Tag | Default | Description |
| --- | ------- | ----------- |
| `{AUTHOR}` | article author | `article_username` of the shown article, guard with `[AUTHOR]…[/AUTHOR]`; empty in list mode. |
| `{CATEGORY}` | current level name | Name of the article's structure level in article view, name of the current level in list mode. |
| `{DATE_ARTICLE}` | — | Article date formatted with `$template_default['date']['article']`; see [date tags](07-date-time.md). |
| `{TIME_ARTICLE}` | — | Article time formatted with `$template_default['time']['short']`. |
| `{CURRENT_ARTICLEID}` | 0 | Numeric ID of the article being rendered, 0 on level pages. |
| `{CURRENT_CATEGORYID}` | 0 | Numeric ID of the current structure level. |

In list mode (no article detail) `{AUTHOR}` renders empty and the date tags fall back to the current time.

Sections follow the guard pattern of `render_cnt_template()`: `[AUTHOR]…[/AUTHOR]` keeps content only when the value exists, `[AUTHOR_ELSE]…[/AUTHOR_ELSE]` keeps it otherwise.

## Date fields of the article

`render_cnt_date()` receives the article date plus the live and kill dates of the shown article and renders the parametric [date tags](07-date-time.md) page wide:

```
{DATE:FORMAT}, {NOW:FORMAT}, {LIVEDATE:FORMAT}, {KILLDATE:FORMAT}
```

`[LIVEDATE]…[/LIVEDATE]` and `[KILLDATE]…[/KILLDATE]` keep their inner content only while the live or kill date is set, so a template can hide a date row for timeless articles.

## Article summary template fields

The article detail renders through `template/inc_default/article_summary.tmpl` or a custom `template/inc_cntpart/articlesummary/article/` template. The detail renderer fills:

| Field | Content |
| ----- | ------- |
| `{TITLE}` / `{SUB}` | article title / subtitle |
| `{SUMMARY}` | summary text, suppressed when the article hides the summary |
| `{IMAGE}` | summary image `<img>` element |
| `{ZOOMIMAGE}` | zoom link markup when configured |
| `{IMAGE_URL}` `{IMAGE_TARGET}` | image target URL and target from the caption info |
| `{THUMB_*}` / `{IMAGE_*}` | thumbnail and zoom image values (name, rel, abs, width, height, ext) |
| `{IMAGE_ID}` `{IMAGE_HASH}` `{IMAGE_EXT}` | original file identity |
| `{CAPTION}` `{CAPTION_SUPPRESS}` `{ALT}` `{IMAGE_TITLE}` `{COPYRIGHT}` | caption values from the file info |
| `{EDITOR}` | author name |
| `{MORE}` | a single space while the article has a read-more link |
| `{CLASS}` | CSS class from `*CSS-class*` keywords and article meta |
| `[SYSTEM]…[/SYSTEM]` | `SYSTEM` block content parts of the article |

The list rendering used by [SHOW_CONTENT](03-show-content.md) adds fields on top: `{SUMMARY:n}` word capped summary, `{CATEGORYID}`, `{ARTICLELINK}` / `{TARGET}`, `{ARTICLEID}`, `{MORE}` as the full read-more markup (`top_readmore_link`), and `{SPACE}` between entries.

The article list navigation is a separate template string (`$template_default['article_paginate_navi']`) placed at list top or bottom; inside it `{PREV:TEXT}`, `{NEXT:TEXT}`, `{NAVI:123}` or `{NAVI:1-3}` build the page links and `{POS}` tells whether it sits on top or bottom. Details for the analogous content part pagination live in [content part pagination](05-cp-paginate.md).

## Page title

`content.article.inc.php` builds `$content['pagetitle']` with `setPageTitle()`: layout title, article level name and article title merge in the order configured by `pagelayout['layout_title_order']` (0-14, default 0 = layout title, level, article), joined by `pagelayout['layout_title_spacer']` (default ` | `). A custom title per article or level (`article_pagetitle` / `acat_pagetitle`) overrides the composed one. See [meta and head tags](06-meta.md).

## Not present in 2.x

`{ARTICLE:FIELD}` variants known from older documentation do not exist in this code base. Article fields reach templates through the summary template fields above, or through article meta values — description and keywords — described in [meta and head tags](06-meta.md).

## Related

- [SHOW_CONTENT](03-show-content.md) — reuses the same list template fields
- [Date and time](07-date-time.md) — full parameter reference of the `{DATE:…}` family
- [NAV_LIST_UL](01-nav-list-ul.md) — article menu variant

---

<!-- docs/frontend/replacement-tags/05-cp-paginate.md -->

# Content part pagination

> Source: `include/inc_front/content.article.inc.php` (page collection), `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php` (navigation render)

Content part pagination turns one article into several pages: each content part belongs to a paginate page, and the reader moves with numbered links or prev/next links. The tags below only render when the article uses pagination; when the article has no second page the whole `CP_PAGINATE` section of the template is removed.

## Syntax

```
{CP_PAGINATE}
{CP_PAGINATE_PREV}
{CP_PAGINATE_NEXT}
{CP_PAGINATE_CLASS}
[CP_PAGINATE_MENU]…[/CP_PAGINATE_MENU]
[CP_PAGINATE_MENU:menu parameters]
```

Place them inside the article summary template (`template/inc_default/article_summary.tmpl`, a custom `template/inc_cntpart/articlesummary/article/` template, or the paginate variant in `articlesummary/article/paginate/`). Guard them with the matching bracket sections, for example `[CP_PAGINATE_PREV]…{CP_PAGINATE_PREV}…[/CP_PAGINATE_PREV]`, so markup disappears when a direction does not exist.

## How pages are collected

For each content part the backend stores a paginate page number (`acontent_paginate_page`) and an optional title (`acontent_paginate_title`). Page `0` and page `1` are the same page; content parts without a pager belong to it. The renderer collects distinct pages only from content parts in the `CONTENT` block that are visible and within their live/kill window. The requested page arrives as the part after the first dash of `aid`, so `/index.php?aid=12-2` shows page 2 of article 12.

While a page greater than 1 is shown, the article summary template falls back to the paginate variant when one exists — `template/inc_cntpart/articlesummary/article/paginate/<selected template>`, `template/inc_default/article_summary_paginate.tmpl`, else a built in fallback with previous/next/number links.

## Tags

| Tag | Default | Description |
| --- | ------- | ----------- |
| `{CP_PAGINATE}` | — | One link per page, label = page number. Link classes from `cp-paginate-link` / `cp-paginate-link-active`. Guard with `[CP_PAGINATE]…[/CP_PAGINATE]`. |
| `{CP_PAGINATE_PREV}` | — | Absolute URL of the previous page, empty on page 1. |
| `{CP_PAGINATE_NEXT}` | — | Absolute URL of the next page, empty on the last page. |
| `{CP_PAGINATE_CLASS}` | — | Value of the class `cp-paginate-link`, convenience for templates outside the standard list rendering. |

Numbered links are built from `$template_default['attributes']['cp-paginate']`: each link is wrapped by `link-prefix` / `link-suffix` and its label by `value-prefix` / `value-suffix`. Active-page handling uses the `cp-paginate-link-active` class.

When `$phpwcms['disable_next_prev']` is unset, the renderer also writes `rel="prev"` / `rel="next"` `<link>` tags into the document head for the current page.

## CP_PAGINATE_MENU

`[CP_PAGINATE_MENU]…[/CP_PAGINATE_MENU]` renders one link per page using each page's `acontent_paginate_title` as the label (fall back: `#n` page number). Custom parameters override the defaults:

```
[CP_PAGINATE_MENU:item_prefix|item_suffix|active_class|hide_active]
```

| # | Parameter | Default | Description |
| - | --------- | ------- | ----------- |
| 1 | `item_prefix` | `link-prefix` | HTML before each item `<a>`. |
| 2 | `item_suffix` | `link-suffix` | HTML after each item `</a>`. |
| 3 | `active_class` | `cp-paginate-link-active` | Class for the active page link; empty removes classes. |
| 4 | `hide_active` | 0 | `1` drops the active page from the menu instead of marking it. |

With custom parameters the outer wrap (`wrap-prefix` / `wrap-suffix`) is dropped; without them the defaults apply, so the menu renders as a `<ul class="pagination">` list by default.

## Output

```html
<!-- template with defaults -->
[CP_PAGINATE]{CP_PAGINATE}[/CP_PAGINATE]

<!-- output; the requested page arrives as aid=12-2 -->
<li class="page-item"><a href="https://example.com/index.php?news" class="page-link active">1</a></li>
<li class="page-item"><a href="https://example.com/index.php?aid=12-2" class="page-link">2</a></li>
```

Page 1 links back to the page alias — article alias when the article has one, else level alias, else `aid=<id>`; all other pages use `aid=<article id>-<page number>` even when the article has an alias.

Class and attribute names come from the default configuration `include/config/conf.template_default.inc.php`: classes `page-link`, `page-link active`, `page-link disabled` and the `cp-paginate` attributes `wrap-prefix` (`<ul class="pagination">`), `wrap-suffix` (`</ul>`), `link-prefix` (`<li class="page-item">`), `link-suffix` (`</li>`), empty `value-prefix` / `value-suffix` / `href-disabled`. A template can overwrite them via its template default include.

Also handled at this stage: `<!--CP_PAGINATE_START//-->…<!--CP_PAGINATE_END//-->` comment markers around the pagination block are stripped while pagination works and the complete section disappears when the article has no pages. The article's canonical `<link>` uses the paginated URL (`aid=<id>-<page>`, see [meta and head tags](06-meta.md)).

## Related

- [Article tags](04-article.md) — the list level equivalent with `{PREV}` / `{NEXT}` / `{NAVI}`
- [SHOW_CONTENT](03-show-content.md) — CP modes can embed a paginated article's content parts

<!-- docs/frontend/replacement-tags/06-meta.md -->

# Meta and head tags

> Source: `index.php` (page assembly), `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php` (metas, Open Graph), `include/inc_front/content.article.inc.php` (article metas), `include/inc_front/front.func.inc.php` (`set_meta()`, `setPageTitle()`)

phpwcms builds the `<head>` automatically: doctype and document language, content type, base href, page title, description, keywords, canonical link and social sharing meta. Templates add to it with `set_meta()` from a frontend render script or with custom code in a template's head fields.

## Document language

The `lang` attribute of the `<html>` tag comes from `PHPWCMS_DOCTYPE_LANG`, defined per doctype mode in `include/inc_lib/default.inc.php`:

```
{DOCTYPE_LANG}
```

The placeholder sits inside the doctype template string and receives the value of `$phpwcms['DOCTYPE_LANG']` — the two letter code of the frontend language (for example `en`, `de`). With `use_content_lang` enabled, a structure level language (`acat_lang`) overrides the default, so a translated subtree serves a matching `lang` attribute. The same value feeds `og:locale` and the localized [date tags](07-date-time.md).

The XHTML doctypes (modes 1 and 2) additionally emit `xml:lang`; the HTML 4.01 and HTML5 forms emit `lang` only.

## Page title

`index.php` writes `$content['pagetitle']` into `<title>`. The value builds from three parts — layout title (`pagelayout['layout_title']`), structure level name and article title — merged by `setPageTitle()` in the order configured by `pagelayout['layout_title_order']` (default 0: layout title, level, article), joined by `layout_title_spacer` (default ` | `). Orders 1-14 produce other combinations up to a single part; empty parts drop out and duplicates collapse.

A custom title wins over the composed one: `article_pagetitle` for the article, `acat_pagetitle` for the level. Replacement tag pairs inside the page title get cleaned before output (`sanitize_replacement_tags()` replaces `{TAG}…{/TAG}` pairs with their inner content), so stray tags never leak into the title.

| Source | Priority |
| ------ | -------- |
| `article_pagetitle` | 1 — article detail view |
| `acat_pagetitle` | 2 — level view and list mode |
| `setPageTitle()` composition | 3 — fallback |

## Description and keywords

| Value | Source | Behavior |
| ----- | ------ | -------- |
| `description` | `article_description` of the shown article | `set_meta('description', …)` when the article defines one; feeds `og:description`. |
| `description` | `acat_info` of the current level | Fallback when the page has no description yet and the level carries an info text. |
| `keywords` | article `article_keyword` plus level `acat_keywords` | Merged, `*CSS-…*` class keywords filtered out, added as one `keywords` meta when none was defined. |

`set_meta()` registers the tag in `$block['custom_htmlhead']['meta.<name>']`; a template or script can set the same key earlier to keep its own value — the automatic pass checks for an existing `description` / `keywords` meta before adding.

Robots: when the article meta defines `noindex` or `nofollow`, phpwcms emits `set_meta('robots', …)` and the matching `X-Robots-Tag` HTTP header.

## Canonical link

The canonical `<link rel="canonical">` resolves in this order:

| Source | Config / field | Behavior |
| ------ | -------------- | -------- |
| Article custom canonical | `article_canonical` | Replaces any other canonical. |
| Level custom canonical | `acat_canonical` | Relative values resolve against `PHPWCMS_URL`; a value starting `{SITE}` expands to the install URL first. |
| Auto canonical | default, unless `canonical_off` | Points at the article alias, or at the level alias when the level shows exactly one article. |
| Off | `$phpwcms['canonical_off']` | No canonical link. |

With `force301_2struct` the auto canonical turns into a real 301 redirect to the level alias where the redirect is allowed (`acat_disable301` excludes a level, and POST requests and content-part-paginated views keep their URL). The level redirect to its alias runs earlier for plain level URLs (`force301_2struct`) and for article URLs with alias (`force301_id2alias`).

## Open Graph and social sharing

When `$phpwcms['set_sociallink']['render']` is enabled and the page allows sharing (`acat_opengraph` / `article_opengraph` per level or article), the renderer adds:

| Meta | Value |
| ---- | ----- |
| `og:type` | `website` on level pages, `article` on article pages. |
| `og:title` | sanitized Open Graph title — article title, level name or layout title, `{TAG}…{/TAG}` pairs cleaned. |
| `og:url` | page URL without the GET values `phpwcms_output_action`, `print`, `phpwcms-preview`, `unsubscribe`, `subscribe`. |
| `og:site_name` | layout title when set. |
| `og:locale` | `$content['opengraph']['locale']` when a frontend script sets it, otherwise `get_locale_canonical()` of `{DOCTYPE_LANG}` with `$phpwcms['default_lang']` and `en` as fallbacks. |
| `og:description` | article description when set. |
| `og:image` | shop, news or article image in `$phpwcms['opengraph_imagesize']` (default `1200x630x1`), else `template/img/opengraph-default.png` when present. |

Twitter / X Cards: `twitter:card` defaults to `summary_large_image` when the page has an image, else `summary`. A template comment `<!--TWITTER:summary-->`, `<!--TWITTER:summary_large_image-->`, `<!--TWITTER:player-->` or `<!--TWITTER:app-->` overrides it; so does `$content['opengraph']['twitter:card']`. `twitter:site` comes from `$phpwcms['twitter_site']`, `twitter:creator` from the article author name when it starts with `@`.

## Generator meta

`<meta name="generator" content="phpwcms …">` and the `X-phpwcms-Release` header render unless `$phpwcms['disable_generator']` is set or the installation runs whitelabeled (`is_whitelabel()`).

## Base href and viewport

`index.php` adds `<base>` when `$phpwcms['base_href']` is set (`true` uses the install URL; a path uses that path), and `<meta name="viewport" …>` from `$phpwcms['viewport']`. The doctype pass also writes the content type meta from `PHPWCMS_CHARSET`, or the HTML5 short form `<meta charset="…">` in doctype mode 3 (`<!DOCTYPE html>`).

## Adding meta from scripts

```php
include/inc_lib: set_meta($name, $content, $type, $return, $allow_multiple)
```

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `name` | — | Meta name (`description`) or property (`og:image`). |
| `content` | — | Value, HTML escaped on output. |
| `type` | FALSE | `FALSE` = `name`, `property` / `prop` = `property`, `itemprop`, `http-equiv` (or TRUE), or any attribute name. |
| `return` | FALSE | TRUE returns the built `meta` string instead of registering it in head code. |
| `allow_multiple` | FALSE | TRUE appends instead of overwriting — used for several `og:image` values. |

## Related

- [Date and time](07-date-time.md) — `{DOCTYPE_LANG}` selects localized date names
- [Site and server tags](02-site.md) — `{SITE}` inside a canonical value expands to the install URL
- [Login functions](08-login-functions.md) — the same head channel carries login redirects

<!-- docs/frontend/replacement-tags/07-date-time.md -->

# Date and time

> Source: `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php` (fixed `{DATE_*}` / `{TIME_*}` pass), `include/inc_front/front.func.inc.php` (`render_cnt_date()`, `render_date()`, `date_callback()`, `international_date_format()`)

Two groups of date tags exist: fixed tags that carry the format from the configuration, and parametric tags that name the PHP `date()` format right inside the tag.

## Syntax

```
{DATE_LONG}          {DATE_MEDIUM}          {DATE_SHORT}          {DATE_ARTICLE}
{TIME_LONG}          {TIME_SHORT}           {TIME_ARTICLE}

{DATE:format}
{NOW:format}
{LIVEDATE:format}
{KILLDATE:format}
{DATE:format lang=xx}
```

## Fixed tags

> Source of the defaults: `include/config/conf.template_default.inc.php`

| Tag | Default format | Description |
| --- | -------------- | ----------- |
| `{DATE_LONG}` | `l, j. F Y` | Current date, verbose (`Monday, 1. October 2003`). |
| `{DATE_MEDIUM}` | `D, j. M y` | Current date, medium (`Mon, 1. Oct 03`). |
| `{DATE_SHORT}` | `Y/m/d` | Current date. |
| `{DATE_ARTICLE}` | `Y/m/d` | Date of the shown article (`article_date`), formatted with `$template_default['date']['article']`. |
| `{TIME_LONG}` | `H:i:s` | Current time with seconds. |
| `{TIME_SHORT}` | `H:i` | Current time. |
| `{TIME_ARTICLE}` | `H:i` (time short format) | Time of the shown article. |

The fixed date tags resolve with `international_date_format()` against `$template_default['date']['language']`, so a language file under `include/inc_lang/date/` localizes month and day names. All values default from the configuration; only the language key and the format strings are configurable there.

## Parametric tags

`render_cnt_date()` runs over the assembled page after article rendering (step 20 of the [pipeline](index.md#processing-order)) and per entry inside article list templates, replacing:

| Tag | Date used |
| --- | --------- |
| `{DATE:format}` | Article date in article view, current time otherwise. |
| `{NOW:format}` | Always the current time. |
| `{LIVEDATE:format}` | Article live date (`article_begin`). [LIVEDATE]…[/LIVEDATE] content stays only when set. |
| `{KILLDATE:format}` | Article kill date (`article_end`). [KILLDATE]…[/KILLDATE] keeps content only when set. |

Outside article detail view the call passes the current time for all four values, so `{LIVEDATE:…}` / `{KILLDATE:…}` render `now()` there.

Format follows PHP `date()` codes; the callback uses `date($format, …)`.

### lang parameter

```
{DATE:j. F Y lang=de}
```

When the tag ends with ` lang=<two letters>` the renderer switches to `international_date_format()` and outputs localized weekday and month names for that language. Language files live in `include/inc_lang/date/`, with aliases `cz`→`cs`, `se`→`sv`, `vn`→`vi`, `el`→`gr`, `uk`→`ua`, `zh`→`zh-cn`, `in`→`id`. An empty language uses `{DOCTYPE_LANG}`.

Without the `lang` parameter, weekday/month format letters still localize automatically when the document language is not `en` and the format contains `M`, `F`, `D` or `l` — otherwise `date()` runs with the plain format.

### set option

```
{DATE:format set=<timestamp>}
{DATE:format set=<date string>}
```

Both date callbacks accept a trailing ` set=` in the format part: a numeric value is the direct timestamp, a string goes through `phpwcms_strtotime()`. Without it the tag uses the article date.

## GMDATE variant

`include/inc_lib/general.inc.php` defines one more parametric pair, applied by `replaceGlobalRT()` — newsletter mail text (content parts 12 / 23) and `verify.php`:

```
{DATE:DATE_FORMAT[ SET:timestamp]}
{GMDATE:DATE_FORMAT[ SET:timestamp]}
```

`SET:` takes a timestamp or a date string; `{GMDATE:…}` renders UTC (`gmdate()`). These run only where `replaceGlobalRT()` applies, not on normal pages — use the `{DATE:…}` family above there.

## SORTDATE

The news content part (type 33) adds `{SORTDATE:format}` inside its entry templates, bound to the entry's sort date — a content part scoped tag, covered by the [content parts reference](../../content-parts/index.md). The tag resolves through the same `render_date()` callbacks as above.

## Not present in 2.x

Older documentation lists `{DATE_M_<format>}` and similar month variants; no such handler exists in this code base. Use `{DATE:format lang=xx}` to get localized output.

## Related

- [Article tags](04-article.md) — which article dates feed the parametric tags
- [Meta and head tags](06-meta.md) — how `{DOCTYPE_LANG}` is set

<!-- docs/frontend/replacement-tags/08-login-functions.md -->

# Login functions

> Source: `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php` (`LOGGED_*` sections, `PERMIT_ACCESS`), `include/inc_front/front.func.inc.php` (`_getFeUserLoginStatus()`, `_checkFrontendUserAutoLogin()`), `template/inc_script/frontend_render/disabled/felogin.render.php`

phpwcms distinguishes the backend session (editors, administrators) from a frontend session. The template layer reacts to both with section markup and, with the optional felogin script enabled, with login replacement tags.

## LOGGED_IN and LOGGED_OUT sections

```
<!--LOGGED_IN_START//-->…<!--LOGGED_IN_END//-->
<!--LOGGED_OUT_START//-->…<!--LOGGED_OUT_END//-->
[LOGGED_IN]…[/LOGGED_IN]
```

Write the two comment sections anywhere in layout template, content part template or admin header/footer code. While the page renders, `_getFeUserLoginStatus()` decides:

- User is logged in: the `LOGGED_IN` section content is kept (comment markers stripped), the whole `LOGGED_OUT` section is removed.
- User is not logged in: the `LOGGED_OUT` content is kept, the `LOGGED_IN` section is removed.

The check answers true only when a session exists and `$_SESSION[<session id>]` holds the login name of an activated user, with GET/POST injection guards on the session key. With no session it answers false.

Both comment sections resolve inside the core `content.func.inc.php` pass. The bracket form `[LOGGED_IN]…[/LOGGED_IN]` — keep content while logged in, `render_cnt_template()` semantics otherwise — ships as the optional frontend render script `template/inc_script/frontend_render/disabled/logged_in.php` and needs that script enabled.

A successful frontend logout runs through the `feLogout` GET or POST value; logout links therefore point at the current page extended with `feLogout`.

## PERMIT_ACCESS and protected levels

A structure level with the "registered only" flag (`acat_regonly`) locks every level below it. The flag walks the level path of the current request; one match sets `PERMIT_ACCESS` to false. When false and no frontend user is logged in:

1. The current URL is stored in `$_SESSION['LOGIN_REDIRECT']` for the way back.
2. The request redirects with HTTP 401 to the login form URL — the template's `feloginurl` field when set (a leading `{SITE}` expands), otherwise `$template_default['login_form_url']`.

Content parts carry their own granted flag (`acontent_granted`); with a frontend user logged in, parts with permission level 2 become visible, without a login they are skipped. Article selection respects the same flag (constant `FEUSER_LOGIN_STATUS`).

`_checkFrontendUserAutoLogin()` reads the `phpwcmsFeLoginRemember` cookie before page assembly, so a remembered login applies without a new POST.

## Frontend login content part

The built-in "Frontend login" content part (type 28, `include/inc_front/content/cnt28.article.inc.php`) renders the standard login form from its template. It uses the template sections `LOGIN_FORM` (form while logged out) and `LOGIN_IS` (state while logged in) plus profile and reminder sections, and fills:

| Field | Value |
| ----- | ----- |
| `{LOGIN_URL}` and `{FORM_TARGET}` | the form action URL; after login the reader returns to `$_SESSION['LOGIN_REDIRECT']` or the current page |
| `{LOGIN}` | current login name inside the logged-in section |
| `[REGISTER_PROFILE]` / `[MANAGE_PROFILE]` / `[REMINDER_FORM]` | links when the content part enables registration, profile management or password reminder |

The related sample script `template/inc_script/frontend_render/disabled/fe_user.php` adds `{FE_USER_REGISTER}` and `{FE_USER_MANAGE}` markup for a customized registration form.

## felogin script tags

The shipped sample login `template/inc_script/felogin/` works with two scripts that are disabled by default — copy them from `template/inc_script/frontend_init/disabled/felogin.init.php` and `template/inc_script/frontend_render/disabled/felogin.render.php` into the active folders. The users and passwords live in `template/inc_script/felogin/felogin.ini.php`; login levels map to structure level IDs.

| Tag | Value |
| --- | ----- |
| `{FELOGIN}` | Complete login or logout form, `felogin.login.html` / `felogin.logout.html`. |
| `{FELOGIN_USER}` | Login name of the currently logged-in user, HTML escaped. |
| `{FELOGOUT_PREFIX}` / `{FELOGOUT_SUFFIX}` | HTML around the user name in the logout link, from `FELOGIN_LOGOUT_LINK_PREFIX` / `SUFFIX`. |
| `{FELOGIN_ERROR}` | Error list wrapped by `FELOGIN_ERROR_PREFIX` / `SUFFIX`, empty when no error. |
| `{FELOGIN_ACTION}` | Inside the login template: form action pointing at the login level. |
| `{FELOGIN_LOGOUT_URL}` | Inside the logout template: logout URL with the configured `logout` GET value. |

The page level tags (`{FELOGIN}`, `{FELOGIN_USER}`, `{FELOGOUT_PREFIX}`, `{FELOGOUT_SUFFIX}`, `{FELOGIN_ERROR}`) render only while `FELOGIN_IS_LOGGED` is defined — that is, only when the init script is active. The `@@Text@@` markers inside the shipped templates resolve through the language pass.

The felogin logout link appears as a virtual last level in navigation when `FELOGIN_LOGOUT_LINK` is set in the INI file; the nav renderers pick it up as a normal entry.

## Backend login

The form at `login.php` handles backend login for editors and administrators. The `LOGIN_REDIRECT` way-back applies to the frontend login content part instead: after a successful login it sends the reader to `$_SESSION['LOGIN_REDIRECT']` (set by the `PERMIT_ACCESS` redirect) or back to the current page.

## Not present in 2.x

`{LOGIN}`, `{LOGIN_REDIRECT_ELSE}` and `{PERMIT_ACCESS…}` tags from older documentation have no handler in this code base. Use the section markup above and the `PERMIT_ACCESS` behavior, or a frontend render script.

## Related

- [Meta and head tags](06-meta.md) — head channel the login redirect uses for 401 handling
- [NAV_LIST_UL](01-nav-list-ul.md) — the logout entry joins the menu tree

<!-- docs/frontend/replacement-tags/09-rss.md -->

# RSS

> Source: `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php` (`RSSIMG` pass), `include/inc_front/front.func.inc.php` (`html_parser()` feed link), `include/config/conf.template_default.inc.php`

phpwcms serves feeds from `feeds.php` and the template layer offers the RSS icon tag plus the feed link markup.

## {RSSIMG}

```
{RSSIMG}
```

Replaced by `$template_default['rss']['image']`. The default value in `include/config/conf.template_default.inc.php` is an inline SVG feed icon (`width="14" height="14"`, fill `#fd7e14`). Overwrite the value in a template default override file to place your own icon markup.

## Feed link markup

The text markup layer converts the pattern below into a link to `feeds.php?feed=<id>`:

```
[RSS 1]Feed title[/RSS]
```

```html
<a href="feeds.php?feed=1" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="link-rss">Feed title</a>
```

The link class comes from `$template_default['classes']['link-rss']` (`link-rss` by default). Feed IDs and their definitions come from the feed configuration (`include/config/feeds.ini.php`), rendered by `feeds.php`.

## Feed listing template (content part 22)

The RSS feed import content part ships its own template fields, resolved within that content part — `{FEEDINFO}`, `{ITEMS}`, `{TITLE}`, `{SUBTITLE}`, `{ATTR_CLASS}`, `{ATTR_ID}` and the entry fields inside `{ITEMS}`. They belong to the [content parts reference](../../content-parts/index.md), not to the global tag cascade.

The news content part (type 33) wraps its output in `[NEWS_ENTRIES]…[/NEWS_ENTRIES]` for the same reason.

## Not present in 2.x

`{RSS_TITLE}`, `{RSS_DESCRIPTION}` and other per-feed replacement tags from older documentation have no handler here. Generate feed pages through `feeds.php` or a frontend render script.

## Related

- [Site and server tags](02-site.md) — `{RSSIMG}` is listed among global output tags
- [Functions and misc](10-functions-misc.md) — the search and browse tags that share the same cascade slot

<!-- docs/frontend/replacement-tags/10-functions-misc.md -->

# Functions and misc tags

> Source: `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php` (dispatch), `include/inc_front/front.func.inc.php` (`get_new_articles()`, `get_related_articles()`, `get_keyword_link()`, `get_index_link_*()`, `include_url()`, `breadcrumb()`)

This page collects the replacement tags outside the groups with dedicated pages. All of them run in the late cascade, after [SHOW_CONTENT](03-show-content.md) and navigation.

## NEW and RELATED

### {NEW:max[,category]}

> Source: `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php` regex `/\{NEW:(\d+):{0,1}(\d+){0,1}\}/`, `front.func.inc.php` `get_new_articles()`

Lists the newest articles of the installation or of one category.

| # | Parameter | Default | Description |
| - | --------- | ------- | ----------- |
| 1 | max | — | Maximum number of links; 0 lists without limit. |
| 2 | category | *(empty)* | Structure level ID to restrict the list to. |

Output comes from `$template_default['news']`: wrapper `before` (`<div class="news">`) / `after`, per link `link_before` (`<p>`) / `link_after` (`</p>`), optional `link_symbol`, `link_target`, title cut at `link_length` with `cut_title_add`, and — when `date_format` is set — a date prefix wrapped by `date_before` / `date_after` (`<span class="datelink">…</span>`, separator ` - `). Sorting follows `$template_default['news']['sort_by']`: `cdate` (creation), `ldate` (live date), `kdate` (kill date), otherwise change date. Articles without a read-more link are skipped; redirected articles link to their redirect target.

### {RELATED:max} and {RELATED:max:keywords}

> Source: `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php`, `front.func.inc.php` `get_related_articles()`

Lists articles whose `article_keyword` matches.

| # | Parameter | Default | Description |
| - | --------- | ------- | ----------- |
| 1 | max | — | Maximum number of links; 0 without limit. |
| 2 | keywords | current article keywords | Comma separated list; `ALLKEYWORDS` expands to the page keyword collection; a leading `-` excludes a keyword; keywords shorter than 3 characters drop out. |

Matching is `LIKE %KEY%` against every keyword; visible mode, deletion and live/kill window apply, the current article is excluded. Output uses `$template_default['related']`: wrapper, link prefix/suffix, symbol, target, title cut — analogous to `{NEW}`. Sorting follows `$template_default['related']['sort_by']`: `title_asc`/`title_desc`, `ldate_asc`/`ldate_desc`, `kdate_asc`/`kdate_desc`, `cdate_asc`/`cdate_desc`, default change date descending.

## {KEYWORD:keyword[,keyword]}

> Source: `front.func.inc.php` `get_keyword_link()`, regex `/\{KEYWORD:(.*?)\}/`

Matches articles whose keyword field contains `*keyword*` markers and returns a link. One matching article renders as a single `<a>` with the keyword list as the link text. Several matches render the keyword as plain text followed by numbered links in brackets: `Keyword [1][2]`. No match renders the keywords as text. The output wraps with `$template_default['article']['keyword_before']` / `keyword_after`.

## {BROWSE:UP|NEXT|PREV:text[,flag]}

> Source: `front.func.inc.php` `get_index_link_up()`, `get_index_link_next()`, `get_index_link_prev()`

| Tag | Behavior | Flag |
| --- | -------- | ---- |
| `{BROWSE:UP:text}` | Link to the parent structure level. | — |
| `{BROWSE:NEXT:text,flag}` | Link to the next article of the current level. | `1` continues into sub levels and then to the next level of the same parent depth. |
| `{BROWSE:PREV:text,flag}` | Link to the previous article of the current level. | same continuation behavior |

The `text` parameter is the link text (`UP`, `NEXT`, `PREV` when empty). When no target exists the text renders as plain text; with a target it becomes `<a href="…">text</a>`. Hidden levels without alias use `id=<level>` URLs.

## {URL:address[,CACHE=seconds]}

> Source: `content.func.inc.php` regex `/\{URL:(.*?)\}/i`, `front.func.inc.php` `include_url()`

Includes an external HTML page — but only the part between `<body>` and `</body>`. Relative `href` / `src` / `action` attributes become absolute, scripts and styles are filtered (`htmlfilter_sanitize`), the charset converts to the installation charset, and PHP markers are HTML escaped before insertion.

```
{URL:https://example.com/news.html CACHE=3600}
```

With `CACHE=seconds` the content is stored in `content/tmp/<md5>-url` and reused until the timeout expires. Remote loading writes no content when the request fails. Do not confuse this with the plain `{URL}` field inside download templates — that one belongs to the [content parts reference](../../content-parts/index.md).

## {BREADCRUMB}

> Source: `content.func.inc.php` regex `/\{BREADCRUMB:?(\-?\d+){0,1}(,[01]){0,1}\}/`, `front.func.inc.php` `breadcrumb_wrapper()`, `breadcrumb()`

Renders the path of structure levels from the current level up to the root.

| # | Parameter | Default | Description |
| - | --------- | ------- | ----------- |
| 1 | end level | 0 | Level ID where the path stops (inclusive). A negative value never stops early and walks to root. |
| 2 | category only | 0 | `1` omits the article title — without it, article pages name the article after the path. |

Output: level names in path order, linked except the current position; hidden level rules and the `acat_breadcrumb` setting of each level decide whether a level appears and whether it links. The active part carries `breadcrumb_active_prefix` / suffix (default `<strong aria-current="page">`), non linking entries wrap with `breadcrumb_nolink_prefix` / suffix, parts separate by `$template_default['breadcrumb_spacer']` (default ` <span class="breadcrumb-spacer">&gt;</span> `).

## Search form placeholders

> Source: `content.func.inc.php` (search_input pass), `include/inc_front/content/cnt13.article.inc.php`

The search content part form uses obfuscated placeholders the cascade rewrites late:

| Placeholder | Replaced by |
| ----------- | ----------- |
| `###search_input_field###` | `search_input_field` — the real input name. |
| `###search_input_value###` | Current search words from the request, the value attribute of the input. |
| `###search_input_action:<article id>###` | URL of the article that carries the search content part; resolves only while that article exists and is active. |

Search result highlighting works with the markers `<!--SEARCH_HIGHLIGHT_START//-->` and `<!--SEARCH_HIGHLIGHT_END//-->` — with a `highlight` GET parameter the text between them gets wrapped by the configured highlight markup, otherwise the markers are removed.

## Other page wide tags

| Tag | Description |
| --- | ----------- |
| `{CURRENT_URL}` | Absolute page URL; only the print/PDF layout template applies it. |
| `[PRINT]…[/PRINT]` | Print link, `print=1`, class `link-print` |
| `[PRINT_PDF]…[/PRINT_PDF]` | PDF link, `print=2`, class `link-print-pdf`; needs `wkhtmltopdf_path` configured. |
| `[BACK]…[/BACK]` | `history.back()` link, class `link-back`; content is the link text. |
| `[LANG:xx]…[/LANG:xx]` | Language split markup, kept for the active frontend language with `lang_parse` enabled; the legacy `[xx]…[/xx]` form works as well. |
| `@@Text@@` | i18n substitution, applied when `i18n_parse` is enabled. |
| `[HTML]…[/HTML]` | Inner text through `html_entities()`. |
| `[HTML_SPECIAL]…[/HTML_SPECIAL]` | Inner text through `html()`. |
| `[IF_CAT:id,id]…[/IF_CAT]` | Keeps inner content when the current level ID matches; `{IF_CAT_ID}` prints the matched ID. |
| `[IF_NOTCAT:id,id]…[/IF_NOTCAT]` | Negated variant; `{IF_NOTCAT_ID}` prints the current level ID. |
| `[LEVEL<n>_ID]…[/LEVEL<n>_ID]` | Level guard tag; `{LEVEL<n>_ID}` resolves to the level ID at depth `n` (root = 0). |
| `{LAZY_LOADING}` | Lazy loading attribute, see [site tags](02-site.md). |
| `{RSSIMG}` | RSS icon, see [RSS](09-rss.md). |
| `{PHPWCMS_RESIZE_IMAGE}` | Image resize path, see [site tags](02-site.md). |
| `{GT:style}text{/GT}` | Deprecated: wraps text in `<span class="gt-style">`; renders only with `gt_mod` enabled. |

## Not present in 2.x

Older documentation lists more tags in this group that have no handler in this code base: `{COUNT_*}`, `{VERSION}`, `{CACHE_*}` and `{EMAIL_*}`. The `{RANDOM:…}` / `{RANDOM_GIF}` / `{RANDOM_JPEG}` / `{RANDOM_PNG}` image tags exist only in the deprecated pass — see [deprecated tags](../deprecated-tags.md).

## Related

- [SHOW_CONTENT](03-show-content.md) — the preferred way to list or embed articles
- [Article tags](04-article.md) — article list pagination fields `{PREV}` / `{NEXT}` / `{NAVI}`

# Template system

> Source: `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/admin.templates.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/admin.pagelayout.tmpl.php`

phpwcms separates layout from content with three independent pieces. You edit them all in the backend admin panel, and every piece has a file based fallback layer under the active `template/` directory.

| Piece | Managed in | Database | File fallback |
| ----- | ---------- | -------- | ------------- |
| **Page layout** | Admin &rarr; Page layout (`p=8`) | `phpwcms_pagelayout` (serialized in `pagelayout_var`) | only through template sections, see below |
| **Layout template** | Admin &rarr; Templates (`p=11`) | `phpwcms_template` (serialized in `template_var`) | `template/inc_settings/template_default/` overrides |
| **Content part template** | selected per content part | filename stored in `acontent_template` | `template/inc_cntpart/<type>/`, then `template/inc_default/` |

## Layout template versus page layout

The layout template holds the editable skeleton of a page: the HTML head extensions, the block texts — header, main, left, right, footer, error — plus classes and settings for tracking, cookie consent and the JavaScript library. All of it serializes into `phpwcms_template.template_var` and arrives in the frontend as the `$block` array.

The page layout defines how the blocks are *assembled*: render mode (table, div, custom), column type, spacing and per-block width or background settings. It serializes into `phpwcms_pagelayout.pagelayout_var` and arrives as `$pagelayout`.

Both are required. If no page layout exists at all the frontend stops with a login notice, because a page cannot be assembled.

## Template fallback chain

### Which layout template is used

| Order | Source |
| ----- | ------ |
| 1 | The template ID assigned to the current structure level (`acat_template`) |
| 2 | The template flagged as default (`template_default = 1`) |
| 3 | Any non-deleted template, ordered `template_default DESC` |

The chain runs in `content.func.inc.php` right after the breadcrumb is built. A copy operation in the template list (`&c=1`) creates a new template row with the same serialized settings.

### Which page layout is used

The chosen template references a page layout by ID (`template_layout`). If the template has none, the page layout flagged `pagelayout_default = 1` is used.

### Which content part template is used

Each content part renderer follows the same three-step chain:

1. The template filename selected in the content part form (`acontent_template`) — loaded from `template/inc_cntpart/<type>/<name>.tmpl` when it exists.
2. The type's default template `template/inc_default/<name>.tmpl` when no template was selected.
3. A hard-coded minimal markup inside the renderer itself, when neither file exists.

Example from the text-with-image renderer `cnt1.article.inc.php`: `inc_default/imagetext.tmpl` &rarr; `inc_cntpart/imagetext/<selected>` &rarr; inline fallback. Type 29 (image div) additionally picks `list.images.tmpl` when the content part runs in list mode. Image special (31) picks `list.imagespecial.tmpl` accordingly.

Content part templates may carry `<!--SECTION_NAME_START//-->…<!--SECTION_NAME_END//-->` blocks that the renderer reads with `get_tmpl_section()`; unneeded sections are stripped with `replace_tmpl_section()`.

## File based template sections

A template can pull each block text from a file instead of the database field. In the template editor, every block offers a file select fed by `template/inc_cntpart/template-sections/`:

| Block field | Directory under `template/inc_cntpart/template-sections/` |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| htmlhead | `head/` |
| header text | `header/` |
| main text | `main/` |
| footer text | `footer/` |
| left text | `left/` |
| right text | `right/` |
| error text | `error/` |

Custom blocks use the lowercase block name as directory (`<customblock>_file`). When the file exists its content replaces the template's block text. This lets you keep template sections in version control.

> **Note:** Serialized templates that still hold a single CSS string (very old rows) are normalized to an array at load time.

## Template default overrides

Two file based override layers can rewrite `$template_default` values (classes, date formats, attributes, tracking snippets, custom fields):

1. The template's `overwrite` select — a file inside `template/inc_settings/template_default/` (`block['overwrite']`).
2. The structure level's overwrite file (`acat_overwrite`), applied after the template one.

Both are filtered against `..` (no path traversal) and included as plain PHP. The template editor lists all `*.php` files in that directory (see [template editor](template-editor.md)).

## Multi-device rendering with render_device

`$phpwcms['render_device']` must be enabled in `config.inc.php` for device markup to work:

`<!--if:condition-->…<!--/if-->` renders its content only when the user agent matches, `<!--!if:condition-->…<!--/!if-->` only when it does not match.

Conditions are `key:value` pairs separated by `;` (OR within one key, AND across keys):

| Key | Values |
| --- | ------ |
| `mobile` | no value — any mobile device |
| `desktop` | no value — any non-mobile device |
| `platform` | WinPhone, WinCE, Win, iOS, Mac, GoogleTV, Android, BlackBerry, WebOS, Linux, Unix, Symbian, Other |
| `device` | Default, Other, Smartphone, Tablet, Desktop, TV |
| `browser` | Other, Firefox, Chrome, Safari, IE, IEMobile, Opera, Mozilla |
| `engine` | Gecko, Other, WebKit, Opera, KHTML |
| `version` | comparison against the browser version, e.g. `>=10`, `<68` |

`render_device()` processes the assembled page twice, once before the replacement cascade and once after the frontend render scripts, so device blocks written by scripts are caught too. The user agent classification comes from `phpwcms_getUserAgent()`.

## Onepage templates

The template editor offers a **onepage** switch (`block['onepage']`). It defines the constant `IS_ONEPAGE_TEMPLATE`, which makes the navigation link levels as `#<alias>` anchors instead of separate URLs — the entire site lives on one page. Per level, `acat_onepage` extends this behavior (see `NAV_LIST_UL` in [the navigation replacement tag](../frontend/replacement-tags/01-nav-list-ul.md)).

## CSS and JavaScript collection

The frontend collects styles and scripts from four sources, all rendered into the page head (or before `</body>` when `$phpwcms['js_in_body']` is on, see [page rendering](../frontend/page-rendering.md)):

1. **Template CSS field** — multi-select of files from `template/inc_css/`; each becomes a `<link rel="stylesheet">` pointing at `TEMPLATE_PATH` + `inc_css/<file>`.
2. **htmlhead block** — free markup the administrator maintains in the template editor; rendered verbatim into `<head>`.
3. **`<!-- JS: … -->` / `<!-- CSS: … -->` comments** — anywhere in the page markup; registered via `renderHeadJS()`/`renderHeadCSS()`, detailed in [assets and libs](assets-and-libs.md).
4. **`$block['custom_htmlhead']`** — array entries appended by renderers and frontend scripts (metas, scripts, links). Scripts without the `head_` key prefix can be moved above the closing body tag by `js_in_body`.

The JavaScript library itself is chosen per template (`template_jslib`); the wrapper file `include/inc_front/lib/js.<lib>.inc.php` then registers the actual `<script>` tags. When no valid library is selected, the fallback `jquery-3.7-migrate-1` wrapper applies. `$block['jslibload']` loads the library on every page, `$block['googleapi']` allows CDN URLs (`PHPWCMS_USE_CDN`), and `$block['frontendjs']` always loads `template/inc_js/frontend.js`.

## Related

- [Layout tags](layout-tags.md) — every tag a layout template understands
- [Template editor](template-editor.md) — the backend forms behind `phpwcms_template` and `phpwcms_pagelayout`
- [Default templates](default-templates.md) — the files in `template/inc_default/`
- [Assets and libs](assets-and-libs.md) — what ships under `template/lib/` and how it loads
