<!-- docs/templates/layout-tags.md -->

# Layout tags

> Source: `include/inc_front/content.func.inc.php`, `include/inc_front/content.article.inc.php`, `index.php`, `include/inc_front/front.func.inc.php`

This page documents the tags available to a **layout template** (block texts plus the custom render markup) and to the print templates. Replacement tags that generate navigation are documented under [NAV_LIST_UL](../frontend/replacement-tags/01-nav-list-ul.md); content part template tags belong to their [content part](../content-parts/index.md) page. Tags work in content parts and custom block texts alike — there is no scoping at the tag level.

Two notations exist:

- `{TAG}` — a replaceable single tag, sometimes with parameters (`{TAG:…}`).
- `[TAG]…[/TAG]` — a conditional section: content stays when the value is non-empty, otherwise the `_ELSE` variant `[TAG_ELSE]…[/TAG_ELSE]` renders. `render_cnt_template()` handles both.

## Content blocks

The block names come from the page layout. The five predefined ones exist on every install; additional blocks are defined by the page layout field *Custom blocks* (comma-separated, uppercase, max 20 characters per name).

| Tag | Filled by |
| --- | --------- |
| `{CONTENT}` | The rendered article stack (list mode or article detail), produced by the content part renderers |
| `{HEADER}` | Content parts assigned to block `HEADER` |
| `{FOOTER}` | Content parts assigned to block `FOOTER` |
| `{LEFT}` | Content parts assigned to block `LEFT` |
| `{RIGHT}` | Content parts assigned to block `RIGHT` |
| `{<CUSTOMBLOCK>}` | Content parts assigned to that custom block |

The template block texts (`headertext`, `footertext`, `lefttext`, `righttext` in the template editor and the `maintext` main text) carry these tags. In table and div render modes the page layout places each block text at its fixed position; if the main text is empty, the rendered article stack takes its place directly. When a block text holds the placeholder (as in `<header>{HEADER}</header>`), assigned content parts land there; when the block text is empty, the raw content parts insert at the pagelayout cell instead. Each block understands the conditional form `[BLOCK]…[/BLOCK]` and `[BLOCK_ELSE]…[/BLOCK_ELSE]` for markup that reacts to empty or filled blocks.

Content parts choose their target block per content part (acontent_block). A content part assigned to a custom block lands in `{<CUSTOMBLOCK>}`; the reserved names `CONTENT`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `HEADER`, `FOOTER`, `CPSET` and `SYSTEM` cannot be defined as custom blocks.

> **Note:** Tags such as `{CONTENT_LEFT}` or `{CONTENT_TOP}` do not exist. Column content uses the plain block names above.

## Page title and meta

There is no `{TITLE}` or `{META}` layout tag. `<title>` and the meta tags are emitted automatically:

- `<title>` is composed by `setPageTitle()` from the page layout's *Pagetitle* field, the level name and the article title, in the order selected per page layout (`layout_title_order`, 15 combinations) joined by the break string (`layout_title_spacer`, default ` | `). An article or level pagetitle field overrides the composition.
- `meta description` — auto-filled from the level's description when none exists in the htmlhead, else from `article_description`.
- `meta keywords` — auto-collected from article and level keywords; `*CSS-class*` tokens are stripped first.
- canonical link — see [URL handling](../general/url-handling.md#canonical-handling).

## Current page context

| Tag | Value |
| --- | ----- |
| `{CURRENT_ARTICLEID}` | Current article ID, `0` in list mode |
| `{CURRENT_CATEGORYID}` | Current structure level ID |
| `{LEVEL<n>_ID}` / `[LEVEL<n>_ID]…[/LEVEL<n>_ID]` | Structure level ID at breadcrumb depth `<n>` (0 = root); the bracket form keeps content only when the level exists |
| `[IF_CAT:id,id,…]…[/IF_CAT]`, `{IF_CAT_ID}` | Keeps content when the current level matches one of the IDs; `{IF_CAT_ID}` holds the matching ID |
| `[IF_NOTCAT:id,id,…]…[/IF_NOTCAT]`, `{IF_NOTCAT_ID}` | Keeps content when the current level matches none of the IDs |

## Site paths

| Tag | Value |
| --- | ----- |
| `{SITE}` | Absolute site URL including installation folder (`PHPWCMS_URL`) |
| `{SITE_URL}` | Host name in mail and system contexts (`PHPWCMS_HOST`); in page markup use `{SITE}` |
| `{TEMPLATE}` | Relative template directory path (`TEMPLATE_PATH`) |
| `{PHPWCMS_URL}`, `{PHPWCMS_TEMPLATE}` | Aliases of the two above, also active in mail text and non-cached strings via `replaceGlobalRT()` |
| `{LAZY_LOADING}` | `loading="lazy" decoding="async"` or empty, per `$phpwcms['lazy_loading']` |
| `{PHPWCMS_RESIZE_IMAGE}` | `img/cmsimage.php`, or `im` when URL rewriting is on |

## PHP and custom code

| Tag | Behavior |
| --- | -------- |
| `{PHP:<file-or-url>}` | Includes a PHP script and returns its buffered output; local paths must stay inside `PHPWCMS_ROOT`, remote URLs additionally need `$phpwcms['allow_remote_URL']` |
| `[PHP]code[/PHP]` | Evaluates a PHP code block — `eval`, `exec`, `system` and similar functions are forbidden and return a comment placeholder |
| `{PHPVAR:var}` | Returns a global variable value; `$phpwcms` access is masked out |

All three require `$phpwcms['enable_inline_php']` in `config.inc.php`; otherwise `render_PHPcode()` strips them with `remove_unsecure_rptags()`. Inside content parts the pair `$phpwcms['allow_cntPHP_rt']` and `$phpwcms['enable_inline_php']` decides whether rendered content keeps PHP tags. The `[PHP]…[/PHP]` form runs early in the replacement cascade, so its output becomes page markup. See also `$content['globalRT']`: a [frontend render script](../frontend/frontend-scripts.md) may register custom global tags which `html_parser()` then replaces in one pass.

## Navigation and structure

| Tag | Purpose |
| --- | ------- |
| `{NAV_LIST_UL:…}` | Primary ul/li navigation — full parameter reference under [NAV_LIST_UL](../frontend/replacement-tags/01-nav-list-ul.md) |
| `{BREADCRUMB}`, `{BREADCRUMB:<depth>}`, `{BREADCRUMB:<depth>,<flag>}` | Breadcrumb path from the level tree; `<flag>` = 1 shows the current page as plain text |
| `[PRINT]…[/PRINT]` | Anchor to the print view of the current page, class `link-print` |
| `[PRINT_PDF]…[/PRINT_PDF]` | Anchor to the PDF view (needs `wkhtmltopdf_path`), class `link-print-pdf` |
| `{SOCIAL_SHARE}` / `{SOCIAL_SHARE:options}` | Social share links rendered by `render_social_share()` |
| `{RSSIMG}` | Default RSS icon defined in `conf.template_default.inc.php` |

## Dates and times

| Tag | Value |
| --- | ----- |
| `{DATE_LONG}`, `{DATE_MEDIUM}`, `{DATE_SHORT}` | Current date in the formats from `conf.template_default.inc.php` |
| `{DATE_ARTICLE}` | Article date, short format |
| `{TIME_LONG}`, `{TIME_SHORT}` | Current time; `{TIME_ARTICLE}` article time |
| `{DATE:<format>}`, `{NOW:<format>}` | Any PHP `date()` format, optionally `SET:<timestamp>` |
| `{LIVEDATE:<format>}`, `{KILLDATE:<format>}` | Article start/end date, section forms `[LIVEDATE]…[/LIVEDATE]` apply |
| `{AUTHOR}` | Article author name, or level related fallback |
| `{CATEGORY}` | Current level name |

## Content selection

| Tag | Purpose |
| --- | ------- |
| `{SHOW_CONTENT:MODE,parameter[,parameter…]}` | Pulls articles or content parts into any block. Modes: `AS`, `ASL*`/`AST*` sort variants (livedate/killdate/change/keyword, `D` suffix = descending, `R` = random), `CP` (by content part IDs), `CPS`, `CPC`, `CPAD`/`CPAS`/`CPASD`. Optional `AS:<count>|<list template>` form |
| `{RELATED:<count>}`, `{RELATED:<count>:<opts>}` | Articles sharing the current article's keywords |
| `{NEW:<count>:<start>}` | Newest articles, sorted per `template_default['news']['sort_by']` |
| `{KEYWORD:<keywords>}` | Turns a keyword list into links to matching articles |
| `{URL:<url>}[,CACHE=<seconds>]` | Includes the `<body>` of an external HTML page; with a trailing space and `CACHE=` seconds the result caches under `content/tmp/` |
| `{BROWSE:UP:<text>}`, `{BROWSE:NEXT:<text>,<catdown>}`, `{BROWSE:PREV:<text>,<catup>}` | Links to the parent level / next article / previous article |

## Search form markers

Hand-built search forms use three markers, replaced by `get_search_action()`:

| Marker | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| `###search_input_field###` | Passthrough identifier of the text field |
| `###search_input_value###` | Current search word, if any |
| `###search_input_action:<article-id>###` | Form action pointing at the search article |

## Print mode sections

`?print=1` (HTML) and `?print=2` (PDF) switch the template: `template/inc_default/print.tmpl` or `pdf.tmpl` (or `{CONTENT}<hr/>{CURRENT_URL}` when the file is missing). Both understand `{CONTENT}` and `{CURRENT_URL}`; the PDF template may hold a `[PDF_SETTINGS]…[/PDF_SETTINGS]` INI section parsed by `parse_ini_str()` before `wkhtmltopdf` runs. The result then flows through the regular replacement cascade, so page level tags apply to print output as well.

| Section | Effect |
| ------- | ------ |
| `[NO_PRINT]…[/NO_PRINT]` | Removed in print/PDF output, neutral markup comment otherwise |
| `[PDF_SETTINGS]…[/PDF_SETTINGS]` | INI options for `wkhtmltopdf`, PDF only |

## Login state sections

| Section | Effect |
| ------- | ------ |
| `[LOGGED_IN]…[/LOGGED_IN]` | Content only for logged in frontend users |
| `[LOGGED_OUT]…[/LOGGED_OUT]` | Content only for anonymous visitors |

There are no `{LOGIN_*}` layout tags. The frontend login form is a content part (28, FE Login) with its own `LOGIN_FORM` templates under `template/inc_cntpart/felogin/`, and `template/inc_script/felogin/` provides an ini-driven variant including the `{FELOGIN_USER}`, `{FELOGOUT_PREFIX}` and `{FELOGOUT_SUFFIX}` tags inside its own templates.

## List mode, pagination and error sections

| Section / tag | Effect |
| ------------- | ------ |
| `[IF_LIST_MODE]…[/IF_LIST_MODE]` | Content only while the level renders an article list |
| `[ELSE_LIST_MODE]…[/ELSE_LIST_MODE]` | Content only in article detail mode |
| `[404]…[/404]` | Error block content when a 404 was detected |
| `[404_ELSE]…[/404_ELSE]` | Error block content when the page renders with no content |
| `{CP_PAGINATE}` | Page numbers `[1][2][3]` of the content part pagination, wrapped per `template_default['attributes']['cp-paginate']` |
| `[CP_PAGINATE_PREV]`, `[CP_PAGINATE_NEXT]` | Hold the previous/next page URL when one exists |
| `[CP_PAGINATE_MENU]`, `[CP_PAGINATE_MENU:first|last|active|hide|wrap…]` | Title menu of the paginated content parts |
| `[CP_PAGINATE]…[/CP_PAGINATE]` | Wraps the pagination list; the START/END comments are stripped when pagination is inactive |

## Head injection comments

Anywhere in template or content:

```
<!-- JS: jquery.ui.slider -->
<!-- JS: https://cdn.example.com/widget.js -->
<!-- JS: ready| jQuery(".gallery").glightbox(); -->
<!-- CSS: my-extension.css -->
<!-- CSS: body{margin:0} -->
```

- A name without extension loads `template/lib/jquery/plugin/jquery.<name>.js` via `initJSPlugin()`.
- A `.js` file or `http(s)://`/`//` URL links as external script; `{TEMPLATE}` inside is replaced first.
- A name known to the installed JS library (e.g. jQuery plugins of `template/lib/jquery/plugin/`) loads through the lib wrapper.
- `ready`, `domready` or `onload` followed by code executes the code on DOM ready (jQuery wrapped when the code uses `$()` or `jQuery()`).
- Inline JavaScript without a `ready` prefix is emitted into the head once per unique code.
- CSS with a `.css` extension links as external stylesheet; everything else becomes an inline `<style>` block.

## Language blocks

With `$phpwcms['lang_parse']` and `$phpwcms['allowed_lang']`:

- `[LANG:de]…[/LANG:de]` and the legacy `[de]…[/de]` keep content for the active frontend language and strip it otherwise.
- `@@Text@@` tokens resolve against the language translation tables when `$phpwcms['i18n_parse']` is on.

## Deprecated tags

`{NAV_ROW}`, `{NAV_LIST}`, `{NAV_LIST_TOP}`, `{NAV_LIST_CURRENT}`, `{NAV_TABLE_SIMPLE}`, `{NAV_TABLE_COLUMN}`, `{RANDOM}`, `{IMAGE}`-family and `{GT:…}` render only with `$phpwcms['enable_deprecated']` or `$phpwcms['gt_mod']` — inventory in [deprecated tags](../frontend/deprecated-tags.md).

## Replacement order

The tags above are processed in a fixed sequence, not alphabetically. The exact top-to-bottom cascade lives in [page rendering](../frontend/page-rendering.md#replacement-cascade).

## Related

- [Template system](template-system.md)
- [Default templates](default-templates.md)

<!-- docs/templates/template-editor.md -->

# Template editor

> Source: `include/inc_tmpl/admin.pagelayout.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/admin.templates.tmpl.php`, `include/inc_act/act_frontendsetup.php`

Both editors live under **Admin** in the backend. Deleting happens through `include/inc_act/act_frontendsetup.php`: `?do=1|<id>` removes a page layout, `?do=2|<id>` removes a template. The template list also offers a copy action (`&c=1`). Every save runs `update_cache()`.

## Page layout editor (p=8)

Defines how the page blocks assemble. Saved serialized into `phpwcms_pagelayout.pagelayout_var` with the name in `pagelayout_name`.

> Source: `include/inc_tmpl/admin.pagelayout.tmpl.php` (POST branch lines 68-212)

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| Name | text | auto timestamp name | List label |
| Default | checkbox | off | Only one page layout may carry the flag; saving clears it on all others |
| Render | radio: custom / table / div | custom (2) | Assembly mode — custom (2) uses the template's block texts as-is, table (0) and div (1) wrap header/left/content/right/footer into classic structure |
| Custom blocks | text | empty | Comma separated block names, uppercased, spaces normalized, max 20 chars each; `CONTENT`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `HEADER`, `FOOTER`, `CPSET`, `SYSTEM` are rejected |
| Pagetitle | text | `Pagetitle` | Base page title |
| Add to title | select | pagetitle, category, articlename | Title composition order, 15 options including short forms (value 0-14, see `setPageTitle()`) |
| Break | text | ` \| ` | Spacer between title parts |
| Align / margin / background / link colors / onload | text or radio | empty | Only used by the table and div render modes; hidden behind a jQuery toggle when render mode is custom |
| Column type | radio: 4-, 3-, 2-, 1-column | 3-column style (0) | Which of left/right blocks the table/div layout renders |
| Width/color/background/class per block | text | empty | Fields for *all blocks*, left, left space, main (content), right space, right, header, top space, bottom space, footer |

All block dimensions accept pixel or percent values (`get_pix_or_percent()`). The background fields of the top area exist only for the classic render modes.

## Template editor (p=11)

Defines the content of blocks plus behavior. Saved serialized into `phpwcms_template.template_var`. A `&c=1` copy pre-fills the form with a suffixed name.

### Base

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| Name | text | random if empty | List label |
| Set as default | checkbox | off | Used when a structure level has no template |
| Page layout | select | first entry | Which page layout assembles the block; changing it with block-relevant differences triggers a confirm warning (`doPageLayoutChange()`) |
| Onepage | switch | off | Sets `IS_ONEPAGE_TEMPLATE`, see [template system](template-system.md) |
| Overwrite | select | empty | PHP file from `template/inc_settings/template_default/` that overrides `$template_default` values |

### CSS and login URL

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| CSS | multi-select | empty | Files from `template/inc_css/`, rendered as `<link>` tags in page order |
| Frontend login URL | text | site URL | Redirect target for regonly levels; `{SITE}` inside is replaced by the site URL, otherwise `$template_default['login_form_url']` applies |

### Blocks

Each block is a code textarea with mode-dependent height: header, main, left, right, footer, plus every custom block declared in the page layout, plus the error block. Every block additionally offers a file select listing `template/inc_cntpart/template-sections/<dir>/` (see [template sections](template-system.md#file-based-template-sections)). The file content wins over the textarea content.

The error block understands the `[404]…[/404]` and `[404_ELSE]…[/404_ELSE]` sections.

### HTML head and JavaScript

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| htmlhead | textarea | empty | Markup emitted into `<head>` verbatim (metas, links, scripts) |
| JavaScript library | select | first of `$phpwcms['js_lib_default']` | Wrapper from `include/inc_front/lib/js.<name>.inc.php`; invalid values fall back to the `jquery-3.7-migrate-1` wrapper |
| Load library permanently | checkbox | off | `jslibload` — calls `initJSLib()` on every page |
| Use CDN | checkbox | on | `googleapi`/`use_cdn` — sets `PHPWCMS_USE_CDN` |
| onload | text | empty | Comma semicolon list of JS calls merged into the DomReady block |
| frontend.js | checkbox | off | Always loads `template/inc_js/frontend.js` |

### Tracking

Google Analytics (gtag.js), Google Tag Manager and Matomo/Piwik each carry an enable switch plus ID fields; none render without a matching ID. GA options: anonymize IP, show optout script, cookie flags, custom properties as a JS object snippet. Piwik needs a host URL without scheme plus site ID. Trackings respect `$phpwcms['donottrack']` cookie consent state.

### Cookie consent

Two variants, the 2.x v3 flavor (orestbida) wins when both are on:

| Group | Fields |
| ----- | ------ |
| v2 | message, dismiss, more, link + target, theme (files `template/lib/cookieconsent2/`) |
| v3 | enable, reload on change, texts (title, description, accept all, accept necessary, accept selected, reject all, customize, more, link), theme, consent and preferences modal layout/position/button options, per-category sections `general`, `necessary`, `functionality`, `analytics`, `marketing`, `social`, `more` with active flag, title and description |

Translations load from `template/lib/cookieconsent3/lang/<lang>.json` with English fallback.

Additionally: *Do not track* respect (`block['donottrack']`, evaluates the browser DNT header) and *Require consent* (block rendering of scripts until the consent cookie named under the given name/value exists).

## Storage and caching

Both editors write a serialized PHP array. The template editor merges loaded values with `array_replace_recursive()` over the defaults above, so newly added option keys survive upgrades of old data rows. Single legacy CSS strings are normalized to arrays on load. Saving also updates the backend cache (`update_cache()`), so list views and structure forms see the change immediately.

- [Default templates](default-templates.md)

# Default templates

> Source: `template/inc_default/`, renderers in `include/inc_front/content/`, `include/inc_front/content.article.inc.php`, `verify.php`

Directory `template/inc_default/` ships one working template per feature plus the print templates and the backend dashboard snippet. Renderers use these files as step two of the [template fallback chain](template-system.md#which-content-part-template-is-used): when a content part has no template selected, the default ships; when the selected file is missing, the hard-coded fallback in the renderer applies.

All files are plain text templates read with `file_get_contents()` and processed with section markers and content part tags — they run as data, not as code (the single `startup.php` below is the exception, included by the backend).

## Content part defaults

| File | Used by | Notes |
| ---- | ------- | ----- |
| `plaintext.tmpl` | CP 0 — Plain text | Loaded from `cnt0.article.inc.php` |
| `imagetext.tmpl` | CP 1 — Text with image | |
| `imagetable.tmpl` | CP 2 — Image table | |
| `bulletlist.tmpl` | CP 4 — Bullet list | |
| `linklist.tmpl` | CP 5 — Link list | |
| `html.tmpl` | CP 6 — HTML | |
| `multimedia.tmpl` | CP 9 — Multimedia | |
| `code.tmpl` | CP 11 — Code | |
| `search.tmpl` | CP 13 — Search | |
| `wysiwyg.tmpl` | CP 14 — WYSIWYG | |
| `guestbook.tmpl` | CP 18 — Guestbook | |
| `flashplayer.tmpl` | CP 25 — Flash player | |
| `rssfeed.tmpl` | CP 22 — RSS feed | Consumer of external feeds, template section `FEEDINFO`/`FEED` loop |
| `tabs.tmpl` | CP 32 — Tabs | |
| `teaser.tmpl` | CP 8 — Article menu (teaser) | Detail mode template |
| `list.teaser.tmpl` | CP 8 — Article menu (teaser) | List mode variant, loaded when `acontent_template_listmode` is set |
| `news.tmpl` | CP 33 — News | October 2025 reworked default |
| `reference.tmpl` | CP 50 — Reference | |

CP 29 (image div) and CP 31 (image special) share two defaults:

| File | Used by |
| ---- | ------- |

| `list.images.tmpl` | CP 29 and CP 31, list mode |
| `imagespecial.tmpl` | CP 31 — Image special |

## Article summary defaults

| File | Used by | Notes |
| ---- | ------- | ----- |
| `article_summary.tmpl` | Full article header on article pages | Loaded by `content.article.inc.php` when the article has no custom full template |
| `article_summary_paginate.tmpl` | Article pages with content part pagination | Used when the article is paginated and the selected template also has a paginate variant |
| `article_summary_list.tmpl` | Article list entries | Loaded by `list_articles_summary()` in `front.func.inc.php` when neither the level nor the caller provides a list template |

The summary templates carry the shared article tags `[TITLE]`/`{TITLE}`, `[SUB]`/`{SUB}`, `[EDITOR]`, `[SUMMARY]`, `[MORE]`, `[CLASS]`, `[SYSTEM]`, the `[IMAGE]` section with `{IMAGE_*}` placeholders, `[CAPTION]`, `[COPYRIGHT]`, `[ZOOMIMAGE]`, `[IMAGE_URL]`, `[IMAGE_TARGET]` and the date tags `{DATE:…}`, `{LIVEDATE:…}`, `{KILLDATE:…}`.

## Print and output defaults

| File | Used by | Notes |
| ---- | ------- | ----- |
| `print.tmpl` | `?print=1` | Wraps `{CONTENT}` plus `{CURRENT_URL}`, may hold `[NO_PRINT]` sections |
| `pdf.tmpl` | `?print=2` | Same plus `[PDF_SETTINGS]` INI section parsed before `wkhtmltopdf` runs |

## Newsletter defaults

| File | Used by | Notes |
| ---- | ------- | ----- |
| `subscribe.tmpl` | `verify.php?s=<hash>` | Double opt-in confirmation page, `{EMAIL}` and global RTs are replaced |
| `unsubscribe.tmpl` | `verify.php?u=<hash>` | Unsubscribe confirmation page, same replacements |

The subscription content part (CP 12) renders its form inline and does not load a file from this directory.

## Backend default

| File | Used by | Notes |
| ---- | ------- | ----- |
| `startup.php` | Backend dashboard (`phpwcms.php` start and news screens) | PHP template; renders the support/Impressum card configured under `$phpwcms['support']` |

## Unreferenced file

`custom.tmpl` ships in the directory but no renderer references it — customizable content parts use the templates under `template/inc_cntpart/custom/` instead (see [template system](template-system.md#which-content-part-template-is-used)).

# Assets and libs

> Source: `template/lib/`, `include/inc_js/`, `include/inc_front/js.inc.php`, `include/inc_front/lib/js.jquery.default.php`, `include/build/build-css.js`, `include/build/build-js.js`

## template/lib/

Libraries a template's markup or settings pull in. Everything under `template/lib/` belongs to the template distribution, not the core.

| Directory | Purpose | Loaded by |
| --------- | ------- | --------- |
| `bootstrap5/` | Bootstrap CSS and bundle JS | `<!-- JS: … -->`/`<!-- CSS: … -->` comments or htmlhead markup |
| `bootstrap-icons/` | Icon font CSS plus fonts | template markup |
| `cookieconsent2/` | Silktide consent scripts and themes | Template setting *Cookie consent v2* — the theme field names a CSS file in this directory, loaded with CDN fallback to cdnjs 1.0.10 | 
| `cookieconsent3/` | orestbida `CookieConsent.run()` assets, components CSS and `lang/<lang>.json` translations | Template setting *Cookie consent v3*; CDN variant pulls jsdelivr 3.1.0 |
| `glightbox/` | Lightbox | `initGlightbox()` (article summary and image lightboxes), options via `$phpwcms['glightbox_options']` |
| `jquery/` | One minified jQuery per version, 1.3.2 through 4.0.0 plus migrate builds and `plugin/` | Selected by the template's JS library setting |
| `jquery/plugin/` | Standalone jQuery plugins: cycle, dimensions, easing, fancybox, mousewheel, switchClass, zebra_accordion | `<!-- JS: <name> -->` for any `jquery.<name>.js` file |
| `simplegmaps/` | Google Maps wrapper | Content part templates load it via a `<!-- JS:{TEMPLATE}lib/simplegmaps/simplegmaps.min.js -->` comment, e.g. `template/inc_cntpart/tabs/simplegmaps.tmpl` |
| `splide/` | Slider | Content part templates reference it through `<!-- CSS: template/lib/splide/splide.min.css -->` and `<!-- JS: template/lib/splide/splide.min.js -->`, e.g. `template/inc_cntpart/images/Splide-Slider-Single-Image.tmpl` |
| `video-js/` | video.js player | `initVideoJs()` for multimedia content parts; falls back to the CDN `vjs.zencdn.net/8.24.0/` unless `template/lib/video-js/video.min.js` exists or `$phpwcms['video-js']` sets a path |

## include/inc_js/

Core frontend scripts served from the include tree:

| File | Purpose |
| ---- | ------- |
| `phpwcms.js` / `phpwcms.min.js` | phpwcms own frontend helper code (minified via build) |
| `bootstrap.bundle.min.js` | Backend-side copy of the Bootstrap bundle |
| `dropzone.min.js`, `exif.min.js`, `flatpickr.min.css/.js` | Upload and date picker assets for backend forms |
| `dayjs.min.js` + `dayjs-locale/` | Date handling in the backend |
| `jquery/jquery-3.7.1.min.js` | Backend jQuery |
| `ace/` | Ace code editor used by the template and code editors in the backend |

`template/inc_js/` is the template-side counterpart: `frontend.js` (loaded by `initFrontendJS()`, the template *frontend.js* switch or the legacy `frontend.js` detection) and `imagezoom.js` for the click-zoom image popup.

## The <!-- JS: --> and <!-- CSS: --> convention

`renderHeadJS()` and `renderHeadCSS()` handle both comment markers, wherever they appear in template, block or content markup:

| Argument | Result |
| -------- | ------ |
| `<name>` without extension | `initJSLib()` plus `initJSPlugin('<name>')` → loads `template/lib/jquery/plugin/jquery.<name>.js` |
| `initJSLib` | Loads only the selected base library |
| `file.js` | External `<script>` from the template path; `{TEMPLATE}` inside the path is resolved first |
| `https://…`, `//…` | External `<script>` from the remote URL |
| `ready|<code>`, `domready|<code>`, `onload|<code>` | Inline script executed on DOM ready; jQuery wrapped when the code uses `$()` or `jQuery()` |
| `<code>` | Inline script emitted once per unique code into `<head>` |
| CSS argument ending `.css` | External stylesheet link, relative to the template path |
| CSS argument with a `.` but no `.css` or plain rule text | Inline `<style>` block, emitted once per unique code |

All entries land in the shared array `$block['custom_htmlhead']` keyed by MD5, so repeated tags emit one tag only.

## JS library wrappers

The template's JS library setting selects one wrapper file, loaded as `include/inc_front/lib/js.` + name + `.inc.php`. `$phpwcms['js_lib_default']` merged in `default.inc.php` defines jQuery 1.4 through 4.0, each with `-migrate`, `-migrate-1` and `-slim` variants; `$phpwcms['js_lib_deprecated']` extends the list when deprecated rendering is on. `js.jquery.inc.php` (a legacy alias) and `js.jquery.default.php` (shared plugin/loader functions, e.g. `initJSPlugin()` and the `initSlimbox()` alias for `initGlightbox()`) are included by every wrapper.

An invalid library name falls back to the `jquery-3.7-migrate-1` wrapper. `PHPWCMS_USE_CDN` (template checkbox plus `$block['jslib']` wrapper) switches local copies to jquery.com/googleapis URLs.

## Build managed files

`npm run build` (scripts `build:css`, `build:js` in `package.json`) regenerates shipped third party assets from `node_modules`:

- `include/build/build-js.js` — terser-minifies `include/inc_js/phpwcms.js`, copies Bootstrap bundle, Dropzone, Flatpickr, dayjs, jQuery 3.7.1, video.js, GLightbox and vanilla-cookieconsent into their destinations, syncs the Ace editor subset into `include/inc_js/ace/` and applies patched minification to the legacy cookieconsent2 script.
- `include/build/build-css.js` — copies Bootstrap, Bootstrap Icons, Dropzone, Flatpickr, Tom Select, Font Awesome solid, video.js, GLightbox and cookieconsent3 CSS.

Destinations include both `include/inc_js/` (backend) and `template/lib/` (frontend). Do not hand-edit these copies — edit the npm dependency set and rebuild. `cookieconsent2/cookieconsent.min.js` is pinned by the build script rather than synced from a current node_modules package.

## Editor libraries

The backend WYSIWYG editors load per `$phpwcms['wysiwyg_editor']` from `include/inc_lib/wysiwyg.editor.inc.php`:

| Value | Editor | Asset location |
| ----- | ------ | -------------- |
| 0 | none | textarea only |
| 1 | CKEditor (legacy) | `include/inc_ext/ckeditor/` (CKEditor 4.22.1 LTS line), configs in `template/config/ckeditor/` |
| 2 | TinyMCE 8 | `include/vendor/tinymce/tinymce/`, translations from `include/vendor/mklkj/tinymce-i18n/langs/` |

They are backend-only; frontend pages never include them. The legacy swfobject loader (`initSwfObject()`) still exists for old multimedia content parts and looks for `template/lib/swfobject/swfobject.js`.

<!-- docs/content-parts/index.md -->

# Content parts

> Source: `include/inc_lib/article.contenttype.inc.php`, `include/inc_front/content.article.inc.php`, `include/inc_lib/modules.check.inc.php`

A [content part](../general/concepts.md) is one functional block inside an article: a text with image, an image gallery, a teaser list, a form, a search and so on. Every article is a stack of content parts; the stack is what the frontend renders into the `{CONTENT}` slot of the page layout. Editors add, order, group and hide content parts in the article detail view of the backend.

## How the stack renders

The frontend dispatch lives in `include/inc_front/content.article.inc.php`. For the current article it selects the content part rows from `phpwcms_articlecontent`:

```sql
SELECT * FROM phpwcms_articlecontent
WHERE acontent_aid = <article id>
  AND acontent_visible = 1 AND acontent_trash = 0
  AND (acontent_livedate IS NULL OR acontent_livedate < NOW())
  AND (acontent_killdate IS NULL OR acontent_killdate > NOW())
  AND acontent_granted = 0        -- anonymous: = 0, logged in: != 2
ORDER BY acontent_sorting, acontent_id
```

So the order is the sort value `acontent_sorting`, set per content part in the backend (the up/down arrows swap two rows' sort values), then the row ID for ties. A content part renders only when it is visible, not trashed, inside its live/kill date window and its frontend permission (`acontent_granted`) matches the login state of the visitor.

Each row is then rendered by its own renderer (see [file layout](#file-layout)) into a temporary buffer. The dispatcher wraps every part with optional pieces before adding it to the output:

| Feature | Behavior |
| ------- | -------- |
| Anchor | `acontent_anchor` emits `<a id="cpid<N>"></a>` with the row's ID as `N` so the part is link-targetable. |
| Spacing | `acontent_before` / `acontent_after` emit spacer CSS classes or `div` wrappers. |
| Content block | `acontent_block` = `CONTENT` (default) appends to the main output; any other value renders into a block slot defined by the layout template instead. |
| Tabs / groups | `acontent_tab` folds the part into a tab box or accordion group assembled after the loop. |
| Pagination | With article pagination enabled, `acontent_paginate_page` selects which article page the part belongs to. |
| Alias | Type 24 replaces its own row with the referenced content part before rendering. |
| `[%CPID%]` / `{CPID}` | Replaced with the DB row ID in the rendered output of every part. |
| Top link | `acontent_top` adds a back-to-top link. |

> **Note:** The layout template can additionally fill `[SYSTEM]` blocks with content parts assigned to the `SYSTEM` block; those parts are only rendered when the layout template requests them.

## Content part types

Types are identified by `acontent_type` and mapped to backend labels in `$wcs_content_type` (`include/inc_lib/article.contenttype.inc.php`); English labels come from `include/inc_lang/backend/en/lang.inc.php`.

| ID | Backend label | Reference |
| -- | ------------- | --------- |
| 0 | Plain text | [Plain text](00-plaintext.md) |
| 1 | Text w/image | [Text w/image](01-text-with-image.md) |
| 2 | Images | [Images](09-images.md) |

| 100 | List | [ul-list](06-list-ul.md) |

- IDs are historical and not consecutive; unlisted IDs belong to removed types. The table itself is ordered by ID, but the backend select lists types alphabetically by label by default (`$phpwcms['cnt_sort'] = 'a-z'` in `include/config/dist.conf.inc.php`; `z-a` reverses it, empty keeps the definition order of the array).
- Labels 4 and 100 are both "List": ID 4 converts lines to a simple `<ul>` (template driven), ID 100 builds nested `<ul>`/`<ol>`/`<dl>` markup from `~` indent markers.
- Type 30 is reserved for modules; see below.

## Module content parts (type 30)

Modules can provide their own content part. A module advertises this by setting `$_module_contentpart = true` in its `module.default.php`; registration happens in `include/inc_lib/modules.check.inc.php`, which stores the flag as `$phpwcms['modules'][<module>]['cntp']`.

When at least one active module registers a content part, the content part select gains the entry **Plug-in** (ID 30). A row of type 30 stores the module name in `acontent_module` and renders through the module instead of the standard renderer:

- Frontend render: `<module dir>/inc/cnt.article.php`
- Backend dialog: `<module dir>/inc/cnt.form.php`
- Submitted values: `<module dir>/inc/cnt.post.php`

The row is only rendered while its module stays enabled. Module-provided types are documented with their module, see the [modules reference](../modules/index.md).

## File layout

Every content part type consists of a small, predictable set of files, numbered by its ID:

| File | Role |
| ---- | ---- |
| `include/inc_lib/content/cnt<N>.readform.inc.php` | Reads the submitted dialog fields from `$_POST` into `$content`. Shared fields (title, spacing, dates, block, …) are handled first in `include/inc_lib/article.readform.inc.php`. |
| `include/inc_lib/content/cnt<N>.sql.inc.php` | Builds the `UPDATE phpwcms_articlecontent …` column assignments. |
| `include/inc_lib/content/cnt<N>.takeval.inc.php` | Repopulates `$content` from the DB row when the dialog opens for editing. |
| `include/inc_tmpl/content/cnt<N>.inc.php` | The type-specific section of the backend dialog; included by `include/inc_tmpl/articlecontent.edit.tmpl.php`. |
| `include/inc_tmpl/content/cnt<N>.list.inc.php` | The one-line summary shown for this part in the article's content part list. |
| `include/inc_front/content/cnt<N>.article.inc.php` | The frontend renderer. |

A type without one of these files falls back: the dialog uses `cnt0.inc.php`/`cnt0.list.inc.php` and the submit handler `cnt0.readform.inc.php`.

### Template resolution

Where a content part supports templates, its renderer resolves in this order:

1. The file selected in the dialog, from `template/inc_cntpart/<type>/<name>.tmpl`.
2. The shipped default from `template/inc_default/<name>.tmpl`.
3. A built-in skeleton hard-coded in the renderer.

Custom templates live under `template/inc_cntpart/`; each backend dialog lists the files of the matching subdirectory. Available shipped default templates:

```text
template/inc_default/
article_summary.tmpl          article_summary_list.tmpl     article_summary_paginate.tmpl
bulletlist.tmpl               code.tmpl                     custom.tmpl
filelist.tmpl                 filelist_inline.tmpl          flashplayer.tmpl
guestbook.tmpl                html.tmpl                     images.tmpl
imagespecial.tmpl             imagetable.tmpl               imagetext.tmpl
linklist.tmpl                 list.images.tmpl              list.imagespecial.tmpl
list.teaser.tmpl              multimedia.tmpl               news.tmpl
pdf.tmpl                      plaintext.tmpl                print.tmpl
reference.tmpl                rssfeed.tmpl                  search.tmpl
startup.php                   subscribe.tmpl                tabs.tmpl
teaser.tmpl                   unsubscribe.tmpl              wysiwyg.tmpl
```

Available custom template directories:

```text
template/inc_cntpart/
articlesummary/   bulletlist/   code/         custom/       faq/
felogin/          filelist/     flashplayer/  guestbook/    html/
images/           imagespecial/ imagetable/   imagetext/    linkemail/
linklist/         map/          multimedia/   news/         newsletter/
plaintext/        recipe/       reference/    rssfeed/      search/
tabs/             teaser/       template-sections/  wysiwyg/
```

> **Note:** `articlesummary/` and `template-sections/` do not belong to a content part type; they hold article summary and layout section templates.

## Reference

Every type has its own page with backend form, rendering, storage and related links. The table under [Content part types](#content-part-types) links them all.

---

<!-- docs/content-parts/00-plaintext.md -->

# Plain text (content part 0)

> Source: `include/inc_lib/content/cnt0.readform.inc.php`, `include/inc_lib/content/cnt0.sql.inc.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/content/cnt0.inc.php`, `include/inc_front/content/cnt0.article.inc.php`

A text block edited without a rich text editor: plain text in, formatted HTML out. Rendering applies one of three text formats — plain, Markdown or Textile — selected per content part.

## Backend form

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| Template | select | *(empty = default)* | Content part template from `template/inc_cntpart/plaintext/`. Empty uses the shipped default. |
| Format | radio buttons | Plain text | Output format: "Plain text", MarkDown or Textile. Invalid values fall back to Plain text. |
| Plain text | textarea, 12 rows | — | The text. Edits in a plain code editor (Ace) whose syntax mode follows the selected format: `text`, `markdown` or `textile`. Stored exactly as typed, without trimming. |

## Rendering

### Template selection

Renderer order: selected file from `template/inc_cntpart/plaintext/<name>.tmpl`, else `template/inc_default/plaintext.tmpl`, else this built-in skeleton:

```html
[TITLE]<h4>{TITLE}</h4>[/TITLE]
[SUBTITLE]<h5>{SUBTITLE}</h5>[/SUBTITLE]
[TEXT]<p>{TEXT}</p>[/TEXT]
```

The shipped default `template/inc_default/plaintext.tmpl` wraps title and subtitle in `h3`/`h4` and outputs the text unwrapped:

```html
[TITLE]<h3>{TITLE}</h3>[/TITLE]
[SUBTITLE]<h4>{SUBTITLE}</h4>[/SUBTITLE]
[TEXT]{TEXT}[/TEXT]
```

### Template tags

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | ------- |
| `[ATTR_CLASS]…[/ATTR_CLASS]` | Present when the wrapper class field is set; `{ATTR_CLASS}` prints its value. `[ATTR_CLASS_ELSE]` marks the branch without class. |
| `[ATTR_ID]…[/ATTR_ID]` | Same mechanism for the wrapper `id` (`{ATTR_ID}`). |
| `{TITLE}` / `{SUBTITLE}` | Content part title / subtitle, HTML-escaped. |
| `[TEXT]…[/TEXT]` / `{TEXT}` | The formatted text. Removed when empty. |
| `{ID}` | Content part record ID. |

### Text conversion

| Format | Renderer |
| ------ | -------- |
| Plain text | `plaintext_htmlencode()`: single line breaks become `<br />`, blank lines separate `<p>` paragraphs, HTML is escaped, basic BBCode renders (`[b]`, `[i]`, `[u]`, `[s]`, `[strong]`, `[em]`, `[p]`, `[br]`, `[nowrap]`). |
| MarkDown | `parse_markdown()`. |
| Textile | `parse_textile()`. |

## Storage

- Text: `phpwcms_articlecontent.acontent_text` (`mediumtext`), stored as typed
- Template: `acontent_template`
- Selected format: serialized `ctext_format` in `acontent_form`

## Related

- Rich text alternatives: [Text w/image (cp 1)](01-text-with-image.md), [WYSIWYG HTML (cp 14)](03-wysiwyg-html.md), [HTML (cp 6)](02-html.md)
- Formatted code output: [Code (cp 11)](04-code.md)

<!-- docs/content-parts/01-text-with-image.md -->

# Text w/image (content part 1)

> Source: `include/inc_lib/content/cnt1.readform.inc.php`, `include/inc_front/content/cnt1.article.inc.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/content/cnt1.inc.php`

The basic building block for editorial pages: a WYSIWYG text plus one image, arranged in one of ten predefined positions. With no image selected it renders as plain rich text.

## Backend form

Fields as they appear in the content part dialog, top to bottom.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| Template | select | *(empty = default)* | Content part template from `template/inc_cntpart/imagetext/`. Empty uses the shipped default. |
| Text | WYSIWYG / HTML | — | Main content. Edits with the configured rich text editor or source mode, per user preference. |
| Image | file select + delete | none | Image from the file center via image browser. Stored as file ID. |
| Position | icon group | 0 | One of 0–9: 0 top left, 1 top center, 2 top right, 3 bottom left, 4 bottom center, 5 bottom right, 6 float left, 7 float right, 8 column left, 9 column right. |
| Max width | number | *`image_default_width`* or content width | Image width in px. Capped at `content_width` (positions 6/7: `content_width / 1.75`) when `RESPONSIVE_MODE` is off. |
| Max height | number | *`image_default_height`* | Image height in px. Both 0 = proportional fit. |
| Crop | switch | off | Crop the image to the given size instead of proportional scaling. |
| Zoom | switch | off | Wrap image in a link to the original; requires an enabled lightbox on the page. |
| Lightbox | switch | off | Force the slimbox/lightbox JS; implies Zoom. |
| No caption | switch | off | Suppress caption output in rendering. |
| Caption title | textarea | — | First caption paragraph. |
| Description (alt) | textarea | — | Used as `alt` attribute and second caption line. |
| Link | text | — | URL wrapped around the caption. |
| Target | select | *(blank)* | `_blank`, `_top`, `_self`, `_parent` for the caption link. |

## Rendering

### Template selection

Renderer order: selected file from `template/inc_cntpart/imagetext/<name>.tmpl`, else `template/inc_default/imagetext.tmpl`, else this built-in skeleton:

```html
<div class="image-with-text">{IMAGETEXT}</div>
```

### Template tags

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | ------- |
| `[IMAGETEXT]…[/IMAGETEXT]` | Block holding the combined image + text; removed when the part is not rendered as image+text column pair. |
| `{IMAGETEXT}` | The combined output (or plain text without an image). |
| `{ATTR_CLASS}` / `[ATTR_CLASS]…[/ATTR_CLASS]` | Content part wrapper class (`acontent_attr_class`), `[ATTR_CLASS_ELSE]` fallback branch. |
| `{ATTR_ID}` / `[ATTR_ID]…[/ATTR_ID]` | Wrapper `id`. |
| `{TITLE}` / `{SUBTITLE}` | Content part title / subtitle, HTML-escaped. |
| `[TOP_LEFT]` `[TOP_CENTER]` `[TOP_RIGHT]` `[BOTTOM_LEFT]` `[BOTTOM_CENTER]` `[BOTTOM_RIGHT]` `[FLOAT_LEFT]` `[FLOAT_RIGHT]` `[COLUMN_LEFT]` `[COLUMN_RIGHT]` | Conditional blocks; the active position block stays, all others are stripped. |
| `[ZOOM]` | Present when zoom is active. |
| `{IMAGE}` | Full `<img>` tag pointing to `/img/resize.php`-style URL: `/img/<width>x<height>x<crop>/<hash>.<ext>/<name>`, `alt`, optional `title`, lazy loading attribute included. |
| `{IMAGE_ID}` `{IMAGE_HASH}` `{IMAGE_NAME}` `{IMAGE_EXT}` | Raw image properties. Without an image: `empty-image-<cp id>`, empty hash, name `empty`, empty ext. |
| `{IMAGE_WIDTH}` `{IMAGE_HEIGHT}` | Effective pixel size. |
| `[CAPTION]` `[ALT]` `[IMAGE_TITLE]` `[COPYRIGHT]` | Caption parts; stripped when "No caption" is set. |
| `{CLASS}` | CSS class assigned to the rendered position (see settings). |
| `{ID}` | Content part record ID. |
| `{TEXT}` | The raw text field. |

### Position classes

Each position prints a class that you define per template via the `IMAGETEXT_SETTINGS` section (INI style). Defaults map to `template_default['classes']…`:

```ini
[IMAGETEXT_SETTINGS]
class_top_left     = imgtxt-top-left
class_top_center   = imgtxt-top-center
class_top_right    = imgtxt-top-right
class_bottom_left  = imgtxt-bottom-left
class_bottom_center= imgtxt-bottom-center
class_bottom_right = imgtxt-bottom-right
class_float_left   = imgtxt-left
class_float_right  = imgtxt-right
class_column_left   = imgtxt-column-left
class_column_right  = imgtxt-column-right
class_column_left_image  = imgtxt-column-left-image
class_column_left_text   = imgtxt-column-left-text
class_column_right_image = imgtxt-column-right-image
class_column_right_text  = imgtxt-column-right-text
width     = 0
height    = 0
zoom      = 0
lightbox  = 0
nocaption = 0
crop      = 0
```

Settings values win over per-part backend entries (`width`/`height` from settings replace the stored ones; `lightbox` implies `zoom`; `nocaption` and `crop` act as backend overrides). Column positions (8/9) emit a wrapper `div` containing `imagediv()` output plus `<div class="<class_column_left_text>">{text}</div>`, skipping the whole block when both rendered empty.

> **Note:** Positions 6/7 float: the width is additionally capped at `content_width / 1.75` when `RESPONSIVE_MODE` is off.

## Storage

- Text: `phpwcms_articlecontent.acontent_text`
- Template: `acontent_template`
- Caption parts joined as `title|alt|url| target`, base64 in `acontent_image` field segment 6
- Image string in `acontent_image`: `id:name:hash:ext:width:height:caption(b64):position:zoom`
- Lightbox / nocaption / crop flags: serialized in `acontent_form`

## Related

- Images-only variants: [Images (cp 2)](09-images.md), [Images &lt;div&gt; (cp 29)](10-images-div.md), [Images special (cp 31)](11-images-special.md)
- Image caption model: file system table `phpwcms_file`

# HTML (content part 6)

> Source: `include/inc_lib/content/cnt6.readform.inc.php`, `include/inc_lib/content/cnt6.sql.inc.php`, `include/inc_tmpl/content/cnt6.inc.php`, `include/inc_front/content/cnt6.article.inc.php`

A pass-through block for your own HTML. You edit the markup in a source editor; the frontend outputs it unchanged — no formatting, no sanitizing, no rich text helper.

## Backend form

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| Template | select | *(empty = default)* | Content part template from `template/inc_cntpart/html/`. Empty uses the shipped default. |
| Plain html | textarea, 20 rows | — | The HTML source. Edits in the Ace code editor in HTML mode. |

Trailing `<br>`, `<br />` and empty `<p></p>` editor artifacts are stripped from the end of the input; the remainder is stored as typed.

## Rendering

### Template selection

Renderer order: selected file from `template/inc_cntpart/html/<name>.tmpl`, else `template/inc_default/html.tmpl`, else this built-in skeleton:

```html
[TITLE]<h3>{TITLE}</h3>[/TITLE]
[SUBTITLE]<h4>{SUBTITLE}</h4>[/SUBTITLE]
[HTML]{HTML}[/HTML]
```

### Template tags

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | ------- |
| `[ATTR_CLASS]…[/ATTR_CLASS]` | Present when the wrapper class field is set; `{ATTR_CLASS}` prints its value. `[ATTR_CLASS_ELSE]` marks the branch without class. |
| `[ATTR_ID]…[/ATTR_ID]` | Same mechanism for the wrapper `id` (`{ATTR_ID}`). |
| `{TITLE}` / `{SUBTITLE}` | Content part title / subtitle, HTML-escaped. |
| `[HTML]…[/HTML]` / `{HTML}` | The stored markup, output as is. Removed when empty. |
| `{ID}` | Content part record ID. |

## Storage

- Markup: `phpwcms_articlecontent.acontent_html` (`mediumtext`)
- Template: `acontent_template`

## Related

- Editor-assisted variant of the same field: [WYSIWYG HTML (cp 14)](03-wysiwyg-html.md)
- Text without markup: [Plain text (cp 0)](00-plaintext.md)
- Code displayed as code, not rendered: [Code (cp 11)](04-code.md)
