# Addresses

> Source: `include/inc_module/mod_addresses/`

The addresses module manages address and contact records in the backend and renders them on the frontend through a filterable address locator. Module registration (`module.default.php`): `$_module_name = 'phpwcms_addresses'`, `$_module_type = 1` (backend only), no content part, frontend render hook.

## Storage

> Source: `backend.default.php`

Records live in the shared contact-detail table `phpwcms_userdetail`, scoped by `detail_regkey = 'PHPWCMS-ADDRESS'` (module constant `MODULE_KEY`). Deletion is a soft delete (`detail_aktiv = 9`); verify toggles the same flag. The table holds generic `detail_*` columns (`detail_text1–3`, `detail_varchar1–4`, `detail_float1–2`, `detail_int1–2`), which the module maps to its fields.

## Backend

Available to usergroups with the addresses module enabled. URL: `phpwcms.php?do=modules&module=phpwcms_addresses`. The routing (GET parameters `edit`, `verify`, `delete`, else listing) lives in `backend.default.php`.

### Entry form

> Source: `backend.editform.php`, `inc/processing.inc.php`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| Representation office | checkbox | off | Marks the entry as a representative office (`detail_varchar2`, CHECK) |
| Company | text | – | Company OR last name is mandatory |
| Location | text | – | Stored in `detail_varchar4` |
| Title / First name / Last name | text | – | Person fields |
| Street / Addition / City / Zip / Region | text | – | Postal address fields |
| Country | select | DE | Country list from `getCountry()` |
| Also for | multi-checkbox | – | Additional countries the entry appears under (stored as text) |
| Fon / Fax / Mobile / Website / Email | text | – | Contact fields; email format is validated |
| Language | select | – | `DE`, `EN` |
| Files | file list | – | Attached files with descriptions, stored as JSON in `detail_text3` |
| Annotation | textarea | – | Free text (`detail_text1`) |
| Zip-code area | text | – | Locator grouping value (`detail_varchar3`) |
| Latitude / Longitude | number | – | Geocoordinates (`detail_float1`, `detail_float2`) |
| Sort | number | 0 | Ordering (`detail_int2`) |
| Public | checkbox | off | Only public entries appear in the frontend locator |
| Active | checkbox | on | Record state |

When lat/long are empty, the edit form can fill them by geocoding the postal address against the Nominatim service; a Google Maps link to the coordinates is shown alongside (`backend.editform.php`). There is no CSV import or export, and no coupling to the frontend login (`template/inc_script/felogin/` does not read address records).

### Listing

`backend.listing.php` shows company and name, city, country and status, ordered by company, city, country. Actions: edit, verify, delete.

## Frontend

> Source: `frontend.render.php`, `inc/search.addresses.php`

The render hook replaces `{PHPWCMS-ADDRESS-LOCATOR}` with the locator. It queries public, active records with the `PHPWCMS-ADDRESS` regkey, left joins `phpwcms_country` on the country code, and sorts by sort value, zip and company.

The locator UI is generated by `inc/search.addresses.php` — it is not template driven. It exposes filters for continent, country, city, free text and zip (`continent_filter`, `country_filter`, `city_filter`, `filter`, `filter_zip` GET/POST parameters) and renders Bootstrap based cards; contact persons and attached files (rendered through the file list renderer of content part 7, `include/inc_front/content/cnt7.article.inc.php`) collapse inside each card. Map images ship in `include/inc_module/mod_addresses/template/` together with `js/GoogleMaps.js`; `frontend.init.php` stays empty.

## Configuration

The module registers no configuration keys. Backend access follows the module group in the usergroup editor — see [Modules overview](index.md).

## Related

- [Modules overview](index.md) — architecture and activation
- [Newsletter (core)](06-newsletter.md) — subscriber addresses use the separate `phpwcms_address` table, not this module

<!-- docs/modules/10-seolog.md -->

# SEO Log

> Source: `include/inc_module/mod_seolog/`

The SEO log module lists search engine referrer data collected by the core: which search engine domain referred visitors, with which query, and at which result position. Module registration (`module.default.php`): `$_module_name = 'seo_log'`, `$_module_type = 1` — backend only, no content part, no frontend hooks.

## Data collection

Logging is core behavior, not the module's:

- `index.php` calls `seReferrer()` when `$phpwcms['enable_seolog']` is set and the `HTTP_REFERER` of the request does not contain the site's own `SERVER_NAME`. The insert into `phpwcms_log_seo` runs with `LOW_PRIORITY`, storing the parsed referrer plus `hash = md5(strtolower(domain . query))`.
- `seReferrer()` (`include/inc_front/ext.func.inc.php`) extracts the search terms from the typical query parameter names (`q`, `p`, `w`, `s`, `qry`, `searchfor`, `as_q`, `as_epq`, `query`, `qt`, `keyword`, `keywords`, `encquery`) and from DogPile's `/search/web/...` path style. It resolves the result position from `start`, `b`, `first`, `stq` style parameters and decodes + converts the charset of the terms. When the referrer carries no recognizable query, nothing is stored — the log holds only search engine traffic, no general referrers.

The `hash` column was added by revision r497 (`include/inc_lib/revision/r497.php`) together with a backfill of existing rows.

## Storage

> Source: `setup/default_sql/phpwcms_init.sql` line 599

| Column | Type | Contents |
| ------ | ---- | -------- |
| `id` | int | Row id |
| `create_date` | timestamp | Insert time, defaults to `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` |
| `domain` | varchar(255) | Referrer host, e.g. the search engine |
| `query` | varchar(255) | Search terms |
| `pos` | int | Position of the linked hit in the result list |
| `referrer` | text | Full referrer string |
| `hash` | char(32) | `md5` of lowercased domain + query, indexed |

## Backend

Available to usergroups with the SEO log module enabled. The page is a single listing, no tabs (`backend.default.php` only defines the module URL and includes `backend.listing.php`).

- URL: `phpwcms.php?do=modules&module=seo_log`
- GET parameters: `page` (pagination), `c` (rows per page: 10, 25, 50, 100, 250 or `all`, default 25).
- Filter: a POST form stores whitespace separated terms in `$_SESSION['filter_seo']`.
- Listing groups by `hash` and orders by hit count descending, so each row aggregates repeated hits for one domain/query combination. Columns: Count, Domain (linked to the referrer URL), Query.

There is no pruning or cleanup routine — the table grows until truncated manually.

## Configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `$phpwcms['enable_seolog']` | int | 1 | Enables referrer logging in `index.php` (`include/config/dist.conf.inc.php` line 112) |

The Statistics module offers an alternative view of the same table — see [Statistics](11-statistic.md).

## Related

- [Modules overview](index.md) — architecture and activation
- [Statistics](11-statistic.md) — per-row SEO listing and top queries

---

<!-- docs/modules/11-statistic.md -->

# Statistics

> Source: `include/inc_module/mod_statistic/`

The statistics module is a read-only reporting layer over data the core and other modules already store. It records nothing itself. Module registration (`module.default.php`): `$_module_name = 'statistics'`, `$_module_type = 1` — backend only, no content part, no frontend hooks. There is no `phpwcms_statistic` table.

## Backend

Available to usergroups with the statistics module enabled. URL: `phpwcms.php?do=modules&module=statistics`.

The active page is selected with the `controller` GET parameter (`backend.default.php`). Tabs are rendered by `inc/tabs.inc.php` and appear only when the underlying data exists:

| Controller | Shows | Availability |
| ---------- | ----- | ------------ |
| (default/overview) | Article status counts (active, start/end not reached, missing alias, missing description), file center image counts, content part usage counts per type, expired articles | Always |
| `downloads` | Files from the file center with download traffic — rows from `phpwcms_file` where `f_dlstart > 0` and `f_trash = 0`, sortable by name, download start, final count, created date; searchable and paginated (`page`, `c`) | When downloaded files exist |
| `subscriptions` | Newsletter subscription lists with recipient counts, verified vs unverified address counts, last 200 entries of `phpwcms_log` for log types 1–4 joined to addresses; per-row delete via `delete`; blacklist an email via `blacklist=<email>` (removes matching log rows and the unverified address, inserts into the blacklist) | When `phpwcms_address` rows exist |
| `guestbook` | Content part type 18 instances with their entry counts from `phpwcms_guestbook` | When guestbook content parts exist |
| `polls` | Content part type 89 instances with summed votes (unserialized `acontent_form` count) | When poll content parts exist |
| `user` | Last 100 backend login log rows from `phpwcms_userlog` | Admin users only (`$_SESSION['wcs_user_admin']`) |
| `seo` | `phpwcms_log_seo` rows per hit (date, domain, position, query) plus a top 20 query frequency list, own session filter `$_SESSION['seo_filter']` | Always — same data as [SEO log](10-seolog.md) |

Listings use POST `list_search` for search terms and GET `page`/`c` for pagination.

## Data sources

The module writes no data. The tables it reads are fed elsewhere:

- `phpwcms_userlog` is written on backend login (`login.php`) and refreshed during the session by `include/inc_lib/checklogin.inc.php`.
- `phpwcms_file` download columns (`f_dlstart`, `f_dlfinal`) are updated by the download handler.
- `phpwcms_log_seo` is filled by the core referrer logging described on the [SEO log](10-seolog.md) page.
- `phpwcms_address`, `phpwcms_subscription` and `phpwcms_log` belong to the [Newsletter (core)](06-newsletter.md) and its address storage.

## Configuration

The module registers no configuration keys. Backend access follows the module group in the usergroup editor — see [Modules overview](index.md).

## Related

- [Modules overview](index.md) — architecture and activation
- [SEO log](10-seolog.md) — the module dedicated to the `phpwcms_log_seo` listing
- [Newsletter (core)](06-newsletter.md) — subscriptions and address data

# phpwcms modules

> Source: `include/inc_module/mod_modules/`

This entry presents available phpwcms modules. It is purely informational — no install, uninstall or configuration actions, no database access. Module registration (`module.default.php`): `$_module_name = 'modulpromo'`, `$_module_type = 1` — backend only, no content part, no frontend hooks.

## Backend

Available to usergroups with the module enabled. Backend URLs use the registered internal name, not the directory name: `phpwcms.php?do=modules&module=modulpromo`.

`backend.listing.php` renders one intro line and three static cards. Card headers and texts come from `include/inc_module/mod_modules/lang/en.lang.php`; no card contains a link:

- "phpwcms shop module" — "…enables you to set up a simple online store." Covered by [Shop](01-shop.md) and its sub-pages.
- "phpwcms calendar module" — "…enables you to build a feature-rich calendar." Covered by [Calendar](05-calendar.md).
- "phpwcms user management module" — "…allows managing user data such as customers or association members."

Installed modules are not listed here; the panel promotes capabilities. Actual module availability and access live in discovery and the module groups — see [Modules overview](index.md).

## Configuration

None. The panel has no settings and no own tables.

## Related

- [Modules overview](index.md) — module architecture and per-module reference pages

<!-- docs/modules/13-glossary.md -->

# Glossary

> Source: `include/inc_module/mod_glossary/`

The glossary module holds term definitions and automatically highlights keywords in frontend pages as `<abbr>` tooltips. Module type: backend **and** frontend with its own content part and frontend search registration (`module.default.php`: `$_module_type = 0`, `$_module_contentpart = true`, `$_module_fe_render = true`, `$_module_fe_search = true`).

## Backend

Available to usergroups with the glossary module enabled. Entry fields: title, keyword list (comma separated), description text, status, and a *highlight* flag — only entries with `glossary_status = 1` **and** `glossary_highlight = 1` participate in frontend replacement. Storage: `phpwcms_glossary`.

## Content part

Selecting "Plug-in" content part type (30) with module *glossary* renders a keyword list on the article page (alphabet navigation, definition list rendering — `include/inc_module/mod_glossary/inc/cnt.*.php`).

## Frontend highlighting

The registered frontend render script wraps matching text with an abbreviation tooltip:

```text
[glossary CMS ]content management system[/glossary]
```

renders as

```html
<abbr class="glossary" title="CMS :: content management system">content management system</abbr>
```

- Keyword matching is exact per comma-separated keyword of an entry (`LIKE` variants cover head, middle and tail positions).
- Best matching entry wins (highest entry count); all matching keywords of that entry go into a per-request cache, so repeated keywords resolve once.
- Styling hook: class `glossary` on the `abbr` element. A jQuery sample ships in `include/inc_module/mod_glossary/template/` (`sample.jquery.tmpl`, `jquery.glossary.js`).

## Frontend search

Glossary text participates in the frontend search (registered via `$_module_fe_search`).

## Activation

Ships disabled for no one — module presence is auto-discovered (`include/inc_lib/modules.check.inc.php`); backend visibility and content part availability are controlled per usergroup. See [Users and usergroups](../administration/users-usergroups.md) and the [modules overview](index.md).
